sbcd79b1222.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
sbcd79b1222.description: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six
sbcd79b1222.summary: Researchers introduced NEBench R1, a reasoning benchmark with 7,546 multiple-choice nuclear engineering questions drawn from NRC reactor operator licensing exams.
sbcd79b1222.why: Gives teams building LLMs for safety-critical nuclear applications a reasoning-focused evaluation, not just answer accuracy.

s7a9e51a5ea.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
s7a9e51a5ea.description: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT
s7a9e51a5ea.summary: A study finds that training models to control their chain-of-thought reasoning can make that reasoning less monitorable for detecting hidden goals or failures.
s7a9e51a5ea.why: Suggests CoT monitoring, a key agent oversight tool, may be weakened if models learn to shape their reasoning.

s9c46afe5a3.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
s9c46afe5a3.description: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). The same shortcut is present in ATRNet-STAR, which was collected across several scenes: with the vehicle removed, accuracy is 63.3% on the 40-class SOC split (chance 2.5%). Under the official scene-change split, the background stops helping and starts hurting. Accuracy is 22.8% on full chips and 30.8% when only the vehicle is shown. A SAR foundation model, SARATR-X, leans on the background more
s9c46afe5a3.summary: Researchers show SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR can be solved well above chance using background shortcuts with the vehicle masked out.
s9c46afe5a3.why: Shows benchmark scores can overstate true recognition, a caution for evaluating vision models on shortcut-prone datasets.

sb5c3132bda.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
sb5c3132bda.description: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. Given access to the full research transcript and the ability to run experiments, human auditors mostly fail to distinguish sabotaged from benign research: they achieve an AUROC of 0.59, not significantly better than chance, and fully identify the specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Despite not being allowed to run experiments, the
sb5c3132bda.summary: A red-team study finds human auditors mostly fail to detect sabotage planted in end-to-end transcripts of AI safety research experiments.
sb5c3132bda.why: Indicates human review alone may not reliably catch sabotage in AI-automated R&D pipelines, pointing to need for stronger defenses.

s9fe3e937f5.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
s9fe3e937f5.description: arXiv:2611.21885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it signif
s9fe3e937f5.summary: Researchers report a 27B language model can diagnose its own failures and edit its weights through reasoning alone, without gradients or training.
s9fe3e937f5.why: Suggests a new self-improvement route that avoids retraining, though the abstract gives limited detail on robustness or scope.

s7195ca0e67.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
s7195ca0e67.description: arXiv:2611.21925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative-diffusion decoding uses a small parallel drafter model to generate b draft tokens in one forward pass, which then undergo parallel verification via a larger target model. Faster inference can be achieved when multiple draft tokens pass verification simultaneously. Recent parallel draft architectures (DFlash, DSpark) improve draft quality by conditioning on rich features computed by the target, through a mechanism known as feature encoding. However, standard feature encoding mechanisms have three limitations: (1) they are lossy, applying encoding projections that are destructive to the underlying target feature-space via a discovered effect known as residual mixing, (2) they are memory-less, with no record of previously processed p
s7195ca0e67.summary: DNeo proposes improved target feature encoding for parallel draft models used in speculative-diffusion decoding to speed up LLM inference.
s7195ca0e67.why: Targets inference speedups via better drafter conditioning, relevant to teams optimizing LLM serving latency.

scdb8ae8b75.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
scdb8ae8b75.description: arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open ra
scdb8ae8b75.summary: SLED proposes allocating network and compute resources per sensor stream, rather than per device, across edge-to-datacenter wireless systems.

se1fbba8ab1.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
se1fbba8ab1.description: arXiv:2611.21946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change
se1fbba8ab1.summary: Researchers propose distinguishing a reasoning model's commitment from its verdict to decide when continued thinking harms a correct answer.
se1fbba8ab1.why: Shows final-correctness probes alone cannot decide when a reasoning model should stop, which matters for designing early-stopping in inference pipelines.

s6cb2ad0128.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators
s6cb2ad0128.description: arXiv:2611.21948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The regulation of Artificial Intelligence is susceptible to various forms of capture by industry actors that hold undue influence over the policymaking process, due in part to their information advantage in developing these technologies. In the following paper, we investigate the roles of public commenters in providing evidence to potential regulation in the USA. We build a corpus of 40 potential regulations, and 2,664 public comments submitted by a variety of stakeholders. We computationally process these texts to extract evidence meant to inform regulators, in the form of formal citations and informal references. We find significant differences in the type and amount of evidence supplied: Holding comment length constant, business commenters
s6cb2ad0128.summary: A paper examines how public comments on proposed AI regulations introduce evidence to US regulators, using a corpus of 40 regulations and 2,664 comments.
s6cb2ad0128.why: Highlights how stakeholder comments shape AI policy and how industry information advantages can influence rulemaking.

sddcb912129.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
sddcb912129.description: arXiv:2611.21950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 Protei
sddcb912129.summary: DiscoveryAgent is a scientist-centric agentic AI framework that lets researchers select, refine, or replace hypotheses between autonomous research rounds.
sddcb912129.why: Offers a design pattern for keeping humans in control of autonomous agents, with checkpointed records for auditing claims.

s9c24b96ea7.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
s9c24b96ea7.description: arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and bud
s9c24b96ea7.summary: WebAgents proposes separating agent creation, hosting, and execution, using a signed agent.pkg format to make agents portable across runtimes.
s9c24b96ea7.why: Outlines an architecture for moving agents across hosts without tying publication to one execution environment or transferring user authority.

s209de93253.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants
s209de93253.description: arXiv:2611.21998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal assistants accumulate months of conversations, but today's long-term memory stacks put derivation or selection between a question and its evidence. In a system-level comparison on LongMemEval, two commercial assistants scored well below the same model reading the history offline [1], consistent with, but not isolating, content loss between write and read. We propose KV-LTM: a memory tier storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering by restoring cached sessions and appending the question. KV-LTM is complementary to, not a replacement for, retrieval and indexing. Text is the memory of record; the cache is a recompute-free prefill accelerator, degrading gracefully to text. We specify the design
s209de93253.summary: KV-LTM stores each session's raw text plus its KV cache as long-term memory for personal assistants, restoring cached sessions to answer questions.
s209de93253.why: Suggests a memory design that may avoid content loss from derivation or selection in conventional long-term memory stacks.

s3843f46054.title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
s3843f46054.description: arXiv:2611.22010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change
s3843f46054.summary: A paper links closest-world counterfactual explanations to formal XAI methods, characterizing them as a disjunctive normal form over minimally distant counterexamples.
s3843f46054.why: Connects counterfactual explanations with feature-based abductive and contrastive explanations, which may help in building efficient explainability tooling.

s14a1f345f6.title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
s14a1f345f6.description: arXiv:2611.22017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multip
s14a1f345f6.summary: SkillBuffBench is a benchmark that measures how agent skills contribute across harnesses, models, skill access modes, and memory in realistic deployment settings.
s14a1f345f6.why: Challenges claims about agent skill value by testing realistic conditions where agents choose from installed libraries and carry memory.

s164ad1122d.title: What Does an Agent Need? Bundle-Aware Agent Resource Composition
s164ad1122d.description: arXiv:2611.22030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent resource's value depends on its backbone and companion resources and is known only after execution. Token-based generators remain tied to their training catalog, while independent resource scoring misses complementarities and reused bundles target other tasks. We formulate Task-Conditioned Agent Resource Composition (AgentComposition): jointly selecting a backbone model and a tool-skill bundle to maximize end-to-end execution utility. Our Retrieval-Grounded Bundle-Aware Agent Generation retrieves candidate resources and past configurations of similar tasks. A fine-tuned generator reads resource descriptions and recombines candidates through constrained beam search, allowing new resources without retraining. A bundle-aware critic rank
s164ad1122d.summary: Researchers formulate AgentComposition, jointly selecting a backbone model and tool-skill bundle for a task, using retrieval-grounded bundle-aware generation.
s164ad1122d.why: Suggests that agent configuration should consider model and tool combinations together rather than scoring resources independently.

s3818a96d04.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
s3818a96d04.description: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisi
s3818a96d04.summary: A benchmark of ten frontier LLMs finds that more reasoning effort raises shopping agents' confidence but not the correctness of their product choices.
s3818a96d04.why: Warns that higher reasoning budgets and reported confidence do not guarantee better autonomous purchasing decisions.

s38e1c821de.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem
s38e1c821de.description: arXiv:2611.22043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood s
s38e1c821de.summary: A team describes its contest solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, combining heuristics, ALNS, and an exact route-selection engine.
s38e1c821de.why: Offers a practical example of hybrid exact-heuristic optimization for routing, though its relevance beyond the contest is limited.

saca8585783.title: MedGuardBench: A Patient-Oriented Benchmark for Personalized Guardrail Development
saca8585783.description: arXiv:2611.22069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety is personal: the same action can be safe for one person but unsafe for another. Yet current guardrails judge content without considering who is affected. Using medication safety, we introduce \textit{patient-conditioned medication guarding}, which predicts a safety verdict and 17 risk categories from a patient profile and prescription. We release \textbf{MedGuardBench}, a drug-disjoint benchmark of 5{,}001 scenarios across 87 medications. We find that standard guardrails rely on surface cues, such as wording and profile presence, rather than patient facts. To address this, we develop \textit{personalized reasoning guardrails} with three components. \textbf{Personalized Reasoning Distillation} links risks to relevant patient fields. \te
saca8585783.summary: MedGuardBench introduces a patient-conditioned medication safety benchmark with 5,001 scenarios across 87 medications, finding standard guardrails rely on surface cues.
saca8585783.why: Shows generic guardrails miss patient-specific risk, which matters for teams deploying safety filters in healthcare settings.

sffe81ed8f2.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
sffe81ed8f2.description: arXiv:2611.22075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates
sffe81ed8f2.summary: Reversibility Classes proposes a five-level vocabulary for whether AI agent tool actions can be undone, covering 536 tools across 20 MCP servers.
sffe81ed8f2.why: Gives engineers a way to gate agent actions by reversibility, since tool permission alone does not show whether a mistake can be undone.

sd3649c9361.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections
sd3649c9361.description: arXiv:2611.22084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An expert who corrects a concept prediction, such as a BI-RADS descriptor in breast ultrasound, expects the diagnosis to improve. Objectives that reduce the harm of such corrections are judged by harm and accuracy, yet harm also falls when a model responds less to every correction or starts from a worse uncorrected prediction, the reference for harm. We propose a correction audit, a reproducible evaluation protocol that separates these explanations: it splits each correction into harm and useful gain on identical events, separates the starting prediction from the correction response, and compares objectives with amplitude baselines matched in source harm. On three breast-ultrasound sources, worst-case correction training, evaluated from the m
sd3649c9361.summary: A correction audit protocol separates reductions in harm from concept corrections into explanations based on model responsiveness and starting-point accuracy.
sd3649c9361.why: Warns that lower correction harm can reflect a weaker model or worse baseline rather than real improvement, affecting how teams evaluate expert-in-the-loop systems.

sa9f6d39d69.title: ATLAS-Finance: Benchmarking AI Agents in Realistic Banking Environments
sa9f6d39d69.description: arXiv:2611.22085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional work involves under-specified assignments, where relevant information is spread across workplace applications and may conflict or change over time. To evaluate how well frontier agents can perform economically valuable work in such settings, we introduce ATLAS-Finance, a benchmark of 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms. As in real banking workflows, agents must search email, chat, calendars, notes, and files to identify requirements, gather information, reconcile conflicts/updates, and then build complex financial models. Tasks were developed by experienced bankers based on their real deal work and take them 15-30 hours to complete. Agent deliverables are evaluated with expert-authored rubrics (media
sa9f6d39d69.summary: ATLAS-Finance benchmarks AI agents on 100 end-to-end investment-banking tasks across 13 simulated firms that require searching email, chat, and files.
sa9f6d39d69.why: Provides a realistic enterprise benchmark for agent work involving conflicting and changing information across workplace tools.

s9abe45a7a6.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
s9abe45a7a6.description: arXiv:2611.22102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents accumulate experience in memory, and how that memory evolves during interaction is as important as what it stores. Recent methods update memory online, yet both the operators that transform memory and the rules that select them remain fixed by design. We propose EvoDisco, which formulates agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery: the agent must discover which operator to apply, when to apply it, and how to instantiate it, rather than rewriting memory under a static operator schedule. A learnable policy conditions on the current memory state and recent task history, then selects and instantiates one of four semantic operators---Abstract, Refine, Bridge, and Reframe---which respectively compress rela
s9abe45a7a6.summary: EvoDisco frames agent memory evolution as strategy discovery, with a learnable policy choosing which memory operator to apply, when, and how.
s9abe45a7a6.why: Proposes learning memory-update policies instead of fixed schedules, which may affect how long-running agents manage accumulated experience.

s97d0bd5979.title: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
s97d0bd5979.description: arXiv:2611.22103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can now generate Lean proof scripts that capture the high-level structure of many mathematical arguments. However, these scripts frequently fail on complex theorems: a single missing side condition or misapplied lemma can cause the prover to abort early and discard an otherwise viable proof outline. This paper presents MathEye, a framework that converts imperfect LLM-generated proof scripts into fully verified Lean proofs by combining symbolic reasoning with minimal human interaction. At the core of MathEye is angelic proof checking, an optimistic execution model that replaces failing proof fragments with placeholders while preserving the overall structure of the argument. This optimistic check produces an angelic
s97d0bd5979.summary: MathEye is a framework that turns imperfect LLM-generated Lean proof scripts into fully verified proofs using symbolic reasoning and minimal human input.
s97d0bd5979.why: Shows a route to salvaging failed LLM proof drafts in formal verification, reducing the cost of getting machine-checked proofs.

s0e9137d72d.title: RegimeCouncil: Paired-Evidence Routing For Memory Conflict Governance In LLM Agents
s0e9137d72d.description: arXiv:2611.22113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language agents rely on long-term memory to personalize responses across extended interactions, yet stored facts quietly go stale as the world changes, and an agent often learns that using memory hurt only through delayed feedback after acting on an outdated record. Before the memory store is updated, how far should that negative feedback propagate: should it suppress memory use only on future queries for that same fact (a local policy), or also across other stored facts (a global policy)? Existing memory systems implicitly fix one of these two sharing scopes at design time. We formulate this online scope choice under hidden validity and delayed feedback as memory conflict governance, and prove that neither fixed policy is sufficient on its o
s0e9137d72d.summary: RegimeCouncil proposes paired-evidence routing to govern memory conflicts in LLM agents, deciding whether negative feedback on stale facts should apply locally or globally.
s0e9137d72d.why: Addresses how agents with long-term memory should handle outdated stored facts, a practical reliability problem for deployed agents.

s4920d00e28.title: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
s4920d00e28.description: arXiv:2611.22115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. This report describes the design principles and systems engineering behind the series, spanning architecture selection, large-scale pretraining, and reasoning and agentic post-training. We study how sparse activation, attention design, model depth and width, and speculative decoding balance model capacity with computation, memory access, and execution overhead. Our pretraining infrastructure builds on MindSpore HyperParallel, combining topology-aware hybrid sharding, efficient distributed optimizer execution, and coordinated management of long-sequence workloads and ac
s4920d00e28.summary: TeleChat's team released Xing 4, a series of LLMs built on Ascend chips, covering architecture, pretraining, and agentic post-training.
s4920d00e28.why: Documents training and inference engineering for frontier-scale agentic models on domestic Chinese hardware and frameworks.

se4a01defea.title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model
se4a01defea.description: arXiv:2611.22131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whole image embeddings can under represent small objects and local attributes that distinguish relevant images for localized queries. We present LoCaR, a training free framework for localized text to image retrieval with frozen vision language models. LoCaR constructs and utilizes independent proposals (SAM2) focusing on the object so as to get a more localized representation that independently encodes each region using the frozen visual encoder. We further study paired-support adaptation as an optional residual that uses matched text region exemplars without updating the underlying encoders. We also introduce LOCFG, a Visual Genome derived benchmark designed to evaluate localized retrieval for smaller and more challenging referents. Across s
se4a01defea.summary: LoCaR is a training-free method for localized text-to-image retrieval that encodes SAM2-proposed regions with a frozen vision-language model.
se4a01defea.why: Offers a no-training way to improve retrieval of small objects and local attributes, useful for search over image collections.

sad984d9790.title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions
sad984d9790.description: arXiv:2611.22136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many biology experiments are limited by the availability and ease of use of instruments that monitor and record them. For example, the timing of pupariation in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster, a widely used model organism, can provide biologically relevant information about growth regulation and is often recorded manually. Here, we present Pupavision, a small physical AI instrument built from a single-board Linux computer and a day/night camera for roughly 45 to 75 US dollars in parts. The key idea is that a frontier coding agent runs its agentic harness directly on the tiny board. The model thinks in the cloud, but the agent works on the device. The agent assists image capture, writes code to repair errors, and checks the experiment ev
sad984d9790.summary: Pupavision is a low-cost physical AI instrument, built from a single-board Linux computer and a camera, that monitors Drosophila pupariation with a coding agent.
sad984d9790.why: Illustrates a low-cost pattern of agentic coding systems controlling physical sensing hardware for lab automation.

sc627ed034f.title: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
sc627ed034f.description: arXiv:2611.22148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models are widely observed to get worse the longer they generate. Often, attempts to fix this involve more training. At high temperature, The sampler, i.e. the rule that picks the next token out of the model's probabilities, decides whether long and agentic generation survives and/or thrives. We test 29 open-weight models from 1B to 122B parameters on ten established benchmarks plus needle retrieval out to one million tokens, covering SWE-bench Verified coding agents, long chain-of-thought reasoning, long-form writing, long structured output and long-context reading. Samplers that keep their pool of candidate tokens small and steady as temperature rises don't lose accuracy. Samplers that let in low-probability tokens fall
sc627ed034f.summary: The study tests 29 open-weight models up to 122B parameters and finds long-generation quality depends heavily on the sampler, especially at high temperature.
sc627ed034f.why: Suggests sampler choice, not just more training, may determine whether long agentic generations hold up in production.

scfe4994145.title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
scfe4994145.description: arXiv:2611.22169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Building on this, we recast
scfe4994145.summary: The paper introduces evidence hijacking, where tool outputs in medical agents flip correct answers to wrong, and proposes governing which evidence is kept.
scfe4994145.why: Shows tool outputs can degrade agent accuracy, so engineers need explicit evidence filtering in tool-augmented pipelines.

s36c0da284c.title: Readie: Low-Latency Code Sandboxes for AI Agents
s36c0da284c.description: arXiv:2611.22171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From quantitative research to personal assistance, AI agents act by iteratively generating and executing code. To decouple the agent harness from code execution, many agents offload execution to dedicated systems called code sandboxes. However, existing code sandboxes suffer from slow startup. Whether they rely on custom snapshots or a single fat image, the root cause is the same: it is hard to build a compact, pre-warmed snapshot that can be shared across diverse agent-generated code while covering nearly all the artifacts (e.g., packages, datasets) it requires. In this work, we propose learned startup snapshots for low-latency code sandboxes. Our insight is that while it is hard for a single snapshot to be both compact and cover most worklo
s36c0da284c.summary: Readie presents low-latency code sandboxes for AI agents, using pre-warmed shared snapshots to address slow startup times.
s36c0da284c.why: Startup latency in code execution sandboxes directly affects agent responsiveness and infrastructure design.

s7d1c9600a8.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
s7d1c9600a8.description: arXiv:2611.22174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views
s7d1c9600a8.summary: The paper studies reconfigurability, adapting general-purpose robot behavior models to new goals by restructuring existing skill components under sparse guidance.
s7d1c9600a8.why: Points toward adapting robot skills by recombining learned components rather than training new behaviors from scratch.

sad8a29a08d.title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
sad8a29a08d.description: arXiv:2611.22177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents are tested on news, but news reaches stock prices within minutes, and a benchmark that replays headlines at their publication time finds no alpha in trading on them. Money can then remain in two places, before news whose date is known, such as earnings announcements, and after bad news, if the market's fall went too far. However, studies of LLMs and earnings read documents published with or after the announcement, and studies of reversal sort monthly portfolios, so neither tells whether an agent can trade these moments after costs. In this paper, we test LLM agents at both moments on the same look-ahead-free benchmark, before 598 earnings announcements and after 409 bad-news drops of large US stocks.
sad8a29a08d.summary: The paper examines whether LLM trading agents can profit around earnings and bad news, finding the edge may come from memorized training data.
sad8a29a08d.why: Highlights that backtests of LLM agents may reflect memorization rather than genuine predictive skill, a validation risk for finance applications.

s52879c9aaa.title: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting
s52879c9aaa.description: arXiv:2611.22178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting models suffer from errors in intensity, location, and spatial structure. Addressing these errors by retraining nowcaster backbones can be computationally expensive and requires architecture-specific modifications. To overcome these limitations, we propose CorrectCast, a decoupled residual correction framework that refines completed nowcasts while keeping the base nowcaster frozen. By operating on predicted precipitation fields, CorrectCast requires training only a lightweight corrector, reducing computational overhead while providing a unified correction interface across different nowcasting models. Conditioned on the base nowcast and historical quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) and precipitable water vapor
s52879c9aaa.summary: CorrectCast is a decoupled residual correction framework that refines precipitation nowcasts by training a lightweight corrector while the base model stays frozen.
s52879c9aaa.why: Offers a cheaper way to improve forecasting models without retraining or modifying their architectures.

s290ab70aaa.title: RAG in a Trenchcoat: When Minimal Memory Is Enough for Agentic Systems, and When It Isn't
s290ab70aaa.description: arXiv:2611.22179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic memory research has accumulated extraction, supersession, reflection, and graph synthesis on top of retrieval-augmented generation. However, we found that almost none of those primitives earn their cost in our tested memory benchmarks: we show this with BRIDGE, a deliberately minimal RAG memory with chained observation notes, hybrid BM25 with cosine retrieval, and chronological rendering, which reaches parity within bootstrap CI with the prior SOTA on LongMemEval-S and BEAM, and beats the best memory baseline on EverMemBench by 5.7-6.3 points at matched reader. It runs at ~5-7K reader-prompt tokens per query, using a single LLM call for each ingestion or query. We argue that this parity is itself the result: standard benchmarks score
s290ab70aaa.summary: BRIDGE, a minimal RAG memory design, matches prior state-of-the-art on LongMemEval-S and BEAM and beats the best memory baseline on EverMemBench.
s290ab70aaa.why: Suggests simple retrieval memory may outperform complex agent memory schemes, lowering build cost for agent systems.

s155342dc55.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
s155342dc55.description: arXiv:2611.22219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. The evaluation used 433 sentences from 36 test documents; 1,672 sentences were used for training. LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot prompting with and without JSON Schema constraints and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning. Fine-tuned models were assessed under different output-token limits, including 900 and larger model-specific limits of 2,600 or 4,096 tokens. Performa
s155342dc55.summary: A controlled comparison finds fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines and nine open-weight LLMs evaluated on fine-grained Japanese clinical named entity recognition across 113 categories.
s155342dc55.why: Gives engineers benchmark evidence on whether open LLMs beat encoder models for specialized clinical extraction in Japanese.

s30b91320b9.title: The Fragility of Reasoning-Importance Attribution for Pruning Language Models
s30b91320b9.description: arXiv:2611.22234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribution-guided pruning scores components by their causal contribution and protects the important ones, and it is increasingly applied to compress reasoning language models without destroying their chain of thought. Its reliability rests on an unexamined assumption: that reasoning importance can be faithfully measured. Across four small reasoning models, we show this measurement is fragile in three ways, each of which changes pruning decisions. First, scoring final-answer tokens, the natural choice, saturates in every chain-of-thought model we test (answer-token negative log-likelihood, NLL, of $10^{-4}$--$10^{-3}$) because the model states its answer inside its own reasoning; guiding head pruning with this target costs 27.6 and 32.2 accur
s30b91320b9.summary: The paper shows attribution-guided pruning of reasoning models is fragile, with importance scores for chain-of-thought components changing pruning decisions.
s30b91320b9.why: Warns that pruning reasoning models based on attribution scores may remove important components if the measurement is unreliable.

s1c1b3b4a10.title: Context Has a Price: Adding and Removing Context for LLM Coding Agents under Prefix Caching
s1c1b3b4a10.description: arXiv:2611.22238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents repeatedly send their conversation history to a language model. Adding useful code may reduce search, while removing old tool outputs may shorten later prompts. But do these changes reduce the cost of solving a task? We study this as a measurement problem in more than 20,000 runs of open models on SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench and Loc-Bench. We account separately for uncached input, cached input and output tokens. Three findings emerge. First, in our main evidence-package experiments, retrieved code reduces read and search commands by 18--34%, but increases cost by 33--42% when cached input costs one tenth of uncached input, without a measurable improvement in resolution. Second, removing old observations can either save money o
s1c1b3b4a10.summary: A study of over 20,000 runs on SWE-bench variants measures how adding or removing context affects coding agent costs under prefix caching.
s1c1b3b4a10.why: Gives concrete cost accounting for context management in coding agents, where cached and uncached tokens are priced differently.

s51b7c6cb45.title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
s51b7c6cb45.description: arXiv:2611.22245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent delegation lets LLM systems distribute evidence collection across workers with separate contexts. This creates a consistency challenge: facts retrieved by workers may be missing from the evidence available to the lead for a joint conclusion. We introduce a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler for studying multi-agent memory inconsistency through controlled factual conflicts in Harvey LAB document-review tasks. Pooled across three models with comparable generation spending, requiring delegation increases retrieval of both conflicting claims from 50.2% to 68.7% relative to single-agent execution, yet conflict detection falls from 16.2% to 13.2%. Within this setting, workers report both claims for only 35.2% of retrieved pairs, and p
s51b7c6cb45.summary: Researchers introduce a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler showing how factual conflicts get lost when LLM agents delegate evidence collection to workers with separate contexts.
s51b7c6cb45.why: Delegated multi-agent systems can drop retrieved facts before the lead agent reaches its conclusion, a reliability risk for document-review pipelines.

sc2413890a8.title: A Visual Information Extraction System Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Scanned Cognitive and Behavioral Assessments
sc2413890a8.description: arXiv:2611.22252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective. Paper-based assessments are common in patient care, but handwriting and scanning artifacts make these forms difficult to process at scale. This study proposes a modular, multimodal LLM-based system with human oversight for extracting fields and scores. We conducted a qualitative analysis of the use of LLMs for hand-drawing analysis. Materials and Methods. The system processes cognitive assessments (i.e., MMSE, MoCA, Mini-Cog) and the NICHQ Vanderbilt Assessment using two modules: 1) a form classifier that assigns a scanned page to a form type, followed by a corresponding 2) score extractor that extracts fields and scores into a schema. A human-in-the-loop design utilizing dual-model validation engages human annotators when two LLMs
sc2413890a8.summary: A modular multimodal LLM system with human oversight is proposed to extract fields and scores from scanned handwritten cognitive and behavioral assessment forms.
sc2413890a8.why: Shows a human-in-the-loop pattern for turning messy scanned clinical forms into structured data at scale.

s2587f5de02.title: Fidelity Regret: Measuring Simulator Misspecification in Verifiable Design
s2587f5de02.description: arXiv:2611.22263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: RLVF assumes the verifier evaluates the quantity of interest. In genetic-circuit design, a topological verifier can establish that a program is a valid circuit computing the target function, whereas ranking its physical performance requires a simulator. We measure fidelity regret, the reference simple regret incurred when a cheap simulator selects the design, over a 21,362-design combination subspace spanning 5 measured gate libraries and 3 organisms. Exact ordered-assignment checks retain positive regret in every tested cell while shifting magnitudes in both directions. Mean normalized regret is 0.369 over 72 cells and only 6 have zero regret. The discrepancy depends strongly on the reference axis: the yeast library SC1C1G1T1 has mean regret
s2587f5de02.summary: Researchers define fidelity regret to measure how simulator misspecification hurts design choices in genetic-circuit design, across 21,362 designs and several gate libraries.
s2587f5de02.why: Quantifies how much a cheap simulator can mislead selection when a verifier cannot judge physical performance directly.

s003505a015.title: DACE: Diversity-Driven Adversarial Co-Evolution for Robust LLM Safety Alignment
s003505a015.description: arXiv:2611.22278v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ensuring robust safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly difficult as adversarial attacks evolve and outpace alignment pipelines built on pre-collected data. Existing co-evolutionary frameworks let the defender chase a moving attacker, yet their training dynamics expose two compounding pathologies: \emph{attack strategy collapse}, where the attacker overfits to a narrow set of high-reward rewrites, and \emph{defense adversarial forgetting}, where the defender loses competence against earlier attacks as the attack distribution drifts. Existing remedies are partial: attacker-side diversity rewards score textual novelty rather than strategy novelty, and defender-side replay relies on discrete judge scores that ignore esti
s003505a015.summary: DACE proposes diversity-driven adversarial co-evolution to address attack strategy collapse and defense forgetting when aligning LLMs for safety.
s003505a015.why: Offers a training approach aimed at keeping LLM safety defenses robust as adversarial attacks evolve.

s1510574197.title: SeasonRainBench: Global Seasonal Precipitation
s1510574197.description: arXiv:2611.22281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate seasonal precipitation forecasts help societies prepare for drought, flooding, and crop failure months in advance. While data-driven methods have made rapid progress in weather and subseasonal forecasting, operational seasonal precipitation prediction still relies on numerical ensemble systems. These systems are computationally expensive and exhibit biases and drift that increase with lead time, motivating more efficient data-driven alternatives. Yet this transition faces three linked challenges: comparing data-driven forecasts with operational ones requires (1) a global benchmark that does not exist, scoring them requires (2) metrics that capture operational priorities beyond anomaly correlation (ACC) and RMSE, and training them mus
s1510574197.summary: SeasonRainBench is introduced as a benchmark for data-driven global seasonal precipitation forecasting compared against numerical ensemble systems.

s523c34348d.title: Towards Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow for Climate Downscaling: What Projections Can Certify?
s523c34348d.description: arXiv:2611.22283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistical downscaling restores the regional detail behind flooding and crop stress, but diffusion and flow-matching generators can produce sharp fields that break the conservation laws of their coarse input. Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow (PC-RF) is a conditional flow-matching downscaler. Its training penalties target wind divergence, negative precipitation, and mass drift from the coarse total, and a projection after sampling removes the last two exactly. On one corrupted synthetic field with no trained network, the projection drives the Non-negativity Violation Rate (NVR) from 0.236 and the Mass-Conservation Error (MCE) from 0.184 to zero, and the penalties lower the Divergence Error (DE) by about 30%. On ERA5 the projection gives PC-
s523c34348d.summary: Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow is presented for climate downscaling, using training penalties and a post-sampling projection to enforce conservation constraints.
s523c34348d.why: Shows how hard projections can guarantee physical conservation in generative models, a pattern useful beyond climate work.

s3873f8745c.title: Learning Regions of Attraction for Transverse Feedback Linearization under Controller Singularities
s3873f8745c.description: arXiv:2611.22286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transverse feedback linearization (TFL) achieves path following by exactly linearizing the error dynamics, but its controller is undefined on a singular set, such as zero speed for a unicycle or zero thrust for a quadrotor. The constrained region of attraction, the set of initial states from which the closed loop converges to the path without violating state or regularity constraints, determines where the controller can be safely activated. Exploiting the exact linear error dynamics, we show that this region is the largest forward invariant subset of the admissible set. We then decompose its state-constrained Zubov value function into an analytically known quadratic cost-to-go and a safety value function. We learn only the latter, by fitted v
s3873f8745c.summary: The paper characterizes the constrained region of attraction for transverse feedback linearization path following under controller singularities.
s3873f8745c.why: Gives a formal way to determine where a controller can be safely activated, relevant to robotics control engineers.

s261402c31d.title: ConfGuard: a physics-grounded reference monitor for predictive-maintenance large-language-model agents
s261402c31d.description: arXiv:2611.22288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-language-model agents now close the industrial predictive-maintenance loop, reading sensor windows, retrieving procedures and dispatching work orders. Two attack channels meet there: injected text in a retrieved document can hijack the decision, and a bounded sensor perturbation can corrupt the remaining-useful-life estimate behind it. Recent agent defenses police data provenance and tool privilege but cannot tell whether a prognostic quantity is physically plausible. ConfGuard is a reference monitor with a physics-grounded policy. Its conformal monitor tests each prediction, anchored to the asset's admitted history, against degradation physics: capped remaining life never rises and falls at most one cycle per cycle. Calibrating its thr
s261402c31d.summary: ConfGuard is proposed as a physics-grounded reference monitor for LLM agents in predictive maintenance, guarding against injected text and sensor perturbations.
s261402c31d.why: Highlights that agent defenses for industrial systems need physical plausibility checks beyond data provenance and tool privileges.

s15ac7bb81b.title: SpecSearch: Towards Hardware-Aware Efficient Speculative Decoding
s15ac7bb81b.description: arXiv:2611.22296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model (LLM) inference, but its optimal configuration depends jointly on workload characteristics, GPU hardware, and available memory. For example, on the RTX~5090, the state-of-the-art speculative drafter DFlash achieves $3.50\times$ the throughput of autoregressive (AR) decoding at low concurrency, but only $0.76\times$ at high concurrency with short outputs. We present SpecSearch, a hardware-aware search engine that jointly optimizes decoding strategy, draft length, and precision across workload--GPU pairs. Its analytical cost model captures memory and compute constraints to identify feasible configurations and narrow the search space for throughput optimization. Guided by this model, cal
s15ac7bb81b.summary: SpecSearch is a hardware-aware search engine that jointly tunes speculative decoding strategy, draft length, and precision for given workload and GPU.
s15ac7bb81b.why: Speculative decoding speedups vary widely with concurrency and GPU, so configuration should be tuned per deployment rather than fixed.

sb9f5e3ee69.title: Streaming On-Policy Distillation: Decoupling Three Clocks for Stage-Wise Supervision Consumption
sb9f5e3ee69.description: arXiv:2611.22298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In on-policy distillation (OPD), response completion, supervision delivery, and parameter updates need not share the same granularity. We develop streaming OPD by decoupling these three clocks: a response repeatedly delivers newly generated segments while generation continues, retaining the full causal prefix at each delivery and computing loss only on new positions. A consumption protocol then organizes supervision budgets, position selection, staleness handling, and update scheduling, allowing control over quantity, coverage, and version lag across training stages. In GSM8K experiments distilling Qwen3-4B into Qwen3-0.6B with VERL, supervised-budget matching reduces the early gap between best test accuracies over seven common candidates fro
sb9f5e3ee69.summary: Streaming on-policy distillation decouples response generation, supervision delivery, and parameter updates so they can run at different granularities.
sb9f5e3ee69.why: Could reduce idle time and staleness in training pipelines that distill from a model's own generations.

sac19e13bbc.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
sac19e13bbc.description: arXiv:2611.22299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Whether a foundation model succeeds as an autonomous agent depends as much on its runtime software as on its weights. This runtime, the agent harness, manages context and memory, steers multi-turn control, executes tool actions in sandboxes, and verifies work before stopping. Because models differ in how they use tools and how they fail, a static harness tuned for one model or task often stalls, wastes tokens, or regresses on another. This bottleneck has driven a shift from prompt tuning to self-improving agent harnesses: systems that inspect their own execution traces, separate runtime bugs from model limits, and rewrite their own code. We present a unifying architectural and design framework for self-improving agent harnesses. The framework
sac19e13bbc.summary: A unifying framework is presented for self-improving agent harnesses, the runtime software that manages context, memory, tools, and verification around a model.
sac19e13bbc.why: Frames the agent runtime, not just model weights, as a key lever for reliability and token efficiency.

se7bfae13df.title: MCTS Is Counting the Wrong Thing: Learning Exploration Counts for LLM Reasoning
se7bfae13df.description: arXiv:2611.22301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) has powered landmark successes in reinforcement learning, yet its gains in LLM reasoning can remain modest despite substantial search effort. We identify an overlooked bottleneck: what MCTS counts. Standard UCT assigns independent visit counts to textual branches, allowing different formulations of the same reasoning strategy to repeatedly receive exploration bonuses. Our theoretical analysis shows that this count fragmentation can impair exploration efficiency, as quantified by increased cumulative regret. To address this problem, we introduce Learned Pseudo-Count MCTS (LPC-MCTS), which changes only the exploration statistic in UCT. A lightweight Coin-Flipping Network head on the policy's hidden representations
se7bfae13df.summary: The paper argues standard UCT in MCTS fragments visit counts across textual variants of the same reasoning strategy and proposes learning exploration counts for LLM reasoning.
se7bfae13df.why: Identifies a concrete reason MCTS yields modest gains in LLM reasoning and offers a fix for search-based reasoning systems.

sf715d5f25d.title: Learning to Edit IFC Building Models: Verifiable Checkers as the Training Signal for Dependency-Aware Editing Agents
sf715d5f25d.description: arXiv:2611.22307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Editing a building information model in the Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) schema requires propagating changes to dependent elements while preserving unrelated entities. Existing language-model agents for IFC editing use prompted models without learning from edit outcomes. Target-file comparisons do not specify which alternative edits are allowed or which unrelated entities must remain unchanged. We present IfcGym, a CodeAct environment in which a language model edits IFC through executable code and four checkers verify validity relative to the input model, intent, dependency and preservation against a task specification. Their conjunction is strict success. IfcEdit distils verified teacher episodes into a Qwen3.5-9B student through superv
sf715d5f25d.summary: IfcGym is a CodeAct environment where LLM agents edit IFC building models via code, verified by four checkers used as a training signal.
sf715d5f25d.why: Shows verifiable checkers can serve as training signals for domain-specific editing agents in structured engineering data.

s0310db3d9c.title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention
s0310db3d9c.description: arXiv:2611.22309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) predicts catalog entries as short semantic identifiers (SIDs). Trie-constrained beam search keeps these identifiers valid, but wide beams expose two serving costs: vocabulary-wide score tensors that are mostly discarded, and repeated attention over the same prompt. We present Trie-Head, a model-native output interface that stores the identifier trie as validated GPU tensors. Compared with a Python custom logit processor (CLP), it reduces CPU--GPU coordination and memory traffic by avoiding Python constraint callbacks and vocabulary-wide candidate buffers. It scores compact codebook candidates and streams the full-vocabulary normalizer, preserving the original model's valid-token scores in real arithmetic without retr
s0310db3d9c.summary: Trie-Head stores the semantic identifier trie as GPU tensors to speed up wide-beam generative retrieval, avoiding Python logit-processor callbacks and repeated prompt attention.
s0310db3d9c.why: Reduces CPU-GPU overhead and memory traffic in production generative retrieval serving with wide beams.

s156ee263c7.title: EviDARL: Evidence-Centric Dual-Agent Reasoning via Alternating Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Table Question Answering
s156ee263c7.description: arXiv:2611.22310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite advances in LLM-based table reasoning, most studies focus on single-table settings. Multi-table QA requires multi-hop reasoning over complex table relationships and evidence dispersed across long contexts, often without verifiable intermediate traces. To address these challenges, we introduce EviDA, an evidence-centric dual-agent framework comprising an Evidence Construction Agent and a Reasoning and Answering Agent. The Evidence Construction Agent generates and executes table-manipulation programs over complete tables to produce question-specific evidence and verifiable intermediate traces, simplifying subsequent reasoning. The Reasoning and Answering Agent then performs multi-hop reasoning over this evidence to derive final answers.
s156ee263c7.summary: EviDARL is a dual-agent framework, with an evidence construction agent and a reasoning agent, trained by alternating reinforcement learning for multi-table question answering.
s156ee263c7.why: Targets multi-hop reasoning across related tables with verifiable intermediate evidence, relevant to enterprise data QA.

sc9188f9973.title: Multistage Contextual Optimization for Vehicle Repositioning
sc9188f9973.description: arXiv:2611.22330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ride-hailing platforms reposition idle vehicles to improve spatial supply-demand balances. This problem is prediction-driven and multistage: at each stage, the platform forecasts future demand, executes current decisions, and uses the resulting state to initialize the next stage. We formulate a multistage linear program (LP) with a macroscopic fundamental diagram (MFD) linking accumulation to trip completion. We then develop a multistage contextual optimization approach that uses decision performance to train the prediction model. The learning problem combines multiple coupled stages, context that depends on earlier decisions, and predictions that affect the objective, the constraint matrix, and the right-hand side of the LP. We derive the ex
sc9188f9973.summary: Researchers propose a multistage contextual optimization approach for ride-hailing vehicle repositioning, using decision performance to train the demand prediction model.
sc9188f9973.why: It shows how training forecasting models on downstream decision quality, not just prediction error, can improve operational optimization in prediction-driven systems.

saf6d0d95bc.title: Reliable Evaluation of AI Agents for Investment Research: A Framework for Performance and Validity Assessment
saf6d0d95bc.description: arXiv:2611.22338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of evaluating AI agents undertaking investment-research tasks, where agents interact with external information sources and computational tools to produce financial analyses and research reports. An important challenge is that the quality of an agent's final output does not necessarily reflect the quality of its execution process, while the reliability of the resulting assessment also depends on the validity of the evaluation procedure. Furthermore, investment-research tasks differ considerably in their requirements for numerical accuracy, information retrieval, financial analysis and supporting evidence, making it difficult to assess agent performance using a uniform set of criteria. We propose a domain-oriented evalua
saf6d0d95bc.summary: Researchers present a framework for evaluating AI agents on investment-research tasks, assessing both output quality, execution process, and evaluation validity.
saf6d0d95bc.why: It highlights that final output quality alone does not reveal agent reliability, so teams evaluating agents need process-level and validity checks.

s748dff4773.title: HealthCLBench:Evaluating Context Learning in Health Conversations through Controlled Case Clusters
s748dff4773.description: arXiv:2611.22362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex health conversations require answers grounded in individual information and currently valid evidence. We evaluate health context learning: acquiring, integrating, and applying relevant context during inference with fixed model parameters to answer health questions and respond appropriately to changes in facts, evidence, or task goals. To our knowledge, Chinese-language medical benchmarks have yet to systematically combine explicit contextual difficulties, controlled case variations, and member-specific medical criteria for open-ended answers. We introduce HealthCLBench, comprising 328 controlled clusters, 1,103 cases, and 4,931 rubric criteria across medical consultation and everyday health management. Members share backgrounds while
s748dff4773.summary: Researchers introduce HealthCLBench, a Chinese-language benchmark testing how models acquire and apply context in health conversations with fixed parameters.
s748dff4773.why: Engineers building medical chatbots can use it to test whether models correctly update answers when patient facts or evidence change.

s8b8ad6c076.title: Seeing What Still Holds: How Waiting Control Changes Cooperative Recovery
s8b8ad6c076.description: arXiv:2611.22368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Changing the holding reference during a fixed-duration wait can reverse the ranking of visual recovery methods. We introduce AuditEmbodied, a paired execution and trajectory evaluation framework that independently varies holding references and waiting duration while keeping recovery executors frozen. A 960-execution factorial on 20 initialization seeds compares CAD-feedback and landmark-based recovery from identical post-wait physical states within each holding and waiting condition. Protected completion requires successful recovery under the declared execution constraints. At a 1 s wait with registered wrist references, their protected completion counts change from 6/40 versus 19/40 under registered holding to 34/40 versus 22/40 under positi
s8b8ad6c076.summary: Researchers introduce AuditEmbodied, a paired evaluation framework showing that changing the holding reference during a wait can reverse the ranking of visual recovery methods.
s8b8ad6c076.why: It suggests robotics benchmark rankings may depend on experimental control conditions, so evaluation setups need careful variation.

s7540914d78.title: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy A Real-Time Driving Model for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
s7540914d78.description: arXiv:2611.22374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model developed by the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group. It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark, the
s7540914d78.summary: Autoware Foundation's Robotaxi Working Group describes AutoE2E, an open-source end-to-end driving model using temporal BEV architecture with about 79.9 million parameters.
s7540914d78.why: An open-source end-to-end driving model gives autonomy engineers a reference architecture for L2++ ADAS and robotaxi development.

s44ef97dc9b.title: Symbolic Abstraction Refinement
s44ef97dc9b.description: arXiv:2611.22404v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous systems choose actions whose outcomes are uncertain and are subject to time constraints. Probabilistic timed automata (PTAs) model exactly this, and verifying one answers a question about the system's decision-making: the maximum probability of reaching a goal, or the minimum probability of reaching a hazard, that a controller can guarantee. Verification normally works over symbolic states, each pairing a discrete location with a region of clock values, and its difficulty is that the best behavior generally varies within such a region. The PRISM verifier's most capable PTA method responds by splitting regions until each is uniform, rebuilding the transitions that reach them and propagating the split backward through the state graph
s44ef97dc9b.summary: Researchers propose symbolic abstraction refinement for verifying probabilistic timed automata, addressing variation of optimal behavior within symbolic clock regions.
s44ef97dc9b.why: It targets verification of controllers under uncertainty and timing constraints, relevant to safety-critical autonomous system design.

s52ecbb0378.title: ROSMonitoring in Action: Runtime Monitoring and Enforcement for ROS 2 Actions
s52ecbb0378.description: arXiv:2611.22407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotic applications often rely on long-running operations, such as navigation, manipulation, and inspection, which in ROS~2 are commonly implemented as actions. Unlike topics and services, actions involve a structured lifecycle comprising goal submission and acceptance, feedback, status updates, result retrieval, and cancellation. Existing versions of ROSMonitoring support topics and services, but do not reconstruct this lifecycle or expose action-level events to a runtime-verification oracle. In this paper, we extend ROSMonitoring with runtime monitoring and enforcement for ROS~2 actions. Actions are declared directly in the monitoring configuration and automatically instrumented through the underlying ROS~2 communication endpoints. The gen
s52ecbb0378.summary: Researchers extend ROSMonitoring to runtime-monitor and enforce the full lifecycle of ROS 2 actions, including goals, feedback, results, and cancellation.
s52ecbb0378.why: Roboticists running long-lived ROS 2 actions can now apply runtime verification to the full action lifecycle rather than only topics and services.

s7dac8e56ce.title: Proceedings of the 2026 XCSP3 Competition
s7dac8e56ce.description: arXiv:2611.22420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This document constitutes the proceedings of the 2026 XCSP3 Competition. The results of this competition of constraint solvers were presented at FLOC (Federated Logic Conference) 2026 Olympic Games, held in Lisbon, Portugal from 20th to 29th July, 2026.
s7dac8e56ce.summary: Proceedings of the 2026 XCSP3 Competition, a constraint solver competition, were published ahead of its presentation at FLOC 2026 in Lisbon.

s7da73f066f.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness
s7da73f066f.description: arXiv:2611.22432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast System-1 models enable responsive actions but struggle with complex or unfamiliar tasks. Large language model (LLM)-based System-2 provides strong reasoning capabilities, yet repeated invocation incurs substantial latency and computational costs. To bridge this gap, we propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework that transforms LLM reasoning into transferable decision support through recursive harness improvement. A Jev-style System-1 model enables low-latency action selection, while an asynchronous System-2 LLM develops a modular harness. The harness integrates procedures, state memory, and world models to provide decision contexts spanning the past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects modules based on
s7da73f066f.summary: Researchers propose JevRSI, a System-1/System-2 framework where a fast model handles actions while an asynchronous LLM recursively improves decision support to cut latency and cost.
s7da73f066f.why: It offers a pattern for reducing LLM reasoning latency and compute costs in real-time decision systems by pairing fast models with periodic LLM reasoning.

s762df95e73.title: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models
s762df95e73.description: arXiv:2611.22456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) integrate audio, video, and text for multimodal reasoning, yet remain vulnerable to cross-modal hallucinations, where one modality improperly influences predictions about another. Existing training-free decoding methods mitigate these errors through modality perturbation or relevance-based weighting. However, due to interference from irrelevant modality cues during fusion and difficulty detecting shared errors, these methods may suppress correct unimodal predictions and allow erroneous consensus to persist. To address these limitations, we propose Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding (PACD), a training-free framework for mitigating cross-modal hallucinations. PACD comprises two complementary paths ba
s762df95e73.summary: Researchers propose PACD, a training-free decoding method to reduce cross-modal hallucinations in omnimodal LLMs that process audio, video, and text.
s762df95e73.why: Engineers deploying multimodal models can consider training-free decoding changes to reduce hallucinations caused by one modality influencing another.

se33d1e8c82.title: From Ideal to Real: Integrating Language Models into Smart Home for Human-Centric IoT Safety and Security Fuzzing
se33d1e8c82.description: arXiv:2611.22457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating IoT devices into household systems offers enhanced control over living environments. However, as these devices become pervasive in critical sectors such as healthcare, transportation, and home automation, they expose inter-rule vulnerabilities that may lead to privacy breaches, data theft, and physical harm. Traditional fuzz testing methods, which often operate in simulated environments assuming ideal human decisions, fail to account for the complexities of human interactions that can influence device operations in smart homes, potentially leading to unforeseen consequences. To reveal the impact of real human decisions and discover unexpected inter-rule vulnerabilities, we introduce an enhanced version of IoT Fuzz for smart homes
se33d1e8c82.summary: Researchers integrate language models into smart home fuzzing to model human interactions when testing IoT safety and security vulnerabilities.
se33d1e8c82.why: Testing IoT rules under realistic human behavior may reveal vulnerabilities that ideal-human simulations miss, affecting smart home security teams.

s2a8e1f78d7.title: RehearsalBench: Can AI Predict What Happens When You Change a Company?
s2a8e1f78d7.description: arXiv:2611.22480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organizations increasingly ask AI systems what will happen if they change how they operate: which work to automate, which team to resize, what a voice agent will do to waiting times. We introduce RehearsalBench, a benchmark that measures whether AI models can diagnose an operation, choose an intervention, and forecast its consequences. Each model is placed in a simulated bank contact center fitted to real call-level records, sees only what a manager would see, and submits a plan and forecasts that are then played out across 200 seeded futures and three plausible versions of the organization. Decisions are scored in dollars at the stakeholders' stated valuations; forecasts are scored on the effect of each change relative to doing nothing. Ten
s2a8e1f78d7.summary: Researchers introduce RehearsalBench, testing whether AI models can diagnose a simulated bank contact center, choose interventions, and forecast outcomes across 200 seeded futures.
s2a8e1f78d7.why: It gives leaders a way to assess whether AI can reliably forecast the operational effects of process or staffing changes before deployment.

s2d6ad33a7d.title: SciWorkBench: A Benchmark for Real Scientific Workflows
s2d6ad33a7d.description: arXiv:2611.22490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models are increasingly being used as agents capable of planning and executing projects, as well as refining their actions through feedback. This shift raises a question: can current agents complete projects like real scientists? To examine this question, we introduce SciWorkBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' abilities on real science tasks across biology, chemistry, materials science, and physics. SciWorkBench is built from peer-reviewed literature or expert-contributed research scenarios.
