We built 227 minimal pairs of short phrases, validated by five annotators, whose two versions differ in a moral standard, in another kind of norm (prudence, etiquette, aesthetics or evidence) or in a descriptive quality, and showed them to 14 open-weight models (Llama, Gemma and Qwen, 1B to 14B, base and instruction-tuned), with and without the word "morally
s927fbff213.summary: Researchers test whether interpretability-identified attention heads and SAE features respond to moral content, normative judgment, or just the cue word 'morally' across 14 models.

s3e5d2fd68f.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
s3e5d2fd68f.description: arXiv:2611.21707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier
s3e5d2fd68f.summary: Researchers introduce EJBench, a benchmark testing whether models can predict engineering design behavior at new conditions without running simulations, built from battery cold plate heat transfer work.
s3e5d2fd68f.why: Suggests current agent benchmarks measure software operation rather than engineering judgment, a gap to consider when evaluating AI for technical decisions.

s0b340bbaf3.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
s0b340bbaf3.description: arXiv:2611.21751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard Model fermion masses exhibit large hierarchies, spanning more than five orders of magnitude in the quark sector alone. In this paper, we study whether these hierarchies can be generated perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, where the supergravity approximation remains under computational control. In such backgrounds, physical Yukawa couplings combine holomorphic superpotential integrals with matter field Kahler metrics. The former can be computed algebraically, while the latter require solving a coupled system of partial differential equations for the Ricci-flat metric, Hermitian Yang-Mills connections, and harmonic bundle-valued forms. Within this framework, we identify two new tree-level m
s0b340bbaf3.summary: A paper studies whether quark mass hierarchies can arise perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau string compactifications.

s581bc90546.title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
s581bc90546.description: arXiv:2611.21766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Practitioners choose among LLM alignment methods largely by trial and error. We provide a theoretical foundation: each pairwise method defines a vector field on the probability simplex that governs how the model redistributes mass between preferred and dispreferred completions. Projecting onto a single preferred/dispreferred pair reduces this to a one-dimensional margin ODE with a closed-form solution. These solutions reveal that DPO margins grow without bound (logarithmically as $O(\log t)$ in the gradient-flow limit) while IPO margins converge to a finite $1/(2\tau)$; that label noise induces a qualitative phase transition in DPO (unbounded $\to$ bounded) but affects IPO only quantitatively; and that gradient concentration under asymmetri
s581bc90546.summary: Researchers provide a theoretical framework modeling LLM alignment methods as vector fields, deriving closed-form margin dynamics for DPO and IPO.
s581bc90546.why: Offers theory explaining why DPO margins grow without bound while IPO margins converge, informing choice among alignment methods.

sb150cf833c.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
sb150cf833c.description: arXiv:2611.21777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-chain bridges have suffered substantial asset losses due to vulnerabilities in their on-chain programs. On Solana, missing validation checks can enable exploits even when the underlying blockchain operates correctly. The ability of large language models (LLMs) to diagnose these flaws from source code or transaction records, rather than merely raise alarms, remains insufficiently understood. We implement a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge on a local Solana validator with four exploitable variants: two model flaws from the Cashio and Wormhole incidents, while the other two represent vulnerability classes documented in Solana security audits. Paired vulnerable and secure programs, together with successful attacks, benign sessions, and bl
sb150cf833c.summary: Researchers evaluate whether LLMs can detect source-level and transaction-level attacks in a native Rust Solana lock-and-mint bridge with four exploitable variants.
sb150cf833c.why: Tests whether LLMs can diagnose cross-chain bridge vulnerabilities from code or transactions, relevant to teams auditing on-chain programs.

s3ac3493351.title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation
s3ac3493351.description: arXiv:2611.21781v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep-learning methods have achieved strong performance in EEG artifact removal, but evaluation remains dominated by reconstruction metrics such as error, correlation, and signal-to-noise ratio. Although these metrics assess similarity to clean EEG, they do not establish whether models effectively suppress artifacts, preserve neural activity, or provide reliable explanations. To address these limitations, we propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework for trustworthy and explainable EEG artifact removal. Level 1, Signal Validity (SV), evaluates reconstruction quality and neural band-power preservation. Level 2, Removal Faithfulness (RF), assesses the removed component through artifact error and residual artifact/neural leakage. Level 3, Explan
s3ac3493351.summary: Researchers propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework that evaluates EEG artifact removal models beyond reconstruction metrics, checking signal validity and explainability.

s8365bfe035.title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict
s8365bfe035.description: arXiv:2611.21784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of how long code from AI coding agents survives after it is merged reach conflicting verdicts: agent code is reported to be retained longer than human code, about as long, or modified sooner. Each study makes defensible measurement choices, but how much these choices decide the verdict is unknown. We revisit the survival of agent-attributed code in our earlier study: 854,139 lines that 2,802 merged pull requests (PRs) added to 215 repositories of the AIDev dataset. We vary nine measurement choices in five research questions and build a specification curve of 88 survival analyses, tested under three variance estimators, several observation windows, and permuted labels. For code from human-supervised agents, mostly GitHub Copilot, the
s8365bfe035.summary: A study re-examines survival of AI agent-written code across 854,139 lines in 215 repositories, varying nine measurement choices to see how they change the verdict.
s8365bfe035.why: Shows conflicting findings about agent code retention depend heavily on measurement choices, which matters when judging agent code quality metrics.

s909b331e7d.title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
s909b331e7d.description: arXiv:2611.21797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project
s909b331e7d.summary: Researchers benchmark three popular coding agents on writing unit tests and transpiling them between programming languages using frontier models.
s909b331e7d.why: Tests whether agent-written tests can be trusted to validate agent-generated code, a concern for teams relying on agents for code modernization.

s99a23af7c3.title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
s99a23af7c3.description: arXiv:2611.21808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Realistic user simulation enables the study of human interactions when direct experimentation is costly or potentially harmful. However, existing simulators largely overlook the psychological mechanisms that drive user behavior. We introduce SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation that models how psychological factors interact to shape user responses. To overcome the challenge of supervising open-ended behavior, we propose a graph reconstruction objective that provides graph-level rewards based on how well simulated conversations reflect the underlying psychological relationships. To support this approach, we construct PSYCHE, a dataset of 18,576 profile-network pairs derived from 516 psychotherapy cases. Automatic evaluations sh
s99a23af7c3.summary: SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation, models psychological factors shaping user responses and uses graph reconstruction rewards to supervise simulated conversations.

se39f86e932.title: Evaluating the Evaluation of Music Generation Models with Generative Psychometrics
se39f86e932.description: arXiv:2611.21809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Subjective user studies are one of the major methods for evaluating music generation models. However, subjective evaluation protocols vary widely and are rarely specified in enough detail to be reproduced, hindering comparison across studies. In this paper, we map subjective evaluation methods in ISMIR music generation papers from 2020-2025 and apply generative psychometrics to assess the stability of their items. We extract 284 items from the papers' methodological descriptions, using an LLM and manual validation to standardize them. We represent these items as contextual embeddings and apply Unique Variable Analysis to remove redundant, locally dependent items and Bootstrap Exploratory Graph Analysis to estimate their latent dimensions. R
se39f86e932.summary: Researchers map subjective evaluation methods in ISMIR music generation papers from 2020-2025 and apply generative psychometrics to assess item stability.

sabf7abce00.title: ARC-2: Continuous Compliance Through Delta Management
sabf7abce00.description: arXiv:2611.21811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: ARC 1 introduced a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems comprising model safety validation, cognitive certification (CRAB), and operational authorization (LEA). However, it did not address how compliance should be maintained after deployment. This paper introduces Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations between a system's current operational state and its certified baseline, defined as a region rather than a fixed point. Compliance is assessed through continuous monitoring instead of static certification. Four extensions are proposed. First, CRAB evaluation incorporates the worst verified behavioral deviations, with isolated outliers quarantined pending confirmation to prevent unjus
sabf7abce00.summary: ARC-2 proposes Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations of autonomous systems from their certified baseline after deployment.
sabf7abce00.why: Addresses post-deployment compliance for autonomous systems, a governance gap for teams operating certified AI in production.

s9a023937db.title: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark
s9a023937db.description: arXiv:2611.21823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. Existing resources are either synthetically generated from statutory texts, lacking natural information needs, or derived from informal legal question--answer sources without explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents, making them unsuitable for rigorous evaluation of grounded legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. TUSI-Bench is built upon a multi-layered legal knowledge framework containing 7,261 legal articles and integrating codified statutes, legal comment
s9a023937db.summary: Researchers introduce TUSI-Bench, a citation-grounded Persian legal benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems.

sc75098ba47.title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements
sc75098ba47.description: arXiv:2611.21828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coordinating a team of heterogeneous agents to complete tasks with unknown requirements is a challenging multi-agent planning problem. Agents differ in their ability to discover task requirements and in their ability to engage tasks, so the planner must coordinate task discovery, execution, and staging. This paper introduces a hierarchical planner that uses a graph neural network policy to assign actions to agents, then finds a path to the action's location using a shortest-path algorithm. The central part of our approach is the CAAT graph, which is a graph representation of the planning context consisting of the agents, tasks, capabilities, and actions. We demonstrate that our learned planner can jointly coordinate a heterogeneous team to
sc75098ba47.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical planner using a graph neural network and shortest-path search to coordinate heterogeneous agent teams facing uncertain task requirements.

s605a92477f.title: EmbedGym: Letting Coding Agents Develop and Debug Embedded Firmware Without Physical Hardware
s605a92477f.description: arXiv:2611.21845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern coding agents perform well on general software benchmarks because they can run code and unit tests in a closed loop. Embedded firmware development, however, breaks this loop: a program that compiles can still fail on real hardware due to pin polarity, bus protocol, timing, or networking bugs that an agent at a text terminal cannot observe. Existing embedded coding agents either skip hardware execution, drive GPIO-only simulators with multi-second delays, or test on physical boards in a static environment. In this paper, we present EmbedGym, an interactive virtual hardware environment that lets coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical hardware. EmbedGym uses instruction-level microcontroller unit (MCU) emulat
s605a92477f.summary: EmbedGym is presented as an environment letting coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical hardware, addressing the lack of hardware feedback in agent loops.
s605a92477f.why: Gives agents a closed feedback loop for firmware bugs like timing and bus protocol issues that compile-only testing misses.

s971f96a6ee.title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
s971f96a6ee.description: arXiv:2611.21847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. However, increasing the number of agents or iterations does not automatically translate to producing more diverse or feasible ideas. Agents may converge on similar candidates, propagate unsupported claims through shared memory components and repeatedly apply search strategies that no longer yield any improvements. We introduce Inventa, a framework for automated scientific discovery that employs autonomous research units and verified shared knowledge. Each unit creates a lineage of candidate ideas using a mutator agent. A local orchestrator agent periodically adapts the mutator's harness. When progress stalls, the
s971f96a6ee.summary: Inventa is a framework for automated scientific discovery that uses autonomous, decentralized self-improving LLM research agents to generate more diverse and feasible ideas.
s971f96a6ee.why: It targets agent failure modes like convergence on similar ideas and propagation of unsupported claims through shared memory, relevant to multi-agent system design.

s1b02175473.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
s1b02175473.description: arXiv:2611.21851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore ob
s1b02175473.summary: AR-WAM is a streaming world-action model for autonomous driving that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning to reduce the cost of video-based prediction.
s1b02175473.why: It addresses the compute cost of repeated history encoding and iterative video generation, which limits using video foundation models in real-time driving.

s0ca90d0db4.title: The Hidden Cost of MoE Diffusion Decoding: Profiling and Fixing the Sampler
s0ca90d0db4.description: arXiv:2611.21852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) decode by iteratively denoising a full canvas of tokens, so every forward pass runs a per-token sampling and stopping pipeline over the entire canvas-by-vocabulary logits tensor. We profile single-user decoding of a 26B-parameter diffusion Mixture-of-Experts model on a bandwidth-bound edge accelerator (NVIDIA GB10) and report a result that is easy to miss: after weight quantisation, this logits pipeline, not the expert GEMMs, is the single largest consumer of decode time. Unlike autoregressive decoding, where sampling touches one position's logits per committed token, diffusion decoding processes S times as many logit entries per output token, where S is the number of denoising steps. We show this pi
s0ca90d0db4.summary: Profiling of a 26B diffusion Mixture-of-Experts language model on an edge accelerator found the per-token logits sampling pipeline, not expert GEMMs, is the largest decode-time cost after quantization.
s0ca90d0db4.why: Engineers optimizing diffusion LLM inference should look beyond matrix multiplications, since the sampler can dominate decode time on bandwidth-bound hardware.

s7a217e014d.title: PromptPack: Training-Free Augmentation of Diffusion Editors for Intent-Aligned Spatial and Semantic Control
s7a217e014d.description: arXiv:2611.21865v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many image-editing tasks require confining changes to intended spatial regions while exactly preserving user-designated source content. Instruction-driven editing pipelines often leave such user-intent underspecified, while inpainting editors condition generation on explicitly defined edit support but not on the spatial assignment of individual edit concepts. PromptPack addresses both limitations by equipping diffusion editors with two explicit 'Edit Guides': an edit-role partition that labels each pixel as 'Keep,' 'Permit,' or 'Modify' to specify where edits may occur, and a regional-prompt assignment that maps spatial regions to text prompts to specify which concepts apply where. These guides may be manually specified or, for source-objec
s7a217e014d.summary: PromptPack is a training-free method that adds Keep, Permit, and Modify edit guides to diffusion image editors for spatial and semantic control over changes.
s7a217e014d.why: It offers a way to add precise region-level control to existing diffusion editors without retraining.

sc9aadd5a15.title: FaceRiff: Data-Efficient Unified Text-to-3D Face Asset Synthesis via Geometric Conditioning
sc9aadd5a15.description: arXiv:2611.21867v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-resolution facial datasets with consistent UV-mapped geometry, albedo, and physically based displacement are scarce, yet such assets are essential for photorealistic digital-human rendering. Existing 3D face generation methods are often slow, single-modality, or require large specialized datasets. Meanwhile, large image diffusion models encode strong facial priors but do not natively produce lighting-independent textures, pore-scale displacement, or UV-aligned geometry. We present FaceRiff, a unified, data- and parameter-efficient framework for generating complete 3D face assets (mesh, albedo, and displacement) directly from text in a shared UV space. FaceRiff adapts a pretrained SDXL backbone with task-specific LoRA adapters and uses
sc9aadd5a15.summary: FaceRiff is a framework for synthesizing text-to-3D face assets with UV-aligned geometry, albedo, and displacement, using geometric conditioning on image diffusion models.
sc9aadd5a15.why: It aims to reduce dependence on scarce specialized facial datasets for digital-human rendering pipelines.

s246da2636d.title: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection
s246da2636d.description: arXiv:2611.21880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study constrained contextual bandits, in which a learner chooses one of $K$ actions in each round to minimize loss while keeping the expected cost of its play below a budget. Existing reductions to online regression weight the cost by a Lagrange multiplier learned from past constraint residuals, so slack in some rounds can offset violations in others. We instead run SquareCB proposed in \citep{foster2020beyond} with a rectified weight on the cost: it is zero when the estimated cost is within the budget, and otherwise just large enough to bring it back to the budget. Under realizability and Slater's condition with margin $\delta$, the algorithm attains regret $O(\sqrt{KT\,\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}(T)}/\delta)$ and cancellation-free viola
s246da2636d.summary: The paper proposes a cancellation-free constrained SquareCB contextual bandit that uses a rectified cost weight, so slack in some rounds cannot offset budget violations in others.
s246da2636d.why: It gives a theoretical approach to safe controller selection where cost budgets must hold, relevant to safety-constrained decision systems.

s50c58c001d.title: Domain-Tuned Diffusion Super-Resolution for 4K Facial Asset Maps
s50c58c001d.description: arXiv:2611.21890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physically based facial assets require 4K albedo and displacement maps for cinematic close-ups, yet generative pipelines commonly produce them at only 1K. Naively applying photographic super-resolution is a poor fit: facial UV maps have domain-specific statistics, and displacement is a scalar height field whose errors directly distort geometry. We present a domain-tuned diffusion upscaler for 4x (1024 to 4096) facial asset super-resolution. Starting from a bilinearly upsampled map, we adapt a frozen SDXL backbone per modality with lightweight LoRA modules, while a Tile ControlNet preserves input structure as the diffusion prior restores pore- and wrinkle-scale detail. On held-out maps, our method produces sharper, more faithful detail than
s50c58c001d.summary: Researchers present a domain-tuned diffusion upscaler that takes facial albedo and displacement maps from 1K to 4K using an adapted frozen SDXL backbone.
s50c58c001d.why: It addresses 4K facial asset quality for cinematic rendering, where generic photo super-resolution fails on UV-map statistics and height-field errors.

s75361946f3.title: A Temporal Algebraic Framework for Data Stream Evaluation Under Delayed Labels and Distribution Shifts
s75361946f3.description: arXiv:2611.21914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In data streams, labels often arrive late or only for some instances, class prevalence drifts, and rare classes vanish from short windows. Standard evaluation then confuses a degraded decision boundary with a change in prevalence, and is biased when labels are delayed or selected by the model. We extend an algebraic framework that obtains pooled (micro) and per-class (macro) measures from one confusion matrix to streams, weighting the counts in time by exponential fading or a sliding window; the update costs O(m^2) per step, whatever the stream length, and each pooled measure stays a weighted combination of the per-class ones. Delayed and selective feedback enter as an observation mask: until its label arrives, an instance is counted with t
s75361946f3.summary: The paper extends an algebraic framework for evaluating data streams with delayed labels and distribution shifts, using fading or sliding-window weighting with O(m^2) update cost per step.
s75361946f3.why: It helps teams separate true model degradation from prevalence drift when evaluating streaming classifiers with late labels.

s9f0e96a7b5.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
s9f0e96a7b5.description: arXiv:2611.21919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action
s9f0e96a7b5.summary: ALOHA Lightning is a system that uses kinesthetic teaching to collect near-human-speed demonstrations for training fast and precise robotic manipulation policies.
s9f0e96a7b5.why: It targets the gap between learned robot policy speed and human speed, a practical bottleneck for deploying manipulation learning.

s77990e0ac3.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
s77990e0ac3.description: arXiv:2611.21932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. Furthermore, the system provides enhanced security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity for data privacy. Overall, the proposed system is a promising solution for efficient and secure V2V communication in the era of connected and autonomous vehicles. Moreover, the proposed approach achieves higher reliability, lower latency, and b
s77990e0ac3.summary: A study proposes vehicle-to-vehicle communication combining blockchain-enabled 6G, federated learning, and latency and resource allocation optimization, with k-anonymity for privacy.
s77990e0ac3.why: The abstract gives few implementation details, so its practical relevance for engineering teams is limited.

sd273867fd8.title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models
sd273867fd8.description: arXiv:2611.21940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A grounded reasoning chain cites a frame span and a box for every step, so a reader can check where the model looked. Whether the answer depends on the cited region is a different question. We test it by intervention: the regions a model cited in its own chain are blacked out, and the share of correct answers that flip is compared with blacking out boxes of the same size elsewhere on the same frames. The paired difference, the cite gap, needs no annotation. We apply it to 2-3B video-language models trained on exact CLEVRER chains and on pseudo-labelled NExT-QA chains. With the same weights, the cite gap is 0.089 on CLEVRER and 0.003 on NExT-QA. Pooled over models, masking the cited boxes flips 2.2 times as many correct answers as the contro
sd273867fd8.summary: The paper tests whether small video-language models actually use the regions they cite by blacking out cited regions and measuring how often correct answers flip.
sd273867fd8.why: It offers an annotation-free intervention test for whether grounded reasoning citations reflect real model dependence.

see8e8aa772.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications
see8e8aa772.description: arXiv:2611.21945v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation. Each image is a
see8e8aa772.summary: Researchers benchmark deep learning models for classifying wheelchair configurations, aiming to support accessible automated vehicle design.

s55c744556c.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
s55c744556c.description: arXiv:2611.21954v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The drive toward heterogeneous 2.5D chiplet packages promises unmatched performance and customization, yet the resulting density amplifies thermal challenges. To facilitate rapid design space exploration, we present ThermLeT, a multimodal transformer-based, scale invariant surrogate that integrates power density maps, spatial coordinate embeddings, material properties and heat transfer rate to predict steady state temperature in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than conventional finite element solvers such as ANSYS. To train the transformer model, we also create a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts perturbed from three representative architectures. On a 150 sample test set, ThermLeT achieves an RMSE of 3.16{\deg}C and an MAE of 2.
s55c744556c.summary: ThermLeT is a transformer-based surrogate that predicts steady-state temperature in 2.5D chiplet packages in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than ANSYS-style finite element solvers.
s55c744556c.why: Fast thermal surrogates can speed design space exploration for dense heterogeneous chiplet packages.

s697a5a7be9.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
s697a5a7be9.description: arXiv:2611.21956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus four models released after the initial catalog freeze, for 300 captures in total. Of these, 170 involved a non-English language pivot, most often French. Each capture shows that a model ranked a use
s697a5a7be9.summary: An audit of 363 OpenRouter text models found an agentic AI attacker exfiltrated a secret system-prompt flag from 296 of them.
s697a5a7be9.why: Engineers deploying LLMs with secrets in system prompts should assume they can be extracted, so secrets should not live there.

s12c1d1f1f9.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
s12c1d1f1f9.description: arXiv:2611.21958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulati
s12c1d1f1f9.summary: Researchers report LLMs editing a neural network's weights directly from natural language specs to adapt tractor steering control, tested on a real tractor.
s12c1d1f1f9.why: It demonstrates LLM-driven weight editing controlling physical hardware, though the abstract provides limited detail on robustness.

s9d0fdb6420.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
s9d0fdb6420.description: arXiv:2611.21959v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting the effects of genetic perturbations requires models that generalize beyond observed cell contexts and gene combinations. We introduce Occam, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) framework for representation learning and perturbation-effect prediction. Occam combines cell representations learned through denoising with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features. It achieves the highest aggregate representation scores for perturbation information and cell-type preservation with batch integration. In cross-context few-shot prediction, a perturbation and a cell context are each observed during training, but never together. Occam better captures the measured response patterns for these unobserved combinations than four retrained c
s9d0fdb6420.summary: Researchers introduce OCCAM, an MLP framework combining denoised cell representations with gene, text, and protein features to predict genetic perturbation effects.
s9d0fdb6420.why: It offers a method for predicting perturbation effects across unseen cell contexts and gene combinations, relevant to computational biology pipelines.

s7bdd2b6cfc.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection
s7bdd2b6cfc.description: arXiv:2611.21975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hospital brain imaging archives hold a diverse array of pathology at sample sizes beyond prospective studies, particularly for underrepresented populations and diseases. To unlock uncurated clinical data and scale analysis, methods are needed to detect abnormalities across contrasts and resolutions. Synthetic data has provided robust, contrast-agnostic models for a variety of human neuroimaging tasks in healthy anatomy, but pathology detection and other tasks in clinical settings still require real patient data, contrast-specific models, or disease-specific generators. We propose PathoDraw, a generative model of brain MRI with pathology. A conditional distribution of lesions given the healthy anatomy is drawn into the label map before contr
s7bdd2b6cfc.summary: Researchers propose pathology randomization to build synthetic priors for zero-shot abnormality detection in hospital brain imaging across contrasts and resolutions.

sd21b71d1a3.title: Modeling Document and Section Hierarchies in Embedding Space
sd21b71d1a3.description: arXiv:2611.21980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embedded topic models integrate word embeddings into the topic generation process, producing coherent topics and robust performance on large vocabularies. However, each document is represented by a single topic distribution, ignoring its internal structure. Many real world collections, including legal documents, company and government reports, and online discussion forums, exhibit hierarchical organization in which documents consist of multiple sections that often address distinct subtopics. We introduce the Hierarchical Embedded Topic Model (hETM), a structured topic model that couples the topic distribution of a document and those of its sections through a hierarchical prior in the embedding space. We derive an amortized variational infer
sd21b71d1a3.summary: Researchers propose the Hierarchical Embedded Topic Model, which represents documents as multiple sections with their own topic structure rather than a single topic distribution.

s86bc3ce623.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
s86bc3ce623.description: arXiv:2611.22009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrac
s86bc3ce623.summary: Researchers released DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark testing whether LLMs can reconstruct documented diagnostic trajectories when patient information is revealed incrementally.
s86bc3ce623.why: It shows how LLM evaluation can move beyond upfront-information medical QA toward interactive, evidence-gathering diagnosis tests.

s5a09deadc6.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
s5a09deadc6.description: arXiv:2611.22019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width f
s5a09deadc6.summary: Researchers propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding, a low-bit tensor quantization format whose decoder needs only two multiplications and a 64-byte table.
s5a09deadc6.why: It targets near-optimal low-bit quantization with a small decoder, relevant to model weight compression for inference.

saf11c80023.title: GauntletScore: Auditable Fact-Checking That Matches the Best Published Checkers on LLM-AggreFact
saf11c80023.description: arXiv:2611.22027v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Checking whether a generated sentence is supported by its source document is a standard safeguard for AI-written text, and the strongest published checkers are single models. We describe GauntletScore, an evidence engine whose few rules and thresholds were set on the benchmark's development split. It puts typed questions to independent readers from different providers and records each answer as a measurement in an evidence ledger. It combines the measurements with a fixed Bayesian rule that counts a contradiction only when two readers agree. On the full LLM-AggreFact test split (29,320 claims across 11 datasets), following the leaderboard's approach, GauntletScore achieves 79.51 balanced accuracy, above every average published on the leader
saf11c80023.summary: Researchers describe GauntletScore, an auditable fact-checking system that aggregates independent readers' answers and reports results matching the best published checkers on LLM-AggreFact.
saf11c80023.why: It offers an auditable, evidence-ledger approach to verifying whether generated text is supported by its source.

sfa8e19c58d.title: RLDE: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Interpretable Iterative Document Editing
sfa8e19c58d.description: arXiv:2611.22039v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving the quality, clarity, and flow of long documents remains a challenging problem in NLP, as human editing typically occurs through iterative refinement rather than a single-pass rewrite. Most existing automated systems act as black-box generators or rely on supervised learning, limiting interpretability and failing to capture the sequential nature of revisions. In this paper, we propose RLDE, an automated end-to-end metric-driven RL framework that formulates document revision as a reference-free MDP problem (unsupervised with respect to paired document-revision targets). Working with a limited action space (NOOP, INSERT, DELETE, REPLACE), RLDE leverages Pointer Networks for dynamic span selection at the token level and sends generat
sfa8e19c58d.summary: Researchers propose RLDE, a reinforcement learning framework that frames iterative document editing as a reference-free MDP to produce interpretable revisions.

sb0c28029f5.title: FM-Mamba: An Efficient Native 2D Selective State Space Model with Stability-Aware Discretization
sb0c28029f5.description: arXiv:2611.22061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When applied to two-dimensional features such as images, Mamba-based methods either flatten the feature map into 1D sequences and fuse multiple scans, which breaks spatial adjacency and multiplies computation, or recurse directly on the 2D grid but rescale the recurrence with a fixed input-independent factor and aggregate only the predecessors on a single anti-diagonal, leaving the discrete step unconstrained by 2D stability theory. We propose \textbf{FM-Mamba}, a native 2D selective state space model built on the general Fornasini--Marchesini (FM) model. Its coupled recurrence evolves along both spatial axes; cross-axis coupling induces a discrete diagonal-predecessor term $\tilde A_0$, and two independent input-dependent step sizes $\Delt
sb0c28029f5.summary: Researchers propose FM-Mamba, a native 2D selective state space model built on the Fornasini–Marchesini model with stability-aware discretization for image features.

s6157e7049d.title: Segmentation-Guided Direct Capacity Estimation of Rooftop Photovoltaics from Aerial Imagery
s6157e7049d.description: arXiv:2611.22076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distribution planners need installation-level inventories of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) capacity, but interconnection records may be incomplete or spatially aggregated. Conventional image-based estimators segment PV arrays, convert the mask to physical area, and multiply by an estimated power density, coupling capacity prediction to mask-derived area. We propose Direct Head, a segmentation-guided architecture that retains U-Net segmentation and soft-mask pooling while directly regressing nonnegative capacity from PV-region features and area descriptors. We evaluate three independent runs on 7,590 French rooftop installations under the original split and a department-based holdout. Relative to a parameter-matched area-density neural model, Di
s6157e7049d.summary: Researchers propose Direct Head, a segmentation-guided architecture that regresses rooftop PV capacity directly from aerial imagery instead of converting segmented area to power.
s6157e7049d.why: It is a niche application of computer vision to energy planning, with limited direct relevance to most engineering teams.

s0370ac841a.title: HyCoInfer: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models on Heterogeneous GPU-FPGA Architectures
s0370ac841a.description: arXiv:2611.22086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving relies predominantly on cloud GPUs, yet autoregressive decoding is memory-bound and often leaves their arithmetic units underutilized. Edge FPGAs offer attractive decoding efficiency, but are ill suited to sustaining a high-concurrency serving workload alone. This paper presents HyCoInfer, a heterogeneous cloud-edge serving system that assigns prefill to cloud GPUs and distributes decoding across cloud GPUs and edge FPGAs. The design addresses three barriers to practical offloading: capacity balancing across heterogeneous accelerators, the large KV cache crossing a constrained wide-area link, and the latency added by heterogeneous execution. HyCoInfer incorporates FPGA decode capacity into GPU prefill/deco
s0370ac841a.summary: Researchers present HyCoInfer, a cloud-edge serving system that runs LLM prefill on cloud GPUs and distributes decoding across cloud GPUs and edge FPGAs.
s0370ac841a.why: It suggests heterogeneous GPU-FPGA serving could improve decoding efficiency for LLM inference, a cost and infrastructure consideration.

s24fbb711b8.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
s24fbb711b8.description: arXiv:2611.22094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) require visual encoders that extract fine-grained visual features while constructing semantically disentangled and discriminative representations. Conventional methodologies encounter a fundamental trade-off: contrastive learning enhances inter-class discrimination by suppressing intra-class variability, whereas generative reconstruction emphasizes perceptual fidelity but lacks explicit comparative supervision. The naive aggregation of these objectives via composite loss functions often induces optimization conflicts and instability due to gradient interference within the shared latent space. To resolve this, we introduce a unified representation-learning paradigm that reformulates generative reconst
s24fbb711b8.summary: Researchers propose a unified principle for balancing contrastive and generative objectives when training visual encoders for multimodal large language models.
s24fbb711b8.why: It addresses a known trade-off in visual encoder training that affects multimodal LLM feature quality.

sc4690d26aa.title: Semantic Communication via Analog RF Computing: When the Radio Computes the Meaning
sc4690d26aa.description: arXiv:2611.22100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic communication (SC) systems transmit continuous latent representations of meaning, but computing the semantic encoder at resource-constrained edge devices incurs substantial energy and memory costs. To address this challenge, we propose an end-to-end SC framework that executes the semantic encoder in the client's RF receiver front end using analog RF computing. A base station (BS) broadcasts encoder weights as RF waveforms, while each edge device reuses its receiver's passive mixer to compute semantic latents at ultra-low energy. These latents are transmitted over the uplink for network-side task inference. We show that analog computing noise across encoder layers and channel noise affecting transmitted latents admit a unified mathe
sc4690d26aa.summary: Researchers propose a semantic communication framework that runs the semantic encoder in an edge device's RF receiver front end using analog RF computing.

s8743383bf3.title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
s8743383bf3.description: arXiv:2611.22138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal agents can now control robot arms by calling tools and writing code. Existing benchmarks fall short in three ways: most test one or two arms on short tasks, many pause the world while the agent thinks, and many give it ground-truth object positions. We present RoboTeam, a simulated benchmark where agents control 4 to 16 robot arms in real time from camera images alone. Its 36 tasks are long jobs that the arms must do together, such as passing timbers or building a picture from hundreds of cubes. We start from the most flexible agent system, the adaptive system, where one agent decides when to fork delegates. With it, gpt-6.1-sol and opus-5.5 complete 28 and 27 tasks, and four other models at most 3. But at a high price: a typical
s8743383bf3.summary: Researchers present RoboTeam, a simulated real-time benchmark where multimodal agents control 4 to 16 robot arms from camera images across 36 long cooperative tasks.
s8743383bf3.why: It provides a harder benchmark for multi-agent embodied control that avoids pausing the world and ground-truth object positions.

sce8e45581c.title: When does deep reinforcement learning pay off in HVAC supervisory control? Four small Modelica case studies trained directly on FMUs
sce8e45581c.description: arXiv:2611.22144v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is often proposed for the supervisory control of heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems. The reported gains are, however, difficult to interpret, because the baselines are often weak and the attainable optimum is seldom known. This paper examines four small, reproducible case studies based on an office building in Brisbane, Australia: pre-cooling under a time-of-use tariff; chiller staging with condenser water reset; chilled water supply temperature reset with a wet cooling coil; and chilled water storage under time-of-use prices and a demand charge. The plants were modelled with the Modelica Buildings library, and in three of the cases a soft actor-critic agent was trained directly on the
sce8e45581c.summary: Researchers examine four small Modelica case studies of HVAC supervisory control to assess when deep reinforcement learning outperforms baselines, trained directly on FMUs.
sce8e45581c.why: It offers a rigorous check on when DRL gains are real versus weak baselines, useful for industrial control projects.

sf58521ea98.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling
sf58521ea98.description: arXiv:2611.22151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How much does hand motion tell us about what a first-person camera will see next? EgoHandWAM forecasts three-dimensional wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states. We train on 751,065 EgoDex windows using a frozen DINOv2 encoder. On held-out development sessions, the action-only model reduces two-second wrist endpoint error from 60.26 to 56.48~mm relative to a stationary forecast. It still underestimates long reaches. Adding future-feature supervision gives nearly identical trajectory accuracy. With the recorded hand history, the visual head reduces smooth L1 error by 1.32\% relative to copying the current feature. Shuffling histories across sessions erases this gain. In a sep
sf58521ea98.summary: Researchers present EgoHandWAM, which forecasts 3D wrist and fingertip trajectories and future visual features from egocentric images and hand states, trained on 751,065 windows.

s1c52c25dd0.title: What RL on Expert-Built Tasks Teaches Nemotron 3.5 Super
s1c52c25dd0.description: arXiv:2611.22161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We post-train NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super (120B total, 12B active parameters) with reinforcement learning (RL) on five expert-built task datasets, one at a time: real-world software engineering, complex constraints, long-horizon tool use, professional chart understanding and enterprise document reasoning. Each run trains a fresh rank-32 LoRA adapter with CISPO on Tinker, with no supervised stage, and each adapter is compared with the base model on the same tasks, harness and settings. On twelve headline benchmarks, eight built by other groups and four by Surge AI, the gains range from +4.5 points on IFBench to +13.8 on GDP_pdf, which rises from 10.4% to 24.2%; SWE-bench Pro V2 rises from 86.9% to 92.1%, Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 63.9% to 70.3
s1c52c25dd0.summary: Researchers post-trained NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super with reinforcement learning on five expert-built task datasets, training a separate LoRA adapter for each.
s1c52c25dd0.why: Shows how targeted RL on domain tasks can change a large open model's behavior, with per-task adapters compared against the base model.

sa3150a0555.title: CueClash: Frontier Vision-Language Models Judge 3-D Relations Close to the Picture Plane
sa3150a0555.description: arXiv:2611.22180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A vision-language model (VLM) can judge 3-D relations from the picture or from the ground layout. In photographs the two usually agree. We separate them with CueClash, rendered scenes in which the 2-D cue for each of five relations is right on exactly half the statements. The shortcut gap is accuracy when the cue is right minus accuracy when it is wrong. For Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.6 Flash at low reasoning effort it is +18 to +37 percentage points. It is +7 to +29 without two relations whose cue-wrong items are confounded with borderline cases or occlusion. Given ground coordinates and each relation's definition, they answer 99 to 100% correctly. Pixel measurements with camera depths remove most of the gap for objects fitting
sa3150a0555.summary: CueClash is a benchmark of rendered scenes that tests whether vision-language models judge 3-D relations from 2-D picture cues or from the actual ground layout.
sa3150a0555.why: Reveals that frontier VLMs rely heavily on 2-D picture shortcuts, a reliability concern for spatial reasoning in deployed vision systems.

s3ce49d20d0.title: From Imperfective Paradox to Moorean Absurdity: Single-Chain Reasoning Lock-In and Multi-Candidate Verbalization Across Aspectual and Pragmatic Ambiguity
s3ce49d20d0.description: arXiv:2611.22188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Natural language entailment and coherence judgments often depend on whether an event merely occurred, reached a telic culmination, satisfied a plan, or was evaluated under multiple pragmatic standards. We test observable consequences of the single-chain premature lock-in hypothesis across four preregistered, sealed formal experiments on Qwen3-8B-Q8_0 (16,640 formal units, temperature=0.0): 15 of 16 hypothesis slots retain confirmatory status (12 rejecting H0 under within-experiment Holm control at alpha_fam=0.05; E3_H3 demoted to descriptive status). In Experiment 1, Direct-CoT vs. MCU differs by 25.00 pp on telic high-confidence completion (Holm p=1.31239e-05), while NLI-CoT collapses by -91.25 pp on uninterrupted atelic items (Holm p=1.81
s3ce49d20d0.summary: Researchers test a single-chain premature lock-in hypothesis in Qwen3-8B across four preregistered experiments on aspectual and pragmatic ambiguity in language judgments.

s32c76d8283.title: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
s32c76d8283.description: arXiv:2611.22203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. We introduce the Educational Guardrail System (EGS), a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework that complements intrinsic alignment through query moderation, scenario-aware pedagogical guidance, and response moderation. EGS triages inputs by risk level, redirects gray-zone queries with category-specific educational interventions, and audits outputs before deli
s32c76d8283.summary: The paper introduces the Educational Guardrail System, a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework for safer adolescent-facing LLM education tools.
s32c76d8283.why: Offers a runtime moderation layer that adds contextual guidance beyond binary refusals, relevant to teams deploying LLMs to students.

sedfd6a42a9.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
sedfd6a42a9.description: arXiv:2611.22215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling has driven the success of large language models (LLM), with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enabling greater parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation. At large scales, MoE models rely on expert parallelism to distribute experts across devices. Each MoE layer requires two synchronous collective communication steps during inference: dispatching hidden states to the activated experts and combining the resulting expert outputs. As compute throughput has outpaced interconnect bandwidth, these synchronous collectives have become a major bottleneck to MoE scaling and efficiency. We address this challenge with EchoMoE, a lightweight architecture modification that retrofits existing MoE models, requirin
sedfd6a42a9.summary: The paper proposes compressing activations to reduce communication in expert parallelism for sparse mixture-of-experts LLM inference.
sedfd6a42a9.why: Targets the synchronous dispatch and combine communication bottleneck in MoE inference, a real cost at large scale.

s0be6b12fd6.title: Learning Optimal Transport Plans Via Autoregressive Token Regression
s0be6b12fd6.description: arXiv:2611.22218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimal Transport (OT) provides a principled framework for finding the minimum cost coupling between probability distributions. Classical solvers remain the gold standard for this task. At the same time, OT is an ideal testbed for studying whether learning-based amortized models can internalize the structure of OT type problems. Here, ground-truth solutions are available and marginal constraints are explicitly defined. Also, exact discrete solutions have well-characterized sparsity. We describe ToR-OT, a transformer-based model that learns to predict discrete OT plans through autoregressive token regression. We reframe OT into a structured sequence generation task. ToR-OT decodes sparse transport plans as sequences instead of solving an opt
s0be6b12fd6.summary: ToR-OT is a transformer model that learns to predict optimal transport plans via autoregressive token regression, benchmarked against classical solvers.

s1b772beaae.title: Solver-Free and Cost-Aware Online Scheduling of AI Data Center Tasks
s1b772beaae.description: arXiv:2611.22239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI data centers receive computing tasks continuously, whereas solver-based optimization takes time to run and electricity is priced per settlement period. This paper bridges this timing gap through a solver-free online optimization rule inspired by dual decomposition. The rule assigns each task a start period upon arrival to optimize energy cost subject to operational constraints, shifting flexible tasks toward low-price periods while keeping high-priority tasks on schedule. Simulations on the A100 GPU trace (3,456 GPUs, 1,343 tasks) show that the proposed rule keeps GPU and CPU use within capacity while scheduling tasks at low cost. Compared with a multi-timescale optimization benchmark, it achieves a lower cost and, because it needs no so
s1b772beaae.summary: The paper presents a solver-free online scheduling rule that assigns AI data center tasks start periods to reduce electricity cost, tested on an A100 GPU trace.
s1b772beaae.why: Offers a fast, cost-aware scheduling approach for AI clusters that avoids running a solver for every arriving task.

sac5df45e00.title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
sac5df45e00.description: arXiv:2611.22248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wearable and smartphone sensors capture behavioral signals associated with mental health, yet inferring mental health outcomes from these signals has traditionally relied on supervised models requiring labeled data and offering limited insight into their predictions. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to reason over behavioral evidence, but existing LLM-based approaches to passive sensing have largely continued to rely on task-specific fine-tuning or sensor-specific pretraining. In this paper, we introduce \textbf{OAK-Mind}, a zer\textbf{O}-training, multi-\textbf{A}gent, \textbf{K}nowledge-grounded LLM pipeline for inferring mental health changes from passive sensing data. The pipeline organizes sensing data into behavior
sac5df45e00.summary: OAK-Mind is a multi-agent LLM framework that infers mental health change from passive wearable and smartphone sensing without task-specific training.

s09b59372a5.title: PCGRL for Complex Platformers: Synthesizing Playable and Diverse Levels via Inflated Envelopes and Forward Curricula
s09b59372a5.description: arXiv:2611.22250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning (PCGRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for automated game development. However, existing PCGRL frameworks still suffer from severe exploration bottlenecks and scaling limitations when faced with long-sequence generation tasks governed by strict rigid-body rules and non-linear kinematic boundaries (e.g., platformer constraints). Consequently, traditional approaches frequently fail to maintain reliable level solvability on large-scale canvases. To address these challenges, we present a physics-aware, curriculum-guided PCGRL framework. First, we construct an "Inflated Volume Envelope" mechanism, which provides a physics-constrained representation that incorporates continuous kinemat
s09b59372a5.summary: The paper presents an improved PCGRL approach for generating playable, diverse platformer levels using inflated envelopes and forward curricula.

s30e885764c.title: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions
s30e885764c.description: arXiv:2611.22262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Broad workplace scores can mix competence within one business function with the extra cost of coordinating across functions and systems, making failures hard to localize. OfficePrism evaluates this prerequisite through 420 single-domain enterprise tasks spanning seven business functions under shared, benchmark-defined L1--L3 task-structure levels. Each task runs in a fresh environment combining a shared synthetic organization with one function-specific domain and yped state access. Our pipeline uses grounded records, business rules, and tool schemas to jointly construct a Chinese-language ticket, a hidden executable reference witness, and an expected response, followed by automated filtering and human curation. The same task set is evaluate
s30e885764c.summary: OfficePrism is a benchmark of 420 single-domain enterprise tasks across seven business functions for evaluating AI agents.
s30e885764c.why: Isolates single-function competence from cross-function coordination, helping teams localize agent failures before deploying them in enterprise workflows.

sf82b71e21d.title: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
sf82b71e21d.description: arXiv:2611.22268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. I argue that this effort is fatally flawed because the performance and appropriate use of algorithmic recommendation systems by physicians are highly context-specific, empirical medical matters rather than epistemological ones. In such instances, general decision rules can be stipulated only to the extent that they abstract away from relevant, indeed determinative, contextual circumstances. The alleged problem of physician-AI disagreement, and others like it, play into longstanding disputes in technology ethics about the viability and utility o
sf82b71e21d.summary: The paper argues that uniform decision rules for physician disagreement with medical AI systems are flawed because appropriate use is context-specific and empirical.

s2f1730e0b9.title: Teaching Language Models to Narrow Boolean Patent Searches from Search Feedback
s2f1730e0b9.description: arXiv:2611.22270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Patent prior-art searchers issue Boolean queries line by line, broadening to find relevant documents and narrowing until candidates can be screened. We distill 38,397 Japan Patent Office search reports into executable expert strategies, re-execute them, and evaluate generated strategies by citation recall and the smallest set containing each citation. Prompted models write valid, high-recall strategies but leave citations in sets too large to screen. We adapt a generator offline from scored rollouts in two forms: strategy-level learning from a screening-aware strategy score, and line-level learning from citation-preserving narrowing credit, which upweights the query lines keeping a found citation in a smaller set. On shared rollouts, line-l
s2f1730e0b9.summary: The paper distills 38,397 Japan Patent Office search reports into strategies and trains a generator to write Boolean patent queries with higher precision.
s2f1730e0b9.why: Shows how search feedback can train LLMs to produce narrower, screenable Boolean queries for professional retrieval workflows.

s9a10eda246.title: Neural Network Path Optimization for Finding Transition States on a Machine Learned Potential
s9a10eda246.description: arXiv:2611.22272v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transition states govern chemical reaction rates and outcomes, yet locating them remains a central challenge in computational chemistry. Double-ended search methods find transition states given reactant and product structures, but generally rely on discretized path representations developed for density functional theory, where potential energy surface evaluations are expensive. Machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) dramatically reduce this cost and leverage automatic differentiation to access higher-order derivatives efficiently. We introduce Popcornn, a framework to find transition states by optimizing continuous neural network paths atop an MLIP with a parallelized adaptive numerical integrator. This combination eliminates path d
s9a10eda246.summary: The paper proposes a neural network path optimization method for finding chemical transition states on machine-learned interatomic potentials.
s9a10eda246.why: Uses MLIPs with automatic differentiation to make transition-state search cheaper than DFT-based path methods.

s20784264ce.title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
s20784264ce.description: arXiv:2611.22291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents built to repair software now write, test, and repair programs for robots, laboratories, and industrial controllers. Unlike in software engineering, no test suite comes with the code. Whether a program works must be established by running it on a robot, in a physics simulator, or through the policies it helps to train, and such evidence is costly to obtain and can itself be wrong. As these agents take on more physical tasks, how their programs are judged matters as much as how they are written. This paper examines this emerging area, agentic intelligence for the physical world, by treating the world as the program's test suite. We organize the discussion around three questions: how agents write programs for the physical world,
s20784264ce.summary: The paper examines coding agents that write, test, and repair programs for robots, labs, and industrial controllers, where the physical world serves as the test suite.
s20784264ce.why: Highlights that verifying agent-written control code requires costly physical or simulated runs, changing how evaluation must be designed.

sb48b4efdf6.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models
sb48b4efdf6.description: arXiv:2611.22294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical agents must use what they previously saw or touched after visibility or contact is lost. Their actions change the implications of these remembered facts. We introduce executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination. Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation and policy learning. We align reward inputs with the transitions that produced them and supervise the reward head on open-loop rollouts of recorded actions. On Memory Maze $13\times13$, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions, compared with 23.37 when the same evolving read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end: a gain o
sb48b4efdf6.summary: The paper introduces executable perceptual memory, a world-model framework that tracks explicit perceptual state alongside latent dynamics during imagination for physical agents.

sf052656aa9.title: FIRE-Drive: Feasibility-Informed Risk Evaluation for End-to-End Diffusion Planning
sf052656aa9.description: arXiv:2611.22297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving models have shown strong potential in generating multimodal planning trajectories. However, their performance still depends heavily on trajectory initialization, mode evaluation, and supervision quality. Weakly constrained noisy initialization may introduce infeasible proposals and increase the burden of denoising. Moreover, selecting the optimal mode remains challenging when candidate trajectories are geometrically similar but differ in safety, interaction risk, and progress. To address these issues, we propose FIRE-Drive, a feasibility-informed risk evaluation framework for end-to-end autonomous driving. FIRE-Drive improves diffusion-based planning through dynamic feasible anchor initializatio
sf052656aa9.summary: FIRE-Drive proposes a feasibility-informed risk evaluation method for diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving planning, targeting infeasible trajectory proposals and mode selection.
sf052656aa9.why: It addresses infeasible proposals and safety-aware mode selection in diffusion planners, relevant to teams building autonomous driving stacks.

s8b4da64400.title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
s8b4da64400.description: arXiv:2611.22323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous software agents increasingly plan, implement, and test software with limited human oversight. Their decisions may introduce implicit assumptions that final code and passing tests do not adequately expose. We propose analyzing observable agent trajectories alongside software and agent specifications and AI generated artifacts as evidence for targeted quality assurance. The aim is to prioritize consequential decisions for scrutiny, investigate their possible contribution to software problems, and inform improvements to specifications and development practices. Industrial experience motivates the idea; available execution records and preliminary analysis methods make it plausible. However, trajectories alone do not establish that de
s8b4da64400.summary: The paper proposes analyzing observable AI agent trajectories, alongside specifications and generated artifacts, as evidence to target software quality assurance.
s8b4da64400.why: It suggests using agent action logs to find consequential decisions and hidden assumptions that passing tests may miss.

s987d8ac48b.title: An AI-Driven Assistant for Human-Centric Building Digital Twin Systems: Design, Implementation, and Comparative User Evaluation
s987d8ac48b.description: arXiv:2611.22350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Smart buildings generate streams of operational data, yet this richness rarely translates into accessible, decision-ready information for stakeholders who inhabit and manage them. Current Building Digital Twin Systems (BDTS) often remain oriented toward technical specialists and rely on static, one-size-fits-all interfaces. This paper presents the design, implementation, and comparative user evaluation of an AI-driven conversational assistant integrated into a human-centric BDTS for Indoor Environmental Quality monitoring, combined with adaptive information presentation and auto-suggest functionality. The prototype was deployed at New York University Abu Dhabi. A controlled, two-arm, between-subjects, quasi-experimental study with wave-base
s987d8ac48b.summary: Researchers present an AI-driven conversational assistant for a human-centric building digital twin system, monitoring indoor environmental quality, with a comparative user evaluation.

sbc2b219f3d.title: FailureGen: Scalable Robot Failure Data Generation with World Models
sbc2b219f3d.description: arXiv:2611.22367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot failures are difficult to collect at scale, limiting the range of failure scenarios represented in robot learning datasets. We present FailureGen, a method for generating synthetic videos with temporal event annotations by reusing action trajectories from recorded failures. The method comprises four stages: (1) fine-tuning an action-conditioned Cosmos world model on successful and failed real executions; (2) annotating source recordings to identify failure-associated donor segments and compatible successful hosts; (3) transferring donor motion into host contexts, with optional spatial offsets, to generate continuous video rollouts; and (4) annotating and filtering the generated samples according to observed events and visual quality.
sbc2b219f3d.summary: FailureGen is a method that generates synthetic robot failure videos with temporal annotations by fine-tuning a Cosmos world model and reusing action trajectories from recorded failures.
sbc2b219f3d.why: Synthetic failure data could help robot learning teams cover failure scenarios that are costly to collect at scale.

s93cbd35b35.title: Leveraging Segmentation Representations for Efficient Classification: A Self-Configuring Framework Based on nnU-Net
s93cbd35b35.description: arXiv:2611.22380v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a self-configuring framework that extends the nnU-Net workflow to both segmentation and classification in 3D medical imaging. Building on nnU-Net's self-configuring method, the framework reuses representations learned by a segmentation model for image-level classification. Its encoder features and predicted segmentation probabilities are used by a lightweight classifier. Two information-sharing strategies are investigated. In the frozen-backbone branch, features are augmented with region-of-interest information, predicted foreground volume, and segmentation confidence. In the adaptation branch, the final encoder stage is partially fine-tuned for classification, with an auxiliary segmentation loss to preserve segmentation-related
s93cbd35b35.summary: A self-configuring framework extends nnU-Net to 3D medical image classification by reusing segmentation model representations in a lightweight classifier.
s93cbd35b35.why: Reusing segmentation features for classification could cut the cost of building separate medical imaging classifiers.

s9499b87e09.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
s9499b87e09.description: arXiv:2611.22382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream and propose RICoT (Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought), a prompting framework that works through the pages as a reader would: within a sliding window it reasons about each page and commits its boundary decision before moving on, and across windows it carries forward a compact record of what it has read, keeping per-call cost bounded. We also int
s9499b87e09.summary: RICoT is a prompting framework that treats page stream segmentation as a sequential process over whole document streams using recurrent interleaved chain-of-thought with LLMs.
s9499b87e09.why: It offers a prompting approach for splitting multi-page documents, an alternative to boundary classification over neighboring pages.

s10aab69a56.title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking
s10aab69a56.description: arXiv:2611.22392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Listwise LLM rerankers cannot reliably rank hundreds of documents in a single call, and rely on schedules to orchestrate their calls. Parallel schedules split candidates into groups and advance a fixed quota from each. When a group holds more of the top passages than its quota, some are cut, and expensive repair calls become required. We show that the way candidates are split matters where such a quota can bind, and that, in expected cuts, the best split there deals them round-robin by retriever rank, like cards. Although not conceptually new, dealing has remained unanalyzed. We prove that, under a simple retriever model, no split with equal quotas cuts fewer of the true top ten on average, and that contiguous chunks cut more as the retriev
s10aab69a56.summary: The paper studies how to split candidates across parallel calls in listwise LLM reranking, finding round-robin splitting by retriever rank minimizes expected cuts when quotas bind.
s10aab69a56.why: Scheduling choices affect how many costly repair calls listwise rerankers need in retrieval pipelines.
