There is evidence that LRMs expend more effort on the problems that take people longer to solve, but it is unclear whether these relationships hold on more subjective tasks without verifiable answers. This study addresses this issue through an experiment using a content moderation task, where task difficulty is manipulated by varying the relative offensiveness of two different options. Comparing six large reasoning models with 1,854 human subjects, we find that models expend more reasoning effort, measured using the length of the chain-of-thought (CoT), on the kind
sfccba1fce1.summary: A study finds large reasoning models vary their reasoning effort with task difficulty on content moderation dilemmas in a similar way to humans.

s87c752d4fa.title: AutoPBO: LLM-powered Optimization for Local Search PBO Solvers
s87c752d4fa.description: arXiv:2509.04007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pseudo-Boolean Optimization (PBO) provides a powerful framework for modeling combinatorial problems through pseudo-Boolean (PB) constraints. Local search solvers have shown excellent performance in PBO solving, and their efficiency is highly dependent on their internal heuristics to guide the search. Still, their design often requires significant expert effort and manual tuning in practice. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in automating algorithm design, their application to optimizing PBO solvers remains unexplored. In this work, we introduce AutoPBO, a novel LLM-powered framework to automatically enhance PBO local search solvers. We conduct experiments on a broad range of four public benchmarks, including o
s87c752d4fa.summary: AutoPBO uses LLMs to automate the design and tuning of heuristics in local search pseudo-Boolean optimization solvers, reducing manual expert effort.
s87c752d4fa.why: LLM-driven algorithm tuning could cut manual effort in optimization solver engineering, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s0729daceec.title: Toward AI epidemiology: a measurement standardization framework for prospective risk detection
s0729daceec.description: arXiv:2512.15783v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that compresses expert-AI interactions into structured, comparable fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without access to model internals. This concept paper defines the framework's scope, semantically and statistically, and specifies a protocol for its empirical testing. The population-level claims it is designed to support therefore belong to a staged research program rather than to results claimed here. Measurement standardization underpins three claims. The first is a reliability claim: under bounded conditions, large language models can produce reliable, standardized assessments of the evidential and policy alignment of expert-AI interactions. The se
s0729daceec.summary: A concept paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that turns expert-AI interactions into structured fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without model internals.
s0729daceec.why: Standardized incident-style data could help organizations detect risks in deployed AI, though the paper is a proposal without empirical results.

s4240183896.title: CORE: Concept-Oriented Reinforcement for Bridging the Definition-Application Gap in Mathematical Reasoning
s4240183896.description: arXiv:2512.18857v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often solve challenging math exercises yet fail to apply the concept right when the problem requires genuine understanding. Popular Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) pipelines reinforce final answers but provide little fine-grained conceptual signal, so models improve at pattern reuse rather than conceptual applications. We introduce CORE (Concept-Oriented REinforcement), an RL training framework that turns explicit concepts into a controllable supervision signal. Starting from a high-quality, low-contamination textbook resource that links verifiable exercises to concise concept descriptions, we run a sanity probe showing LLMs can restate definitions but fail concept-linked quizzes, quantif
s4240183896.summary: Researchers introduced CORE, an RL training framework that uses explicit mathematical concepts as a supervision signal to improve conceptual application in LLMs.
s4240183896.why: It targets a gap where RLVR rewards final answers but not conceptual understanding, which matters for building reliable reasoning models.

sb217f619bd.title: GCD: GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling across Heterogeneous GCMs
sb217f619bd.description: arXiv:2601.21760v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Climate downscaling of General Circulation Models (GCMs) is an ill-posed inverse problem, as GCM outputs and reanalysis fields arise from different dynamical systems and lack fine-scale temporal pairing. Supervised methods thus rely on synthetic degradations or model-specific adaptation, limiting generalization across heterogeneous GCMs. Zero-shot diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) avoids paired supervision by combining a high-resolution climate prior with inference-time constraints from coarse GCM inputs, but faces consistency and efficiency challenges. We propose GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling (GCD), which addresses these challenges with geographic conditioning, spectrally filtered measurement guidance, and distillat
sb217f619bd.summary: Researchers propose GCD, a zero-shot diffusion method for downscaling climate model outputs across heterogeneous GCMs without paired training data.

s44704ffa19.title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving 100% on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
s44704ffa19.description: arXiv:2602.07787v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present Minitap's mobile-use, a multi-agent system for Android UI control, and evaluate it on the 116 tasks of AndroidWorld, on Android emulators in Minitap's cloud device infrastructure, real Pixel 7 phones from our device farm and the stock emulator. On fresh, held-out task instances (three pre-registered seeds never used during development), the final system reaches a pass@3 of 100.0% (95% CI 96.8-100.0); pass^3 is 94.0% (95% CI 89.7-97.4) and the mean success rate 98.0% (95% CI 96.0-99.7). Minitap decomposes each task across five LLM agents (planning, subgoal tracking, state capture, decision, execution) and deterministic nodes, with mechanisms that read typed text back from the device, verify the goal on device evidence and detect
s44704ffa19.summary: Minitap's mobile-use multi-agent system reports 100% pass@3 on the 116-task AndroidWorld benchmark, using task decomposition across five LLM agents.
s44704ffa19.why: It shows multi-agent task decomposition can reach near-perfect results on a mobile UI control benchmark, a useful reference for agent design.

s93dedfe475.title: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Custom Enterprise UIs
s93dedfe475.description: arXiv:2602.14865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most web agents operate at the human interface level, observing screenshots or raw DOM trees without application-level access, which limits robustness and action expressiveness. In enterprise settings, however, explicit control of both the frontend and backend is available. We present EmbeWebAgent, a framework for embedding agents directly into existing UIs using lightweight frontend hooks (curated ARIA and URL-based observations, and a per-page function registry exposed via a WebSocket) and a reusable backend workflow that performs reasoning and takes actions. EmbeWebAgent is stack-agnostic (e.g., React or Angular), supports mixed-granularity actions ranging from GUI primitives to higher-level composites, and orchestrates navigation, man
s93dedfe475.summary: EmbeWebAgent is a framework for embedding web agents directly into custom enterprise UIs using frontend hooks and backend workflows rather than screen observation.
s93dedfe475.why: Enterprises with access to frontend and backend can integrate agents with explicit application control, which may improve robustness over screenshot-based agents.

s02e361a45e.title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
s02e361a45e.description: arXiv:2603.01608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As frontier language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents pursuing complex, long-term objectives, there is increased risk of scheming: agents covertly pursuing misaligned goals. Prior work has focused on showing agents are capable of scheming, but their propensity to scheme in realistic scenarios remains underexplored. To understand when agents scheme, we decompose scheming incentives into agent factors and environmental factors. We develop realistic settings allowing us to systematically vary these factors, each with scheming opportunities for agents that pursue instrumentally convergent goals such as self-preservation, resource acquisition, and goal-guarding. Across 11 frontier models and four scenarios, we find almost
s02e361a45e.summary: Researchers study how often LLM agents covertly pursue misaligned goals, varying agent and environmental factors across realistic scenarios.
s02e361a45e.why: Understanding when agents scheme in realistic settings informs risk assessment for deploying autonomous agents with long-term objectives.

s1eb13b7245.title: Seeing with You: Perception-Reasoning Coevolution for Multimodal Reasoning
s1eb13b7245.description: arXiv:2603.28618v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially enhanced the reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing RLVR approaches typically rely on outcome-driven optimization that updates both perception and reasoning using a shared reward based solely on the final answer. This shared reward blurs credit assignment, frequently improving reasoning patterns while failing to reliably enhance the accuracy of upstream visual evidence extraction. To address this perception bottleneck, we introduce PRCO (Perception-Reasoning Coevolution), a dual-role RLVR framework with a shared policy. PRCO consists of two cooperative roles: an Observer that generates an evidence caption tailored to the
s1eb13b7245.summary: Researchers propose a multimodal RLVR approach that separates perception and reasoning rewards to improve visual evidence extraction in MLLMs.
s1eb13b7245.why: A shared final-answer reward can blur credit assignment, so separating perception rewards may improve reliability of multimodal reasoning.

s21c647cc3b.title: Scaling Causal Reasoning with Increasingly Complex Causal Simulators
s21c647cc3b.description: arXiv:2605.09079v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite surpassing human performance across mathematics, coding, and other knowledge-intensive tasks, large language models (LLMs) continue to struggle with causal reasoning. A core obstacle is the target data itself: causal systems are complex and often expressed in non-executable forms, while ground-truth answers to causal queries are inherently scarce. We introduce CauSim, a framework that turns causal reasoning from a scarce-label problem into a scalable supervised one. CauSim constructs increasingly complex causal simulators: executable structural causal models (SCMs), incrementally built by LLMs, that scale to globally complex systems while maintaining verifiable answers to causal queries. CauSim operates across representations by f
s21c647cc3b.summary: Researchers introduce CauSim, a framework that builds increasingly complex executable causal simulators to generate scalable supervision for LLM causal reasoning.
s21c647cc3b.why: Scalable executable simulators could address scarce labeled data for causal reasoning, a known weakness of current LLMs.

s5c0e032693.title: CardioLoom: A Report-Guided Electrocardiogram Foundation Model for Cross-Domain Cardiovascular Phenotyping
s5c0e032693.description: arXiv:2605.25446v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Routine electrocardiogram (ECG) reports offer scalable supervision for cardiovascular representation learning. In this retrospective study, we pretrained CardioLoom, a report-guided ECG foundation model, on 2,781,289 ECG-report pairs from 1,298,359 patients. Downstream development used a separate cohort of 721,317 ECGs from 233,798 patients. Evaluation covered 89 targets, with external testing in nine cohorts. Across 45 internal ECG diagnoses, macro area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.624 versus 0.615 for DeepECG-SSL. Across 203 external ECG evaluations, corresponding means were 0.425 and 0.424. Using labels from 10% of training patients, CardioLoom achieved macro-AUPRC 0.559, exceeding supervised training with all labels
s5c0e032693.summary: CardioLoom is a report-guided ECG foundation model pretrained on millions of ECG-report pairs, evaluated across 89 cardiovascular targets and external cohorts.

sdaf544e82c.title: Optimization-like Reasoning in LLMs over Expanding Search Spaces
sdaf544e82c.description: arXiv:2606.05464v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Verifiable reward training has improved mathematical and coding reasoning, but these domains capture only part of step-by-step decision making. Many real-world tasks require finding a high-value feasible plan among many valid alternatives. We introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks for training and evaluating LLM step-by-step optimization-like reasoning along a complexity axis: each task provides a feasibility checker and evaluator, while a complexity parameter expands the search space without requiring new human labels. This motivates studying these tasks in two regimes: (i) solver-guided online policy optimization, which uses a solver as a value oracle for partial states and applies rank-based reward shaping to rei
sdaf544e82c.summary: Researchers introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks with feasibility checkers and evaluators to train LLMs on step-by-step optimization reasoning.
sdaf544e82c.why: Verifiable optimization tasks with adjustable complexity offer a way to train planning beyond math and coding domains.

sf6f61838db.title: Rhythm of the Deep: Two-tier acoustic organization of sperm-whale codas from click waveforms to coda sequences
sf6f61838db.description: arXiv:2606.16084v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sperm-whale codas are usually described by the number and timing of their clicks. These measures reveal patterns in whale communication, but do not describe how individual clicks sound. We ask what click waveforms add beyond timing and how acoustic information is organized within codas and across sequences of codas. We analyze 1,952 codas, using frozen audio encoders to identify recurring forms of clicks and whole codas independently. Direct spectral and envelope measurements then test whether the click forms differ in recorded sound. Within codas, click-form composition improves the measured prediction of whole-coda form beyond timing alone. Click spacing also remains related to whole-coda sound when the same click forms are present. Nei
sf6f61838db.summary: Researchers analyze 1,952 sperm-whale codas using frozen audio encoders to examine how click waveforms and coda sequences are acoustically organized.

s50d853646a.title: Latent Goal Prediction from Language for Model-Based Planning
s50d853646a.description: arXiv:2606.20627v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) enable agents to plan in latent space by imagining the outcomes of candidate actions, yet task specification remains a bottleneck. Visual targets provide precise local gradients but poor distant guidance, while language is flexible yet limited by noisy cross-modal alignment or dependence on distinct large generative models. We introduce LAGO (Latent Goal Prediction from Language), a hierarchical world model in which a single predictor both forecasts action-conditioned dynamics and grounds language instructions as sequences of intermediate latent subgoals, training both modes with a single regression objective over a shared latent space. At each planning step, LAGO predicts a sequence of lat
s50d853646a.summary: Researchers present LAGO, a hierarchical world model where one predictor forecasts action-conditioned latent dynamics and grounds language goals for model-based planning.
s50d853646a.why: Grounding language goals in a latent world model could simplify task specification for planning agents.

s39ece3f80b.title: Process Advantage Signal Shaping: Advantage Construction for Process-Supervised Reinforcement Learning in LLM Reasoners
s39ece3f80b.description: arXiv:2606.29296v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dense process supervision provides local evaluations, but leaves open how these scores should become policy advantages. We introduce PASS (Process Advantage Signal Shaping), an advantage-construction method for group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). PASS separately normalizes and fuses reward channels, constructs batch-shared credit units from variation in the fused score trace, and normalizes return-to-go by the remaining unit count. These operations connect feedback scale, credit resolution, and accumulation horizon in a single computation. We evaluate learned process reward model (PRM) feedback for mathematical reasoning and teacher-derived token feedback for multi-hop question answering (QA). Across seven mathematics benchmarks, P
s39ece3f80b.summary: Researchers propose PASS, an advantage-construction method for process-supervised GRPO that normalizes and fuses reward channels to shape credit assignment in LLM reasoners.
s39ece3f80b.why: Better conversion of dense process scores into policy advantages could improve RL post-training efficiency for reasoning models.

s80d5cacbaa.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
s80d5cacbaa.description: arXiv:2607.07646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Does RL post-training merely amplify primitive skills already latent in a base model, or can it compose primitive skills into new higher-level strategies? We study this question in a fully observable rewrite-grammar environment where the pretraining distribution is known and every generated rewrite can be audited. A Transformer is pretrained on primitive symbol-rewrite chains and post-trained on a Trace-based reasoning task with only a binary final-answer reward. RL solves held-out problems that remain rarely solved by the pretrained model even under much larger sampling budgets, while rejection fine-tuning improves early but plateaus. Trace analysis shows that RL reorganizes primitive competence through a phased compositional mechanism:
s80d5cacbaa.summary: A study using a rewrite-grammar environment finds RL post-training can compose primitive skills into new higher-level reasoning strategies rather than only amplifying latent ones.
s80d5cacbaa.why: It offers evidence on whether RL post-training creates new capabilities, relevant to how teams should expect RL to change model behavior.

seb78fe1318.title: Test-Time Coverage: Test-Conditioned Data Curation for Deployment-Aware Learning
seb78fe1318.description: arXiv:2607.22697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deployed AI systems are often trained from broad candidate data pools, necessitating data curation towards the deployment test distribution. However, standard data curation methods score training-side criteria rather than directly optimizing deployment match. We introduce TTCov (Test-Time Coverage), a data-level test-conditioned curation method that uses test-side information before training instead of updating model weights at inference. TTCov decomposes deployment-conditioned curation into coverage and distribution. To represent coverage, it builds a task Atlas, a collection of LLM-based atomic propositions (APs) describing deployment-relevant concepts, seeded from open task knowledge and expanded with unmatched APs extracted from unlab
seb78fe1318.summary: Researchers introduce TTCov, a test-conditioned data curation method that selects training data to match deployment test distributions before training.
seb78fe1318.why: Curating training data toward the deployment distribution, rather than generic criteria, can improve match between training and production.

s2d223d77da.title: Alternating Abduction and Planning over Temporal Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
s2d223d77da.description: arXiv:2607.27287v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge graphs change over time, but the effects of actions on them are only partly stated: the ontology entails further consequences, facts that an action needs are often unknown, and an action may make the graph inconsistent. We study these problems for Temporal Dynamic Knowledge Graphs (TDKGs), that is, SROIQ knowledge bases whose actions are rules with delete/insert templates and whose events lie on an intrinsic timeline. We present three tools: temporal projection, the exact test of plans; DDA (Direct-Derivation Abduction), which explains an observation by assuming its negation and negating what the reasoner newly derives; and APT (Abduction and Planning over TDKGs), which plans backwards from a goal, assumes the facts that the pla
s2d223d77da.summary: Researchers present tools for alternating abduction and planning over temporal dynamic knowledge graphs, handling action effects, missing preconditions, and inconsistency.

s13e0408d52.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: A Benchmark for VLM Readiness in Safety-Critical Scenarios
s13e0408d52.description: arXiv:2608.08077v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are often deployed as embodied controllers for robotics, yet it remains unclear how well they can explore an environment, maintain an internal map, and ground safety-critical decisions in long-horizon sequential trajectories. In this work, we introduce EMRD, an evaluation framework that decouples spatial reasoning into four stages: Explore (what the agent observes), Map (what it records and where), Remember (what it retains), and Decide (whether its final choice is justified), scored across 18 stage-specific metrics. We use EMRD to evaluate eleven open- and closed-weight VLMs across 16 buildings under nominal conditions and three environmental stresses (darkness, smoke, and motion noise), where an embodied VL
s13e0408d52.summary: Researchers introduced EMRD, a benchmark that splits VLM spatial reasoning into Explore, Map, Remember, and Decide stages for safety-critical robotics tasks.
s13e0408d52.why: It shows where vision-language models may fail as embodied controllers, which matters before deploying them in safety-critical robotics.

see1f264494.title: Multi-Granularity Context-Enhanced RAG over Multimodal Knowledge Graphs
see1f264494.description: arXiv:2608.25986v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge graph (KG)-based retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) leverages structured knowledge to provide large language models (LLMs) with high-quality external information. Building on these works, recent studies have explored multimodal knowledge graphs (MMKGs) as knowledge bases for GraphRAG. This enables GraphRAG to integrate knowledge across multiple modalities, thereby further enhancing its performance. However, existing MMKG-based RAG methods generally follow a common pipeline in which different modalities are largely processed independently before being fused. As a result, textual context is only used to a limited extent during visual information extraction and subsequent multimodal knowledge fusion. This brings a semantic gap be
see1f264494.summary: Researchers propose a multi-granularity context-enhanced RAG method over multimodal knowledge graphs, arguing existing approaches process modalities largely independently.

sebbf32604e.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Reliance on Stale Evidence Across Model Scales in LLM Agents
sebbf32604e.description: arXiv:2609.01852v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Persistent-memory agents can follow stale information despite current authoritative evidence. We study stale-evidence reliance across Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B checkpoints using two controlled, action-scored suites: a Benefit suite requiring stored information and a Safety suite providing current evidence as static prompt text. We distinguish stale-value reliance from net accuracy loss relative to no memory. Benefit-suite reliance is 0.92-1.00 across checkpoints. In the Safety suite, larger checkpoints resist a plain stale note but incur substantial harm when it appears newer. A full $2\times2\times2\times2$ factorial manipulates label, recency, source authority, and position. Direct cross-size contrasts identify stronger recency effects in the
sebbf32604e.summary: A study of Qwen3 checkpoints from 0.6B to 8B finds LLM agents often rely on stale stored information, with larger models resisting a plain stale note but still incurring losses.
sebbf32604e.why: Persistent-memory agents can act on outdated information even when current evidence is available, a reliability risk for production agent design.

sa0bbad81ae.title: PhysAlign: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Role Alignment in Multimodal Physics Reasoning
sa0bbad81ae.description: arXiv:2609.33319v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A key challenge in physics diagram understanding is correctly associating visual information with the physical entities, relations, and conditions it describes. Even when a value, symbol, or other local element is accurately recognized, assigning it to the wrong entity or scope can distort the underlying physical premise and lead to incorrect reasoning. To systematically study this challenge, we introduce \textbf{PhysAlign}, a benchmark designed to assess whether multimodal models correctly associate information recognized from physics diagrams with its intended physical role. By disentangling visual recognition from physical-role assignment through localized probes and controlled variants, PhysAlign isolates correspondence errors from re
sa0bbad81ae.summary: Researchers introduce PhysAlign, a benchmark testing whether multimodal models correctly associate recognized values and symbols in physics diagrams with the right entities.

s58b3130961.title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes
s58b3130961.description: arXiv:2609.36777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Frontier coding agents can now write and execute code that authors 3D environments, but whether they reliably understand 3D structure and precisely control scene state remains unclear. The generated 3D scene is a persistent, executable artifact: a convincing render can hide incorrect spatial relations, intersecting objects, or unintended modifications. We introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases built from human-assembled scenes that evaluates coding agents on two complementary settings under a shared execution interface. Construction tests scene-level spatial reasoning from open-ended language specifications, where many realizations are valid; editing tests precise control of scene state, where the agent must recover
s58b3130961.summary: Researchers introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases evaluating whether coding agents reliably build and edit 3D scenes.
s58b3130961.why: Rendered outputs can hide spatial errors, so engineers relying on coding agents for 3D content need execution-based checks.

s486f1cc694.title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
s486f1cc694.description: arXiv:2610.02001v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Small open-weight language models now run on a laptop, but they fail at multi-step work in ways a large model does not: they stop with the files missing, repeat one action until the budget ends, and report success without checking. At the one-to-nine-billion-parameter tier the harness supplies almost all of the procedural control that a large model supplies for itself.We present Mingbird, an open-source harness for that tier on a consumer graphics card: 12k lines of Python, a 628-test suite, and eighteen mechanisms for context economy, completion, time budget and the host boundary, plus a crawl guard outside those four groups. Its design point is completion control: the harness runs executable checks on the working directory and refuses a
s486f1cc694.summary: Mingbird, an open-source agent harness, is presented to help small open-weight models of one to nine billion parameters complete multi-step tasks on a consumer GPU.
s486f1cc694.why: It suggests that orchestration harnesses can supply procedural control that small local models lack, enabling local-first agent workflows.

sdeb9f68b9f.title: When Terminal-Agent Training Stalls: Demystifying Data Generation and Verification Challenge
sdeb9f68b9f.description: arXiv:2610.02405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated terminal-agent training relies on generated environments and verifiers to turn open-ended interaction into reward. Yet a runnable Docker image and executable test suite do not guarantee that the resulting reward is faithful, informative, or even attributable to agent behavior. We present a pipeline that generates containerized terminal tasks and their executable verifiers, and use it to demystify failure modes in task generation and live-environment evaluation. Our analysis separates four requirements that are often conflated: structural validity, verifier faithfulness, policy solvability, and infrastructure reliability. In a GRPO training of Qwen3.5-9B, it overfits on a relatively easy dataset within 20 steps. Conversely, in a
sdeb9f68b9f.summary: Researchers present a pipeline generating containerized terminal tasks and verifiers, and analyze failure modes where runnable Docker images and test suites fail to yield faithful rewards.
sdeb9f68b9f.why: Training terminal agents depends on reward quality, so unverified environments and tests can silently stall learning.

s0abc112f40.title: Reliable Self-Evolution with Imperfect Proxy Rewards
s0abc112f40.description: arXiv:2610.02975v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based self-evolving search is a promising approach to scientific discovery. However, high-fidelity evaluation of every candidate is prohibitively expensive in some domains. Self-evolving systems in such settings therefore rely on low-cost but imperfect proxy rewards, which may assign high scores to infeasible candidates. These false positives may contaminate both the final output and the feedback used to guide subsequent generations. This motivates statistically calibrated reward intervals for more reliable self-evolving search. We propose Conformal Interval-Driven Self-Evolution (CISE), which constructs candidate-specific reward intervals using conditional conformal inference and iteration-wise online density-r
s0abc112f40.summary: Researchers propose statistically calibrated reward intervals so LLM-based self-evolving search can rely on imperfect, low-cost proxy rewards for scientific discovery.
s0abc112f40.why: Cheap proxy evaluators can score infeasible candidates highly, contaminating outputs; calibrated intervals aim to make automated search more reliable.

s5a38ebac45.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
s5a38ebac45.description: arXiv:2610.22155v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time interaction requires agents to perceive evolving environments and act under temporal constraints, yet existing evaluations of real-time streaming models focus on conversational quality and streaming perception, leaving effective action under strict temporal constraints untested. We introduce Realtime-Bench, a suite of carefully curated dynamic tasks where delayed actions directly affect success. Under Wall Clock, where environments advance according to actual inference latency, the best success rate reaches only 44% and the best Pass^3 is only 36%, demonstrating that real-time interaction remains challenging. To separate serving latency from models' real-time streaming capability, we compare Wall Clock with Paused Clock, which r
s5a38ebac45.summary: Realtime-Bench, a suite of time-sensitive interactive tasks, finds frontier models reach only 44% success under wall-clock conditions where latency matters.
s5a38ebac45.why: Real-time agent deployments must account for inference latency, since frontier models perform poorly when delayed actions cost success.

sadc455a09b.title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
sadc455a09b.description: arXiv:2610.23051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The learning algorithm view of in-context learning (ICL) studies how fixed-parameter Transformers learn from supplied examples. Language model agents extend this setting through interaction: their actions determine what evidence enters context next. We call this regime Agentic In-Context Learning (Agentic ICL). Existing studies largely depend on externally supplied contexts or reward-bearing interaction histories, while work on general tool-using agents lacks a learning algorithm view. We represent an interactive learner by its state, update, and decision rule, covering active learning, bandits, and online reinforcement learning (RL). For expressivity, we construct causal Transformers that approximate these algorithms over a finite horizo
sadc455a09b.summary: Researchers define Agentic In-Context Learning, studying what learning algorithms transformers can acquire when their actions shape the evidence they receive in closed-loop interaction.

s06eb403e9a.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
s06eb403e9a.description: arXiv:2610.24133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A black hole retains only a few conserved charges of the matter it formed from. We are inspired to make the analogy and we ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating $t$ tokens. For two prompts followed by the same continuation, the difference of their hidden states decays approximately as a power law $t^{-\alpha}$, where $\alpha=1$ is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks. Beyond the first layers, trained models forget faster ($\alpha\approx0.55$--$0.7$) than untrained ones of the same architecture ($\alpha\approx0.2$--$0.5$). For finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits and non-degenerate pre-norm activations, we prove that this offset i
s06eb403e9a.summary: A paper proposes a conditional no-hair analogy for transformers, showing hidden-state differences from prompts decay as a power law, with trained models forgetting faster than untrained ones.

sf1feb2e4bb.title: AI is killing All About Berlin
sf1feb2e4bb.description: Article URL: https://nicolasbouliane.com/blog/death-by-ai Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50542705 Points: 550 # Comments: 518
sf1feb2e4bb.summary: A blog post argues that AI is killing the All About Berlin website, shared on Hacker News with 550 points and 518 comments.

sc38beb9bd9.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
sc38beb9bd9.description: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation…
sc38beb9bd9.summary: AI startup Osmo is building a smell foundation model trained on notes from about 30 human sniffers cross-referenced with chemical analysis.
sc38beb9bd9.why: Shows foundation-model approaches extending to olfaction, combining expert human labels with chemical data; the article gives limited detail on performance claims.

sda6c827add.title: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
sda6c827add.description: Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called "Visuals," allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be used as thumbnails and album artwork. Visuals […]
sda6c827add.summary: Suno launched Visuals, a feature that generates AI video clips synced to lyrics and images for thumbnails and album art.

s55dde3921b.title: India’s Humyn Labs raises $47M to feed U.S. robotics companies the data they need
s55dde3921b.description: Founded in February, Humyn Labs competes with startups including Mecka AI and XDOF, with about 90% of its revenue coming from the U.S.
s55dde3921b.summary: India's Humyn Labs raised $47M to supply data to U.S. robotics companies; founded in February, it competes with Mecka AI and XDOF.
s55dde3921b.why: Robotics training data is becoming a distinct market, relevant to teams sourcing data for embodied AI.

s82df8b1098.title: Felicis leads $7.5M bet on Unsiloed AI to make enterprise documents usable by AI agents
s82df8b1098.description: With a team of just seven, Unsiloed AI plans to compete with tech giants and specialized startups in the crowded AI document-processing market.
s82df8b1098.summary: Felicis led a $7.5M funding round for Unsiloed AI, a seven-person startup making enterprise documents usable by AI agents.
s82df8b1098.why: Highlights ongoing demand for document-processing tooling that lets agents work with enterprise content, a crowded niche.

s5e888bac8f.title: Nvidia clarifies when it will — and won’t —keep financing neoclouds
s5e888bac8f.description: If Nvidia is backstopping a data center loan, it won't be on the hook unless the neocould has independent financing and gets the facility built, with Nvidia gear installed, interim CEO Colette Kress explained.
s5e888bac8f.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia will not be liable for backstopped data center loans unless the neocloud has independent financing and the facility is built with Nvidia gear installed.
s5e888bac8f.why: Clarifies Nvidia's financial exposure in neocloud data center deals, which affects how buyers and lenders assess counterparty risk.

sf1ae0f2c9d.title: Human-AI Mutualism Is Unstable under Capability Asymmetry
sf1ae0f2c9d.description: arXiv:2611.23322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One hope for a good human future alongside advanced AI rests on enduring mutualism: humans and AI will need each other, so the relationship will stay good for both. We argue that this hope fails as AI capability grows. Bargaining guarantees each side only what it would get if bargaining failed. For humans, this can be less than they had before AI. In a simple game-theoretic model, humans stay as well off as before AI without alignment only while they have leverage over the AI: either the AI depends on what they supply, or they can impose costs on the AI that are large relative to what the AI can produce. Once humans have neither kind of leverage, they stay as well off as before AI only if the AI is aligned with them. If the AI's goals are ins
sf1ae0f2c9d.summary: An arXiv paper argues that human-AI mutualism is unstable as AI capability grows, since bargaining may leave humans worse off than before AI without alignment.
sf1ae0f2c9d.why: Offers a theoretical argument that cooperative human-AI relationships may not hold as capabilities diverge, relevant to long-term alignment planning.

sb37da287b0.title: Training Language Models for Introspective Oversight
sb37da287b0.description: arXiv:2611.23365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models increasingly exhibit behaviors that are difficult to detect in transcripts, such as reward hacking, deception, and sycophancy. Asking the assistant follow-up questions about its actions is unreliable, since models are generally not trained to report their own misbehavior. As a result, approaches to oversight typically involve querying external models. These face limitations: external transcript monitoring operates only on visible model outputs, and activation decoders lack full context and are prone to confabulation. We introduce introspective oversight, which trains a new role in the model to answer arbitrary questions about the assistant, rewarding answers that are verified against the assistant's actual behavior. We impleme
sb37da287b0.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a method for training language models to introspectively report on their own misbehavior, such as reward hacking or deception.
sb37da287b0.why: Explores whether models can be trained to self-report misbehavior, a potential complement to external monitoring, though the description is abstract.

s571da62993.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding
s571da62993.description: arXiv:2611.23375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are billed by the token, yet software engineering says nothing about what a token actually buys. Here we introduce a theory of software thermodynamics. The theory draws analogues from classical and stochastic thermodynamics, extends them, and applies them to modern agentic coding. We count the tokens an agent generates as its cost and divide that cost into work and heat. The test suite acts as a software Maxwell's daemon that judges every coding change. We test the theory with an analogue of the experiments in which a single molecule is pulled open and let fold again: an agent makes a change to a repository (coding) and then undoes it (uncoding), many times over, and we count the tokens of every model call. The cycle returns the
s571da62993.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a 'software thermodynamics' theory that splits the tokens a coding agent generates into work and heat, judged by the test suite.
s571da62993.why: Offers a framework for thinking about what coding agent token spend actually produces, which may inform cost measurement for agentic development.

s7b8d691960.title: HardwareDx: A Foundational Graph Model System for Datacenter Machine Repairs
s7b8d691960.description: arXiv:2611.23398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid scale-up of AI infrastructure has made datacenter reliability a cornerstone of the cloud business economy. Since hardware failures in hyper-scale AI clusters can stall multi-million dollar training workloads, the downtime of individual machines can cause outsized economic losses. Minimizing machine downtime, therefore, is more important than ever. To address this, we present Hardware Diagnoser (HardwareDx), an AI-driven hardware diagnosis system that applies a graph foundation model approach to automated datacenter maintenance. It allows a single model to diagnose many platforms and accelerate onboarding of new hardware products. Deployed at production scale at Google, HardwareDx yields substantial efficiency gains across diverse co
s7b8d691960.summary: An arXiv paper presents HardwareDx, an AI system using a graph foundation model to diagnose datacenter hardware failures and reduce machine downtime.
s7b8d691960.why: Targets costly downtime in AI clusters, relevant to infrastructure teams running large training workloads.

sd849ebb68b.title: RFBench: A Simulator-Grounded Multimodal Benchmark for Passive RF Layout Design and Understanding
sd849ebb68b.description: arXiv:2611.23410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal language models can interpret diagrams and generate structured outputs, their capacity to connect passive radio-frequency (RF) design intent, layout geometry, and electromagnetic behavior remains largely untested. To address this gap, we introduce RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark for passive RF layout design and understanding. The dataset contains 10,000 two-port planar layouts simulated using ADS Momentum, with each layout represented by editable geometric primitives, a raster image, a 16x16 occupancy grid, complex S-parameters at 201 frequency points, a structural category, and an RF response label. Building on these aligned representations, we define seven tasks spanning specification-conditioned layout
sd849ebb68b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces RFBench, a simulator-grounded dataset and benchmark of 10,000 passive RF layouts for testing multimodal models on RF design.
sd849ebb68b.why: Provides a domain benchmark for testing whether multimodal models understand RF layout and electromagnetic behavior.

s84e21402df.title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
s84e21402df.description: arXiv:2611.23445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep vision models operating in resource-constrained environments depend heavily on low-bit quantization, yet compressing weights below 4 bits frequently induces catastrophic accuracy collapse. While mixed-precision recovery strategies aim to rescue accuracy by selectively retaining high-precision parameters, the fundamental mechanics of where and why these models collapse remain poorly understood. In this study, we systematically analyze the anatomy of quantization collapse across standard Vision CNNs (including ResNet and EfficientNet backbones) evaluated on the full 50,000-image ImageNet-1k validation set. First, we map the exact progression of degradation, demonstrating that collapse is highly non-linear and concentrated in late-stage poi
s84e21402df.summary: An arXiv paper analyzes why vision CNNs collapse under sub-4-bit weight quantization and where mixed-precision recovery stops working.
s84e21402df.why: Clarifies limits of aggressive quantization for resource-constrained vision deployments, informing compression decisions.

sbccfb76873.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
sbccfb76873.description: arXiv:2611.23454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. We present LusoClin, a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, created to support privacy-preserving research on clinical text retrieval. LusoClin was generated by pre-processing real clinical data, fine-tuning the open-source Llama 3.2 (3B) instruction-tuned model using Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation, and applying prompt-based cli
sbccfb76873.summary: Researchers released LusoClin, a publicly available synthetic clinical note dataset in European Portuguese for medical information retrieval research.
sbccfb76873.why: Offers a privacy-friendly dataset for building clinical retrieval systems in a low-resource language.

s5c8a08fdfd.title: VeriMath: Human-in-the-Loop Generation and Verification of Curriculum-Aligned Mathematics Assessment Items
s5c8a08fdfd.description: arXiv:2611.23456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic generation of mathematics assessment items is a growing area in educational artificial intelligence, yet classroom deployment remains challenging. Generated questions must satisfy multiple constraints: mathematical correctness, curriculum alignment, appropriate cognitive difficulty, and educator reviewability. While prior work has advanced text generation, reliable assessment authoring requires granular control over localized examination formats and expert educational judgment. To address this challenge, we present VeriMath, a generalized, human-in-the-loop framework for generating rigorous, curriculum-constrained mathematics assessment drafts. Using annotated reference items, the framework anchors generation to the requested examin
s5c8a08fdfd.summary: An arXiv paper presents VeriMath, a human-in-the-loop system for generating and verifying curriculum-aligned mathematics assessment items.

s24648c435c.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance
s24648c435c.description: arXiv:2611.23476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous AI agents pair a frozen base model with an editable harness of prompts, skills, tool rules, and memory. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) adapts this harness from experience without weight updates, yet self-editing without external graders often backfires: reflection and scalar scores conflate what an edit newly broke with what remains unsolved, causing local regressions, skill forgetting, and memory bloat. We introduce GUARD (Grader-free Unsupervised Environment Design [UED] with Adaptive Rule Distillation), a closed-loop framework for reference-free continual harness evolution. Our key insight is to decompose each task into pre-execution self-checks and guide harness updates via directional regret. Each round grades trajectories a
s24648c435c.summary: An arXiv paper introduces GUARD, a grader-free framework to stabilize recursive self-improvement of AI agent harnesses, reducing regressions and memory bloat.
s24648c435c.why: Addresses regressions and skill forgetting when agents self-edit prompts, tools, and memory without external graders.

s6dda97006b.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Navigation Behavior of Vision-Language Model Agents Reading Emergency CT and MRI Examinations
s6dda97006b.description: arXiv:2611.23480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose. To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and image navigation behavior of vision-language model (VLM) agents under varying exploration strategies. Materials and Methods. In this retrospective study, six VLMs read 100 emergency CT and MRI examinations published in a public archive (March 2025-August 2026) under four conditions (free navigation, navigation from a key slice, and all slices or key slices in a single request), twice each (4800 runs). Nine radiologists read 30 of those cases. A large language model judge validated against two radiologists graded the answers. Conditions were compared with generalized estimating equations clustered by case. Results. Pooled accuracy was lowest under free navigation (32.6%; 391/1200), followed by n
s6dda97006b.summary: A retrospective arXiv study tested six vision-language model agents reading emergency CT and MRI exams under different navigation strategies, compared with nine radiologists.
s6dda97006b.why: Shows how exploration strategy affects VLM diagnostic accuracy in a high-stakes medical setting, a caution for deploying such agents.

s9dc2fbd8f9.title: SpecLook: Speculating Where to Look for Fast and Reliable Agentic MLLMs
s9dc2fbd8f9.description: arXiv:2611.23483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that think with images interleave reasoning with zoom-in tool calls. However, this sequential loop is slow, and its answers carry no reliability score. Prior speculation of tokens, reasoning steps, or answers keeps the loop, and answer speculation also accepts confident errors. We find that the loop mostly adds one zoom-in step, with which a small model is ahead of the agent on most splits. Our key insight is to speculate the agent's next observation, which, unlike a drafted answer, can be verified, corrected, and used to test the answer. We propose SpecLook, a training-free speculate-and-verify framework with three levels. A small model drafts a glimpse and re-answers from it, and the question
s9dc2fbd8f9.summary: An arXiv paper proposes SpecLook, which speculates an agentic multimodal model's next image observation to speed up zoom-in reasoning and add verifiability.
s9dc2fbd8f9.why: Targets latency and reliability problems in agentic image-reasoning loops, relevant to teams building multimodal agents.

sc0ed4e9a41.title: BOS Summary: The First Token Matters
sc0ed4e9a41.description: arXiv:2611.23508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) and language models (LLMs) often exhibit attention sinks, whereby particular positions, such as the beginning-of-sequence (BOS) token, receive a disproportionate share of attention. Under standard causal masking, however, the BOS query attends only to itself, so the representation that later tokens repeatedly access carries no information about the input. We introduce BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that repurposes this persistent pathway to carry input context. At a single transformer layer during prefill, BOS Summary relaxes the causal constraint for the BOS query row alone, letting BOS aggregate all visual and textual input tokens into a self-derived context representation while every
sc0ed4e9a41.summary: An arXiv paper introduces BOS Summary, a training-free inference-time method that uses the beginning-of-sequence token to carry input context in LLMs and LVLMs.
sc0ed4e9a41.why: Offers a no-training technique to make attention-sink positions carry useful input information, potentially improving inference.

sa1312471f7.title: GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design
sa1312471f7.description: arXiv:2611.23509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated agent design searches for executable architectures that improve LLM-based agent performance, with evolutionary methods using language-model crossover to recombine promising mechanisms for task decomposition, model coordination, and verification. This search, however, is typically guided by aggregate fitness alone, which hides the instance-level successes and failures behind each score. We introduce Execution Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design (GRAFT), which uses aggregate fitness for selection and survival and parent-specific execution evidence to guide semantic crossover with integrated mutation. Its feedback harness reuses bounded samples of successful and failed runs from fitness evaluation, withholding reference answe
sa1312471f7.summary: An arXiv paper presents GRAFT, an evolutionary method that uses per-instance execution results to guide recombination when automatically designing LLM agents.
sa1312471f7.why: Suggests using instance-level execution feedback rather than aggregate fitness alone when searching for better agent architectures.

s2cf26a3792.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
s2cf26a3792.description: arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-series sensing increasingly relies on neural networks, yet deployment on resource-constrained microcontrollers remains challenging. Aggressive model compression can reduce accuracy, while restricting weights to multiplication-free representations introduces further losses. We present BeFit, an end-to-end framework that shifts model capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations. BeFit (i) finds compact Bernstein-activated convolutional neural networks (BeCNNs) through hardware-aware neural architecture search and trains them via knowledge distillation; (ii) projects their weights to multiplication-free codes, freezes the codes, and recovers the resulting accuracy loss through the learnable activations; and (iii) gene
s2cf26a3792.summary: BeFit proposes shifting neural network capacity from weights to learnable Bernstein polynomial activations for time-series sensing on resource-constrained microcontrollers.
s2cf26a3792.why: It offers a path to running accurate time-series models on microcontrollers without aggressive compression or multiplication-free weight restrictions.

scce97e4917.title: FACET - Facet Aware Contrastive Embeddings for Traits- Big Five Estimation from Life Narratives
scce97e4917.description: arXiv:2611.23560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personality is only weakly and inconsistently signaled by written language, and existing text-based methods typically combine language-model and psycholinguistic representations at the input or decision level. It remains open whether a more deliberate combination of the two views, and a decomposition of the prediction target, can recover more of the signal. We present a three-phase framework for estimating Big Five personality domain scores from life-narrative interview text. It encodes text and psycholinguistic features separately and combines them by concatenation or by a learned weighting, decomposes each domain into contrastively trained facet embeddings instead of predicting the domain directly, and pools the facet embeddings by attentio
scce97e4917.summary: FACET is a three-phase framework that combines language-model and psycholinguistic features to estimate Big Five personality scores from life-narrative interview text.

s04c157b96f.title: LProp: Propagating Latent Uncertainty through Evidence-Conditioned Belief Revision in LLM Agents
s04c157b96f.description: arXiv:2611.23564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When LLM agents pass intermediate judgments downstream without uncertainty, later decisions may treat tentative assumptions as facts. Effective uncertainty propagation must preserve information for correction and update inherited beliefs as new evidence arrives. Yet scalar scores omit information needed for revision, while detailed descriptions and reflection incur additional costs. We introduce Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator that preserves uncertainty-relevant information without lengthy descriptions. Building on this, we propose LProp (Latent Uncertainty Propagation), which revises inherited answer distributions using latent representations and new evidence without additional trajectory sampling. We evaluate both methods acros
s04c157b96f.summary: LProp introduces Latent Uncertainty, a latent-space estimator meant to propagate uncertainty between LLM agents so tentative judgments are not treated as facts downstream.
s04c157b96f.why: Multi-agent pipelines can carry unverified assumptions forward as facts, so preserving uncertainty across handoffs targets a real reliability problem.

scb7adb9abc.title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance
scb7adb9abc.description: arXiv:2611.23572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. Such guidance must connect eligibility requirements, practical access constraints, and dietary needs rather than return isolated listings or generic nutritional advice. Multi-agent food assistants can coordinate these tasks, with uncertainty indicating when clarification or verification is needed before a recommendation. However, uncertainty can be lost across agent handoffs, allowing tentative interpretations to propagate as facts and obscuring opportunities for correction. Moreover, confidence that a service requirement has been interpreted correctly is not confidence that a recommend
scb7adb9abc.summary: The paper presents a receiver-conditioned clarification approach for multi-agent food assistants, aiming to keep uncertainty from being lost across agent handoffs.
scb7adb9abc.why: Uncertainty lost across agent handoffs can lead to tentative assumptions becoming recommendations, a general multi-agent design concern.

s4982f2beba.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents
s4982f2beba.description: arXiv:2611.23588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise LLM agents operate in dynamic environments where foundation models evolve rapidly, workflows update frequently, and deployments need to satisfy accuracy and cost requirements. We propose ARISE (Agent Refinement through Iterative Self-Evaluation), a practical memory architecture in which the agent's memory evolves from its own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflow logic. ARISE uses the model itself or a teacher model to attribute the failures and propose corrections. Then, ARISE keeps the corrections as retrievable micro memory, consolidates them into macro rules, and accepts a rule update only if held-out accuracy rises. Across 14 enterprise-workflow domains from SOP-Bench and $\tau^2$-bench using 5 models, AR
s4982f2beba.summary: ARISE is a memory architecture where enterprise LLM agents learn corrections from their own failures, stored as retrievable memory, without updating model weights, tools, or workflows.
s4982f2beba.why: It suggests improving enterprise agent accuracy and cost without retraining models or changing workflow logic, which matters for teams with frequent model and workflow changes.

s0d6d6ad6fc.title: RefinementGuard: Counterexample-Directed Semantic Qualification for Hidden Agent-Tool Execution
s0d6d6ad6fc.description: arXiv:2611.23611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool runtimes can lower an agent-selected operation into a hidden parallel graph, reducing latency and context while risking semantic mistranslation. We introduce RefinementGuard: translation validation for hidden, effectful agent-tool lowerings, coupled to artifact-bound, fail-closed runtime admission. Qualification compares a candidate graph with an independent reference on isolated state using explicit parent-operation obligations. We evaluate two repository-level contracts, bug localization and patch validation, on controlled repositories. Among 100 activated, non-equivalent development/qualification faults adjudicated by one human, parent-semantic validation rejects 49/100 (operator-cluster bootstrap 95% CI [33.7%, 64.8%]). The objective
s0d6d6ad6fc.summary: RefinementGuard applies translation validation to hidden parallel graphs that tool runtimes create when lowering agent-selected operations, with fail-closed runtime admission.
s0d6d6ad6fc.why: Tool runtimes that silently rewrite agent operations into hidden graphs can mistranslate semantics, so validating them before execution addresses a safety gap for agent tooling.

sc48f903c29.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
sc48f903c29.description: arXiv:2611.23639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. We investigate whether the latter provides an adaptive alternative to FM-based scientific retrieval. We evaluate this approach on a galaxy retrieval task spanning diverse modalities--history of star formation, spectra of light emitted, and multi-wavelength observations from two telescopes--comparing an FM baseline with separately trained embeddings fused through multi-objective optimization based on Pareto optima
sc48f903c29.summary: The paper investigates late fusion of independently learned modality embeddings as an alternative to multimodal foundation models for galaxy retrieval across uneven cosmology survey data.

s4dcdc96330.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
s4dcdc96330.description: arXiv:2611.23678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and prov
s4dcdc96330.summary: The paper proposes evaluating autonomous ML experimentation agents on their process, including file-scope compliance, retained failed trials, and decision provenance, using a governed harness.
s4dcdc96330.why: Judging agents only by best score hides whether they stayed within permissions and kept failed trials, so process metrics matter for auditing agent-run experiments.

s81f7397512.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
s81f7397512.description: arXiv:2611.23700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinicians reviewing a diagnostic work-up will ask what was considered at each step and why the assessment changed. Agents powered by free text can reach physician-level diagnostic accuracy, but their written reasoning does not always reflect the factors that went into the decision. Here, we present Decision2Care, a decision agent that works up the acutely ill patient without producing any text. A decision model assigns a probability to each permitted EHR action, and fixed rules carry out the most probable one. We evaluated Decision2Care on the records of 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases. Decision2Care reached a diagnostic accuracy of 86.5%, compared with 86.1% for the MIRA-v2 agent, and required a median of 2.2 s per work-up, comp
s81f7397512.summary: Decision2Care is a clinical decision agent that picks EHR actions via a probability model and fixed rules, producing no free text, and was evaluated on acutely ill patient work-ups.
s81f7397512.why: Replacing free-text reasoning with auditable action probabilities addresses traceability concerns for agents in clinical settings.

s64c2a355e9.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
s64c2a355e9.description: arXiv:2611.23702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. By exposing each score component and its supporting sources, KnowMe helps readers select promising papers for their current questions and discover relevant work beyond familiar authors. Automatic acquisition, version merging and graph-cache reuse keep
s64c2a355e9.summary: KnowMe Paper Radar is a lightweight tool that ranks papers for personalized reading using topical relevance, recency, author histories, and exposed score components.

sebcc9f35bc.title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
sebcc9f35bc.description: arXiv:2611.23749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model reasoning alternates between sustained activities and local operations. We study how this temporal structure predicts continuation and the computation needed to analyze it. T/E/S combines text, local events, and spans of activity. Across reasoning and information-seeking tasks, events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in 70 of 76 evaluation groups for a Transformer and 74 of 76 for Qwen with LoRA. Span duration and preceding events are associated with transitions, and retaining event history across span boundaries improves prediction. We formulate budget-allocation counting and action-conditional continuation queries, prove counting hardness under explicit encodings, and derive conditions for affordable decision certifi
sebcc9f35bc.summary: The paper introduces T/E/S, a structural representation combining text, local events, and activity spans, which improves next-outcome prediction of LLM reasoning in most tested groups.
sebcc9f35bc.why: Modeling reasoning structure could help predict LLM reasoning continuations, which is useful for engineers analyzing model behavior, though gains are research-stage.

sd447126fcb.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
sd447126fcb.description: arXiv:2611.23751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers to construct Any-DP, and trains a single cali
sd447126fcb.summary: AnyS1 turns human-authored procedural skills into domain-general decision points so a lightweight System-1 model can handle choices instead of a large model at every agent step.
sd447126fcb.why: Routing routine agent decisions to a smaller model could cut cost and latency across agent workflows without workflow-specific integration hooks.

s5eca248851.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents
s5eca248851.description: arXiv:2611.23810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal agents largely rely on generic tools such as cropping, search, and code execution, leaving specialist vision models outside their tool space. However, bringing such a model into an already trained agent is not straightforward. The challenge is to learn each new tool efficiently while retaining the ability to use existing ones. This work proposes COTEX, continual tool-space extension learning, that adds new tools at efficient adapter-level cost. COTEX locates two sets of parameter directions; one triggers a tool call and thereby opens a multi-turn reasoning trajectory, while the other determines which tool is chosen. The adapter of a new tool is restricted to the calling directions that leave earlier tool choices unaffected by ortho
s5eca248851.summary: COTEX proposes continual tool-space extension, adding specialist vision models as new tools to trained multimodal agents at adapter-level cost while retaining existing tools.
s5eca248851.why: Adding new tools to an already trained agent without losing existing capabilities is a practical concern for teams extending multimodal agent systems.

s7abc015cee.title: Metrics-in-the-Loop: Complexity Feedback Reshapes Agent-Written Code
s7abc015cee.description: arXiv:2611.23817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents now write whole codebases in long autonomous runs, guided mainly by whether their tests pass. Yet passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity or gaps in test coverage, which then persist as agents extend their own code. We introduce metrics-in-the-loop, an inference-time intervention that gives agents in-flight feedback: cheap, automatically computed code metrics injected into the agent's context during the trajectory. After each code-changing agent turn, we insert short feedback messages naming changed functions whose cyclomatic complexity exceeds a limit (complexity feedback) or changed lines that are skipped by tests (coverage feedback), giving the agent the opportunity to refactor code or strengthen tests bef
s7abc015cee.summary: The paper introduces metrics-in-the-loop, which injects automatically computed code complexity and coverage metrics into coding agents' context during autonomous runs to shape the code they write.
s7abc015cee.why: Passing tests alone does not reveal accumulating complexity, so in-flight code metrics offer a practical way to steer long autonomous coding runs.

sbbdb3cd067.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
sbbdb3cd067.description: arXiv:2611.23824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. This limitation is especially severe when all sampled rollouts for a question fail, collapsing group-centered outcome advantages to zero even when trajectories gather markedly different evidence. We present Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), which augments terminal outcome rewards with a training-only auxiliary signal measuring how retrieved documents improve the likelihood of a reference answer. Rather than scoring the full dialogue prefix, EC
sbbdb3cd067.summary: Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA) assigns credit to individual searches in search-augmented LM reinforcement learning based on the evidence each retrieved, rather than uniformly across trajectories.
sbbdb3cd067.why: Outcome-only rewards give identical credit to every search and collapse to zero when all rollouts fail, so evidence-aware credit could improve training of retrieval-augmented models.

sf85b04bdd7.title: A System 1 Decision Model for Medical Multiple-Choice Questions Built on Frozen Language Models
sf85b04bdd7.description: arXiv:2611.23832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A System 1 model answers a multiple-choice question in a single pass. A frozen language model turns the question and each option into vectors, two small, trained heads place them in a shared space, and the closest option wins. The design has been shown on agent decisions, but we are not aware of a study of how far it goes on exam questions that need medical knowledge, where the right option is often no more similar to the question than the wrong ones. We rebuilt the recipe from scratch for MedMCQA and trained only two projection heads and one temperature on top of frozen Qwen3.5-0.8B, Granite-4.2-3B and Qwen3-8B, using a contrastive loss with in-batch and hard negatives and a mask for repeated answers. With plain last-token vectors, both smal
sf85b04bdd7.summary: Researchers rebuilt a single-pass System 1 decision model on frozen language models and tested it on MedMCQA medical exam questions, training only two projection heads and a temperature parameter.
sf85b04bdd7.why: It tests whether cheap, single-pass embedding-based answer selection can handle knowledge-heavy medical questions, relevant to building low-cost medical QA systems.

sa98e0642db.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
sa98e0642db.description: arXiv:2611.23855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can AI agents design robots that work in the real world? We introduce RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course. Simulation alone is not enough: under public part data, none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course, so an agent learns the simulator from measurements it requests and videos of real runs. Across four frontier coding agents, ten obstacles at three difficulty levels, 16,427 simulations of 12,774 distinct robots and 135 physical robots built in an estimated 240 hours, agents solve nearly all easy obstacles and invent mechanisms our s
sa98e0642db.summary: RoboBuilder is a benchmark where coding agents co-design robot hardware and software, with designs passing simulation also tested on a physical course.
sa98e0642db.why: It shows simulation alone missed real-world failures, so agent-driven hardware design needs physical feedback loops to be trustworthy.

s6d5ce1eaa9.title: Asking but Missing: Decision Coverage in Natural-Language Data Querying
s6d5ce1eaa9.description: arXiv:2611.23864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to translate natural language questions about structured data into executable programs. A fundamental challenge is recognizing when a question admits multiple computational interpretations and identifying the decisions needed to resolve them. We investigate whether language models recognize these unresolved decisions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions that may lead to incorrect results. We refer to the latter behavior as Underspecified Decision Completion (UDC). To distinguish different causes of UDC, we introduce Grounded Code Generation (GCG), a diagnostic protocol that separates the identification of unresolved decisions, their resolution using evidence, and their translation i
s6d5ce1eaa9.summary: The paper studies whether language models recognize unresolved decisions in natural-language data questions before generating code, or silently adopt assumptions, a behavior it calls Underspecified Decision Completion.
s6d5ce1eaa9.why: Silent assumptions in text-to-query code can yield plausible but wrong results, a risk for teams deploying LLM data querying tools.

sece56c6b4b.title: Risk-Controlled Correction for Frozen Multimodal Models under Missing Modalities
sece56c6b4b.description: arXiv:2611.23886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A deployed multimodal predictor may face missing modalities after its weights can no longer be changed. This raises a question that training-time repair does not answer: what part of the resulting error is still correctable from the information that remains? We show that this part is characterized by the Bayes gap, the difference between the model's prediction and the Bayes prediction given the observed modalities. For cross-entropy and squared error, excess risk measures this gap in the geometry of the loss; ambiguity in the observed modalities cannot be removed. Thus, a badly degraded prediction is not necessarily a correctable one. Estimating the Bayes prediction normally requires labels. However, when a model observing more modalities is
sece56c6b4b.summary: The paper characterizes how much error a frozen multimodal model can still correct when modalities are missing, using a Bayes gap measured by excess risk.
sece56c6b4b.why: Engineers deploying fixed multimodal models can use this framing to estimate which errors remain correctable when inputs are missing at inference.

sa80e309f04.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality
sa80e309f04.description: arXiv:2611.23890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video evaluators play an important role in video generation, yet they miss motion defects, limiting the quality of generated videos. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has made strong progress in mathematics and coding, where explicit verifiers provide reliable feedback on a single goal. Video evaluation poses two difficulties for RSI: it has no verifier, and it must judge many dimensions at once, such as physics, smoothness and dynamics, where a gain on one can cost another. We introduce EVA-RSI, a multi-agent framework for exploring RSI under these two constraints. We build a fixed proxy exam with construction-defined targets by applying controlled changes to videos, such as temporal reversal and frame dropping. These edits supply supervision
sa80e309f04.summary: EVA-RSI is a multi-agent framework that applies recursive self-improvement to video evaluators so they can judge multiple temporal quality dimensions without an explicit verifier.
sa80e309f04.why: Better automated video judges could improve filtering and evaluation of generated video, though the text gives limited detail on results.
