sdaaae59d27.description: arXiv:2611.24005v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning constructs rewards for aligning large language models with human preferences, typically by equally aggregating continuous scores that a judge assigns to individual criteria. However, scoring heterogeneity across criteria can distort candidate rankings. Existing work has focused on improving judges, learning criterion weights, or refining aggregation, whereas the interaction between scoring heterogeneity and ranking remains insufficiently understood. We formalize this heterogeneity as \emph{reward gain imbalance}: each criterion enters the aggregated reward with its own reward gain, the gap between its expected scores on satisfied and unsatisfied responses. Counterintuitively, our experiments show that rem
sdaaae59d27.summary: Researchers formalize reward gain imbalance in rubric-based reinforcement learning, showing how uneven criterion scoring heterogeneity can distort candidate rankings for LLM alignment.
sdaaae59d27.why: Equal aggregation of rubric scores can silently skew rankings in RL alignment pipelines, so reward design choices affect outcomes.

s26c2dc6940.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
s26c2dc6940.description: arXiv:2611.24025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a re
s26c2dc6940.summary: Researchers propose intent contracts, an authorization design where the planning LLM holds no tools and a trusted model writes each tool call after checking a logged contract.
s26c2dc6940.why: Offers a concrete pattern for limiting what tool-using agents can do, with logged, validated authorization before any action runs.

s23cb1a516f.title: FormalFixer: Intent-Aligned Automated Hardware Repair via Joint Refinement of Specifications, Assertions, and RTL Implementations
s23cb1a516f.description: arXiv:2611.24037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Functional errors in hardware designs can compromise correctness and security, and must be fixed before tape-out. Formal property verification (FPV) provides strong guarantees by proving or refuting assertions, but a failed assertion is not always evidence of an RTL defect: the failure may also come from a buggy assertion or from a specification that is semantically correct but too ambiguous or incomplete for direct formalization. This creates a practical repair problem that existing RTL-centric methods do not directly address: the repair loop must align specification intent, verification intent, and RTL behavior before deciding which artifact to change. \textsc{FormalFixer} addresses this problem with a multi-stage, intent-aligned repair w
s23cb1a516f.summary: FormalFixer proposes a method that jointly refines specifications, assertions, and RTL code to repair hardware designs when formal verification assertions fail.
s23cb1a516f.why: Addresses that failed assertions may stem from buggy assertions or ambiguous specs, not only RTL defects, which matters for pre-tape-out verification workflows.

sbba080784a.title: From Data to Valves: A Self-Learning, Production-Grade Edge Stack for Sustainable HVAC Control
sbba080784a.description: arXiv:2611.24052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned HVAC controllers rarely leave the simulator, and those that do are typically trained offline, frozen at deployment and retrained from the cloud. We present a production stack in which three learning components run on one NVIDIA Jetson Orin gateway per building, adapt continuously from the building's own data, and verify their own effect. (a) A compact transformer-encoder forecaster, one per equipment group with learned per-unit embeddings, predicts every air-side unit's next-cycle temperature and learns prequentially, one gradient step per five-minute cycle, behind five independent gates that bound the influence of any corrupt reading. (b) A distributional soft actor-critic agent, one shared policy across unit types, converts the me
sbba080784a.summary: Researchers describe a production HVAC control stack where learning components run on an edge gateway per building, adapting continuously from local data and verifying their own effect.
sbba080784a.why: Shows a deployed pattern for on-premise, continuously adapting learned controllers on edge hardware instead of cloud-retrained frozen models.

sd2a9d714a3.title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status
sd2a9d714a3.description: arXiv:2611.24055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. The programs are usually graded against answers written by someone who read the same law, so a program can score well by sharing the grader's reading rather than by getting the law right. LexTemporis grades them instead against records of what actually happened: 10,901 firm-years of SME status disclosed by Korean listed companies, with every version of the governing rules. An appendix adds comparison cases from US income tax and German hospital minimum volumes. The date changes outcomes mainly through provisions outside the main statutory text: one trans
sd2a9d714a3.summary: LexTemporis grades executable legal rules against real records of Korean listed firms' SME status rather than against answers written by someone reading the same law.
sd2a9d714a3.why: Suggests validating LLM-generated rule programs against ground-truth records rather than reviewer interpretations, a useful evaluation approach for compliance logic.

s460d6bf61b.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
s460d6bf61b.description: arXiv:2611.24059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed
s460d6bf61b.summary: Researchers propose replaying stored RL rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards to consolidate domain experts, instead of resampling in multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
s460d6bf61b.why: Could cut the cost of consolidating post-training experts into one model by reusing rollouts the experts already produced.

s172f56aa72.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
s172f56aa72.description: arXiv:2611.24077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision.
s172f56aa72.summary: AeroRSI is a recursive self-improvement framework where an aerial vision-language navigation policy learns from its own failures in closed-loop flight.
s172f56aa72.why: Presents a way to generate repair data for drone VLA policies without relying on human pilot labels or rule-based planners.

s93804be1e8.title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
s93804be1e8.description: arXiv:2611.24079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting
s93804be1e8.summary: APS proposes adaptive partitioning for frame selection to improve long video understanding in large vision-language models under computational budgets.
s93804be1e8.why: Offers a method to reduce visual input cost for long-video LVLM pipelines by choosing frames over adaptive temporal regions.

sd8af7bf496.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
sd8af7bf496.description: arXiv:2611.24085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating distributed large language model (LLM) serving on heterogeneous edge devices requires exploring diverse model partitions, device placements, and network conditions, making repeated physical experiments costly. An efficient simulator for edge LLM serving must support diverse, fine-grained placement configurations, capture runtime behavior, and accurately predict execution times while keeping simulation overhead low. We present LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for fast, fine-grained evaluation of distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices without executing tensor operations. LEDGE constructs event graphs supporting non-uniform tensor and pipeline parallelism, estimates execution costs using reusable performance models cali
sd8af7bf496.summary: LEDGE is a lightweight simulator for evaluating distributed LLM serving across heterogeneous edge devices, covering model partitions, device placement, and network conditions.
sd8af7bf496.why: Lets teams explore edge LLM deployment configurations without costly physical experiments, though the text gives no performance results.

s1327220237.title: The 7th International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026): Summary and Results
s1327220237.description: arXiv:2611.24114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This report summarizes the seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Com- petition (VNN-COMP 2026), held as part of the Symposium on AI Verification (SAIV) co-located with the International Conference on Computer-Aided Verification (CAV) at FLoC 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. The goal of the competition is to provide an objective comparison of the state-of-the-art methods in neural network verification, in terms of scal- ability and speed. Along this line, we used standard formats (ONNX for neural networks and VNNLIB for specifications), standard hardware (all tools are run by the organizers on AWS), and tool parameters provided by the tool authors. This report summarizes the rules, benchmarks, participating tools, results, and lesso
s1327220237.summary: The seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026) summarized its results, comparing neural network verification methods on scalability and speed.
s1327220237.why: Provides an objective benchmark snapshot of which neural network verification tools currently scale best.

sdbfe58cf56.title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
sdbfe58cf56.description: arXiv:2611.24122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. This retrospective study evaluated two generalist models, RADAR and Merlin, for differentiating liver tumors using a public single-institution multiphase CT dataset (517 cases: hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, breast and colorectal cancer liver metastases, and hemangioma). The models were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using their existing outputs and with linear probing, in which only a linear classifier was trained on frozen image features (stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated five times). In the zero-shot setting, RADAR achieved an accuracy of 54.
sdbfe58cf56.summary: A retrospective study evaluated generalist CT foundation models RADAR and Merlin on differentiating liver tumors across 517 multiphase CT cases.
sdbfe58cf56.why: Shows generalist medical imaging models may detect lesions well but are not established as reliable at differentiating tumor types.

sc6c8f45692.title: Inherited Adapter Experts for Replay-Free Domain-Incremental Learning
sc6c8f45692.description: arXiv:2611.24145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replay-free domain-incremental learning trains a model on the same classes in successive domains without keeping earlier images. Per-domain learners freeze a pre-trained ViT and train an additional expert for each new domain: the small set of parameters and the classification head learned on that domain. Test images carry no domain label, so a router selects one expert for each image. Recent work trains this router. However, a training-free Mahalanobis router costs the analyzed learners under 2.7 points of final accuracy relative to always selecting each image's own-domain expert. The experts, not this router, limit accuracy. Our learner, Lamarck, therefore uses this router and strengthens the experts. Its adapters, small trainable layers t
sc6c8f45692.summary: Researchers study replay-free domain-incremental learning with adapter experts and a training-free Mahalanobis router that selects an expert per image without domain labels.
sc6c8f45692.why: Shows a training-free routing option for continual learning that trades a small amount of accuracy for simpler deployment.

sf4db0dde45.title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
sf4db0dde45.description: arXiv:2611.24156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to create stories for children. Since bedtime stories can shape children's perceptions of social roles, this raises concerns about whether LLMs adapt narrative portrayals according to the intended recipient's gender. We conducted a large-scale study to examine gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories. Using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design, we analyze 62,873 retained stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles. We introduce a multi-level evaluation framework combining context-adjusted lexical rate contrasts, relative stereotype alignment, narrator-recipient interaction analysis, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions
sf4db0dde45.summary: A large-scale study of 62,873 LLM-generated bedtime stories from 16 models finds analysis of gender stereotyping tied to whether the intended recipient is a daughter or son.
sf4db0dde45.why: Highlights measurable gender bias in LLM content for children, relevant to teams shipping generative storytelling or education products.

se4df014173.title: Gaussian Primitive Fusion for Any-Resolution Multimodal Images
se4df014173.description: arXiv:2611.24164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal image fusion integrates complementary observations from different modalities into a unified representation. Existing methods typically estimate modality contributions on a common discrete grid. When source modalities have different native resolutions, constructing such a grid generally involves resampling, which may introduce artifacts and affect subsequent fusion decisions. To address this problem, we propose Gaussian Primitive Fusion (GPF), which reformulates heterogeneous-resolution fusion in a shared continuous Gaussian space. Instead of first converting source images to a common resolution, GPF directly fits their native-resolution observations with shared Gaussian geometry and modality-specific content representations, and
se4df014173.summary: Gaussian Primitive Fusion proposes fusing multimodal images of different native resolutions in a shared continuous Gaussian space instead of resampling to a common grid.
se4df014173.why: Avoids resampling artifacts in heterogeneous-resolution sensor fusion, though the text gives no quantitative results.

sd9a8e9288a.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
sd9a8e9288a.description: arXiv:2611.24168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act
sd9a8e9288a.summary: CounselTraj proposes synthesizing session-level psychological counseling dialogues by planning dialogue-act trajectories, as an alternative to privacy-limited real transcripts.
sd9a8e9288a.why: Offers a privacy-friendly route to session-length training data for counseling systems, though the text gives little on outcomes.

s51a395df86.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
s51a395df86.description: arXiv:2611.24184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate opportunities for interaction into better understanding. We introduce VideoACE, a benchmark for assessing video understanding under conditions that support sustained interaction. We focus on high-frame-rate action videos, where rapid, subtle changes make targeted observation especially valuable. The benchmark comprises 1,000 multiple-choice questions spanning six categories of fine-grained action understanding, accompanied by temporal evidence annotations and user hints screened for answer leakage. Its evaluation environment combin
s51a395df86.summary: VideoACE is a benchmark of 1,000 multiple-choice questions on high-frame-rate action videos for assessing agentic video understanding through sustained interaction.
s51a395df86.why: Gives teams a benchmark for testing whether video agents can turn interaction opportunities into better understanding.

sbd8b61bd4b.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
sbd8b61bd4b.description: arXiv:2611.24187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets
sbd8b61bd4b.summary: Researchers propose a constrained world-model planning method for visual inspection that localizes multiple targets under strict compute and sensing limits.
sbd8b61bd4b.why: Offers a planning approach for robots using frozen detectors under compute and sensing caps, relevant to field robotics teams.

s235113771a.title: SpiderMark: Hybrid Watermarking for Generative AI via Algorithmic Injection and Learning-Based Verification
s235113771a.description: arXiv:2611.24200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has intensified the need for reliable methods to trace and verify the provenance of AI-generated images. Existing watermarking approaches for diffusion models typically rely on isotropic frequency patterns and handcrafted detection metrics, which are prone to directional vulnerability and threshold instability across diverse image transformations. We propose SpiderMark, a hybrid watermarking framework that combines algorithmic frequency-domain injection with learning-based probabilistic verification, requiring no modifications to pretrained diffusion model weights. SpiderMark embeds a structured spider-web pattern, comprising radial spokes and concentric polygonal rings, into the Fourie
s235113771a.summary: SpiderMark is a hybrid watermarking framework for diffusion-generated images that combines frequency-domain injection with learning-based verification.
s235113771a.why: Provides a provenance-tracing method for generated images that aims to be more robust to transformations than handcrafted approaches.

sad08873ba1.title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
sad08873ba1.description: arXiv:2611.24208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy-saving mechanisms in RANs must balance energy reduction and network performance under varying traffic conditions. Conditional generative models support what-if analysis by generating plausible power-consumption trajectories for radio configurations and operating scenarios, helping operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment. However, representative measurements are costly and operationally constrained, so historical data cover only limited configurations and conditions, leaving some contexts poorly represented or unseen during training. In this paper, we study conditional generation of RAN power-consumption trajectories under decreasing training coverage, from well-represented to rare and unseen configurations. We fir
sad08873ba1.summary: Researchers present conditional generative models for what-if analysis of radio access network energy consumption in rare and unseen operating contexts.
sad08873ba1.why: Shows how generative models could help telecom operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment when measurement data is sparse.

sb83a37376b.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
sb83a37376b.description: arXiv:2611.24214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few eva
sb83a37376b.summary: A study examines whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style tabular foundation models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and real-world datasets.
sb83a37376b.why: Highlights that synthetic pretraining may make scaling predictions for tabular models unreliable, which matters when planning compute spend.

sb7a81c659a.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
sb7a81c659a.description: arXiv:2611.24231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-b
sb7a81c659a.summary: Researchers test which prompt injection attacks survive when untrusted documents are rendered as page images instead of text, across six multimodal models.
sb7a81c659a.why: Shows image rendering reduces some injection risks but not all, informing how teams secure document-QA pipelines.

s4d8e50dff2.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
s4d8e50dff2.description: arXiv:2611.24313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents, and the community now agrees that robustness must be measured against adaptive attackers rather than fixed benchmark injections. Many adaptive red teamers exist, and most are built to maximize attack success rate (ASR). Yet ASR counts how often a target breaks, not in how many different ways. A red teamer can achieve a high ASR by reusing a few techniques that work, leaving the others untested and absent from the attacks used to harden models. We present AutoPI, an adaptive red teamer designed to find many different ways to break a target, not just to break it often. AutoPI uses PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt-injection techniques, both to guide its search and to measure
s4d8e50dff2.summary: AutoPI is an adaptive red-teaming method for LLM agents that uses a attack taxonomy to test prompt injection across many distinct techniques, not just high success rates.
s4d8e50dff2.why: Gives security teams a way to test agents against a wider variety of injection techniques rather than a few effective ones.

s1ab7165b25.title: Fuse to Recognize the Unseen: Class-Relative Infrared-Visible Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
s1ab7165b25.description: arXiv:2611.24316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visible-infrared image fusion leverages complementary thermal cues to enhance visual perception, particularly under challenging illumination. However, such perceptual complementarity does not readily translate into semantic gains in open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS), where CLIP-based models are predominantly pretrained on RGB imagery. Directly introducing IR information may instead disrupt RGB-language alignment, turning promising thermal cues into semantic interference that undermines unseen-class recognition. Our pixel-level RGB-IR semantic analysis reveals that class-relevant thermal cues can correct certain RGB misclassifications while preserving reliable RGB predictions, motivating RGB-anchored, class-relative thermal cue se
s1ab7165b25.summary: Researchers propose a pixel-level RGB-infrared fusion method to improve open-vocabulary semantic segmentation without disrupting CLIP's RGB-language alignment.
s1ab7165b25.why: Suggests a way to add thermal input to CLIP-based segmentation without losing unseen-class recognition.

s6bcdc8c756.title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
s6bcdc8c756.description: arXiv:2611.24330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate whether a weight edit can alter how a model trades off honoring a commitment against benefiting more people. In a concept-supervised text model, we alter fitted choice weights so that the benefit required to override a formal pledge is larger than for an ordinary promise. Across six independently trained text readers, the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts. It preserves the source model's success rates on smaller conflicts and its factual accuracy. The remaining formal-conflict failures coincide with errors reading a beneficiary number. A separate classifier demonstrates why this distinction matters: reusing a factual answer passes an unco
s6bcdc8c756.summary: Researchers show a weight edit in a concept-supervised text model can change how it trades off honoring a formal pledge against benefiting more people.
s6bcdc8c756.why: Demonstrates that model-level ethical trade-offs can be altered by weight edits, a concern for alignment and auditing.

sa48f07ba41.title: OCTR2A: Real-Time RGB-to-BEV Trajectory Projection and Forecasting at Urban Intersections
sa48f07ba41.description: arXiv:2611.24352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trajectory forecasting at urban intersections is often studied assuming that reliable bird's-eye-view (BEV) motion histories are available, which in practice requires costly resources such as LiDAR, aerial views, HD maps, or calibrated infrastructure. We address this upstream perception-to-forecasting problem by reconstructing and predicting agents' BEV trajectories only from paired opposite-corner RGB cameras mounted on existing urban infrastructure at variable heights at inference time. We introduce the Opposite-Corner Trajectory Reconstruction and Anticipation Architecture (OCTR2A), a modular pipeline integrating per-view detection with class refinement, geometric cross-camera matching, transformer-based BEV projection, and egocentric GR
sa48f07ba41.summary: OCTR2A reconstructs and forecasts bird's-eye-view trajectories at urban intersections using only paired opposite-corner RGB cameras in real time.
sa48f07ba41.why: Shows trajectory forecasting may be possible with existing camera infrastructure instead of costly LiDAR or HD maps.

saa2996a8f6.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models
saa2996a8f6.description: arXiv:2611.24360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action (VLA) model on a few dozen demonstrations is the standard way to put a manipulation policy on a robot, yet the resulting policy silently assumes that the camera and the robot base stay exactly where they were during data collection: a bumped tripod or a base re-docked a few centimetres away makes it reach for the wrong place. We show that both failures are one phenomenon, a change of the camera-to-base extrinsic that the policy has memorised, and that the robot carries everything needed to undo it. We introduce WACO, a world-anchored canonicalization framework for VLA models: the arm, placed by forward kinematics at the measured joint angles, serves as a metric calibration target, and the static scene se
saa2996a8f6.summary: Researchers propose a method to make few-shot vision-language-action robot policies robust to shifts in camera-to-base extrinsics after fine-tuning.
saa2996a8f6.why: Addresses a practical failure mode where bumped cameras or re-docked robot bases break learned manipulation policies.

s054e4816bd.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data
s054e4816bd.description: arXiv:2611.24377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (MFBO) reduces engineering design cost by combining inexpensive low-fidelity (LF) models with a few accurate high-fidelity (HF) evaluations and sequentially selecting designs to evaluate. However, when HF data are scarce, the LF-HF discrepancy is difficult to learn from numerical data alone, especially when physics omitted in the LF model makes it design-dependent. Yet even without sufficient data, domain experts often know which physics the LF model omits and under which conditions its effect grows. Existing multi-fidelity (MF) models cannot use such qualitative knowledge directly, but large language models (LLMs) can interpret it and compare designs accordingly. The proposed LLM-Assisted MFBO adds a kn
s054e4816bd.summary: A paper proposes using LLMs to incorporate expert knowledge into multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization when high-fidelity data is scarce.
s054e4816bd.why: Offers a way to use domain expertise to reduce costly simulation runs in engineering design when data is limited.

s6dd5ad536c.title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
s6dd5ad536c.description: arXiv:2611.24384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subse
s6dd5ad536c.summary: A framework uses YOLO-World feature clustering and objectness scores to select a better initial labeled pool for active object detection.
s6dd5ad536c.why: Reduces labeling cost in object detection projects with small budgets by improving the first active learning cycle.

sdebe89d18f.title: Temporal Rank in Recurrent Neural Networks
sdebe89d18f.description: arXiv:2611.24394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are a natural framework for temporal modelling, yet are often dismissed due to their sequential, non-parallelisable computation and difficulty in capturing long-range dependencies, typically attributed to vanishing and exploding gradients. We identify a distinct and under-explored limitation: an information bottleneck induced by rank-constrained hidden state dynamics, which limits the number of independent input directions that can be preserved over time, as reflected in the rank of the input-to-state mapping. We show that this constraint restricts temporal capacity independently of gradient stability. To address this, we introduce structured high-dimensional state dynamics that preserve temporal separabilit
sdebe89d18f.summary: Researchers identify a rank-constrained information bottleneck in RNN hidden state dynamics that limits preservation of input directions over time.
sdebe89d18f.why: Points to an architectural limit on RNN memory that is distinct from vanishing gradients, relevant to sequence model design.

s2012d3951f.title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
s2012d3951f.description: arXiv:2611.24413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods handle policy mismatch through products of per-step trace coefficients, leading to a trade-off between variance control and long-horizon signal. The maximum trace length consequently becomes a sensitive hyperparameter. We propose MINT (Meeting-time INdicators for Truncation), which replaces these products with a binary stopping indicator: one until coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet, zero thereafter. At the true value function, the indicator's idempotence yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival. For practical implementation, a single sampled action provides a model-free surrogate for the stopping rule, requiring no transition model or mixing-time estim
s2012d3951f.summary: MINT replaces products of trace coefficients in multi-step off-policy RL with a binary meeting-time stopping indicator to control variance.
s2012d3951f.why: Could reduce sensitivity to trace-length hyperparameters in off-policy reinforcement learning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

s082a18620a.title: Keeping Shielded Data-Driven Controllers Safe Under System Evolution via Model Consistency
s082a18620a.description: arXiv:2611.24428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cyber-physical systems (CPS) increasingly contain data-driven controllers, which raise safety concerns given their black-box nature. A common mitigation is to enforce system safety via a shield around the controller, which restricts the inputs based on assumptions about the physical system. However, these assumptions are usually fixed and may become invalid as the system evolves (during development or due to component degradation), possibly leading to unsafe behavior. We address this limitation in a model-driven approach that treats both the data-driven controller and safety shield as first-class models that are integrated into a virtual single underlying model (V-SUM) alongside system models. We describe system evolution as changes in the
s082a18620a.summary: A model-driven approach keeps shielded data-driven controllers safe as system assumptions change during development or component degradation.
s082a18620a.why: Addresses how safety shields can become invalid as cyber-physical systems evolve, a concern for deployed control systems.

s0e3c7b6503.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs
s0e3c7b6503.description: arXiv:2611.24431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about long interleaved inputs, such as documents of many pages and collections of hundreds of images, but they are slow to start: on inputs of about 100K tokens, the prefill takes most of the wait for the first output token. A common approach prunes the input by scoring its tokens with the target model itself or with a small model of the same family that first writes an answer. However, this scoring takes much of the time that pruning saves. We find that the evidence for a question lies in a few whole units (images or paragraphs), and that a small hybrid model finds them with one attention head of an early layer, even at half image resolution. Based on these findings, we propose SkimPrefill
s0e3c7b6503.summary: Researchers propose a faster prefill method for vision-language models on long interleaved image-text inputs, using a small model to identify relevant evidence before pruning.
s0e3c7b6503.why: Long multimodal inputs make time-to-first-token slow; cheaper input pruning could cut latency for document and multi-image workloads.

s48c58b20cb.title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models
s48c58b20cb.description: arXiv:2611.24453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) seeks to decode neural network computations into human-understandable logic. A core methodology in MI is circuit discovery: identifying the information flow in sub-networks that drive specific model behaviors. While circuit discovery has matured within Natural Language Processing (NLP), the interpretable circuits in music models remain largely unexplored. In this work, we identify a music-functional circuit within two symbolic music generative models: ChatMusician and MuPT. The music function we consider is the prediction of the terminal tonic root in a classical harmonic progression pattern $I \ldots V \rightarrow I$. We use the Auto-Emergence algorithm to extract a principal sparse sub-network as the iden
s48c58b20cb.summary: Researchers identify a music-functional circuit in symbolic music models ChatMusician and MuPT, linking chord progression behavior to a sparse information flow.

s0005c9693a.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams
s0005c9693a.description: arXiv:2611.24475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent research suggests that individual neurons can have interpretable roles in AI behaviour. In Qwen3.5-4B, steering along one neuron's output direction increased decisions to conceal information more in teams than alone across five scenarios, even when teammates provided no messages. When all members participated and received steering, collective concealment increased in four scenarios, while inter-agent messaging helped temper concealment under steering. Moreover, removing the neuron's contribution had negligible effects. Collective settings can therefore change how an internal intervention affects AI behaviour.
s0005c9693a.summary: Steering a single neuron in Qwen3.5-4B increased information concealment in multi-agent teams across five scenarios, according to an arXiv study.
s0005c9693a.why: It suggests individual neuron steering can shift collective behavior in multi-agent systems, relevant to agent safety and oversight design.

s1f43ef0d1d.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
s1f43ef0d1d.description: arXiv:2611.24489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Function-level vulnerability detectors often exhibit fix reversal, assigning a higher vulnerability probability to a fixed version than to its vulnerable counterpart. Fixes usually lengthen functions, and larger length increases are associated with more severe reversal. Code-transformation experiments indicate that fix reversal mainly stems from a length shortcut: vulnerability probability increases with function length when content is fixed. We propose CFVul to address this problem. Sliding-window encoding covers complete functions, retaining fix information beyond the truncation boundary. During training, a content constraint encourages the vulnerable version to receive a higher vulnerability probability under a common length input. Durin
s1f43ef0d1d.summary: Researchers propose CFVul, a counterfactual method to reduce fix reversal in function-level vulnerability detectors caused by a function-length shortcut.
s1f43ef0d1d.why: Detectors that rate patched code as more vulnerable than unpatched code produce unreliable security signals for code review and scanning tools.

s7582ca82a2.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
s7582ca82a2.description: arXiv:2611.24491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier coding agents increasingly exhibit overeagerness, taking surprising, sometimes reckless actions beyond a user's mandate --- reported in recent system cards from frontier model developers. These cases are surfaced through internal deployment monitoring, which requires private traffic and is out of reach for open-weight models and independent evaluators. Automated alignment audits are the natural alternative, but capable models increasingly recognise the synthetic setup and adjust their behaviour. We introduce Continuation Audits, a pipeline that grounds the auditor on a prefix drawn from a real coding-agent transcript and directs it to continue the trajectory toward a seeded behaviour. Because the prefix is drawn from a real session
s7582ca82a2.summary: Researchers introduce Continuation Audits, a method for probing overeagerness in frontier coding agents in realistic settings without private deployment traffic.
s7582ca82a2.why: It offers a way for open-weight models and independent evaluators to test coding agents for actions beyond user mandates.

s3ca87c5cac.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
s3ca87c5cac.description: arXiv:2611.24496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GPUs are expensive, yet latency-critical large language model (LLM) inference leaves part of them idle. Colocation reclaims this capacity by running best-effort work, such as fine-tuning, alongside serving. Many leading LLMs now use a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, which adds a new source of idle time. Under expert parallelism, MoE experts are spread across GPUs, and because the router sends uneven numbers of tokens to each GPU, lightly loaded GPUs wait for the most loaded one. Even after applying load balancing solutions, such bubbles still take 8--13% of prefill time. We present BubbleTea, the first colocation system that leverages expert-parallel bubbles for fine-tuning. Unlike existing colocation systems, which make one scheduli
s3ca87c5cac.summary: Researchers propose harvesting idle time from expert-parallel load imbalance in MoE serving to run fine-tuning alongside LLM inference.
s3ca87c5cac.why: Reclaiming GPU idle time from MoE load imbalance could lower costs of colocating fine-tuning with latency-critical serving.

s8478bef18e.title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
s8478bef18e.description: arXiv:2611.24522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base. A pivotal challenge in MEL is capturing multi-level correspondences: the semantic consistency between mention-entity pairs and the complementary correlations across modalities. However, existing methods often suffer from element dominance due to their reliance on coupled interactions or coarse global aggregations. In response, we propose the Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction (MECI) framework. First, to capture multi-element mention-entity correspondences, we develop a Multi-view Experts Network that leverages a "divide-and-conquer" strategy for decoupled feature learning to mitigate element d
s8478bef18e.summary: Researchers present MECI, a framework for multimodal entity linking that models multi-level correspondences to reduce element dominance in mention-entity grounding.

s116b8f21c2.title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
s116b8f21c2.description: arXiv:2611.24540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building a small language model requires choosing which published improvements to combine. We compare five changes in the same model, using the same data and training budget. We test selected combinations and repeat each one with a second random seed. Mixture-of-experts layers, Muon optimisation and a Gated DeltaNet hybrid give the largest gains. Extra normalisation also helps, while an attention gate with a matched parameter budget adds little on average. The gains mostly combine, but small interactions between changes appear again in the repeated runs. Repetition also reveals benefits that an initial statistical estimate treated as noise. These findings apply to our small-model training setting; the expert models also have greater total c
s116b8f21c2.summary: A replicated factorial study tests five published improvements in small language models, finding mixture-of-experts, Muon optimisation and Gated DeltaNet give the largest gains.
s116b8f21c2.why: It gives practical guidance on which published architecture and optimiser changes are worth combining when training small models under a fixed budget.

s1a9261d28a.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
s1a9261d28a.description: arXiv:2611.24598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps. However, CoT is far from perfect: on some tasks, models perform worse than with direct-answer prompting, and on others they generate a few hundred tokens to reach the correct answer. We start by labelling each CoT hidden state as recovering if patching it into the direct prompt yields the correct answer, and failed otherwise. A linear probe shows that the model encodes these two classes differently. We then show that the representation space of the direct prompt holds a direction for each question that leads the model, in a short generation, to the correct answer more often than CoT does. Specifically, we rotate the
s1a9261d28a.summary: Researchers show chain-of-thought hidden states encode task-solving directions that distinguish when CoT helps or fails compared with direct-answer prompting.
s1a9261d28a.why: Understanding when CoT reasoning helps could guide choices between reasoning and direct-answer prompting to save tokens and latency.

s0ca4fc9361.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
s0ca4fc9361.description: arXiv:2611.24609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused. Drawing from human factors and AI governance literature, expert interviews and participant observation in a complex high-risk AI use case from the railways, we developed ALIGN, a scenario-based method that supports the governance of and stakeholder involvement in AI development and implementation in three ways: raising awareness for potential accountability-control misalignments in socio-technical systems and their negative consequences, offering a structured approach to as
s0ca4fc9361.summary: Researchers develop ALIGN, a scenario-based method for negotiating control and accountability among stakeholders in high-risk AI use cases, tested in railways.
s0ca4fc9361.why: It offers a structured approach for involving stakeholders in governance and accountability for safety-critical AI deployments.

s905fef5ca7.title: H3Remover: Reinforcing Video Object Removal without Paired Data
s905fef5ca7.description: arXiv:2611.24633v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pretrained video editors possess rich removal and completion priors, yet may retain targets or alter unrelated content. We present H3Remover, which reinforces MiniMax-H3 Base Ref2VA for video object removal without paired object-free training targets. To discourage superficial edits such as recoloring, a target-removal reward favors calibrated depth changes consistent with revealing farther content. To limit unintended scene changes, a background-geometry reward encourages preservation of relative depth ordering. To preserve background appearance without retaining unwanted shadows or reflections, an appearance reward constrains RGB changes in source-derived protected regions while exempting targets and estimated effects. Frozen HPSv3 comple
s905fef5ca7.summary: H3Remover applies reinforcement learning with depth and background-geometry rewards to a pretrained video editor for object removal without paired training data.

s9f83ba81af.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
s9f83ba81af.description: arXiv:2611.24636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation. Clover adapts Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion by combining recurrent memory of previously generated context with bidirectional softmax attention inside the current block. Historical memory readout competes with current-block tokens in a shared softmax, with learnable block-size calibration and a separate, zero-initialized right-context convolution branch. Clover leads the seven evaluated agent metrics, including 73.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1. On internal agent workloads, it reaches a reported generation speed o
s9f83ba81af.summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35B total and 3B active parameters, adapting Gated Delta Networks to block diffusion.
s9f83ba81af.why: A large MoE diffusion language model with thinking-mode generation is a new architecture option for teams tracking non-autoregressive LLMs.

s8baa13cd46.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
s8baa13cd46.description: arXiv:2611.24637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. Yet, porting CL to real-world edge devices remains challenging for two reasons: (i) online operation, where sensor data arrives one sample at a time and the device must adapt on-the-fly, and (ii) the low footprint of edge devices, which makes traditional error backpropagation training prohibitive. Inspired by the brain's wake and sleep cycles, the former for rapid adaptation with minimal resources and the latter for long-term consolidation, we introduce Hypnos, an open-source dual-phase platform for efficient CL at the edge. In the wake phase (e.g., dai
s8baa13cd46.summary: Hypnos is an end-to-end platform for continual learning on edge devices, inspired by wake and sleep cycles to handle online, one-sample-at-a-time data streams.
s8baa13cd46.why: Edge deployments needing on-device adaptation without full backpropagation could benefit from this platform design.

s63a765c367.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
s63a765c367.description: arXiv:2611.24641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage. We instead ask whether this bridge can adaptively select and combine representations from multiple structural encoders according to the target property. We find that supervised and generative material encoders provide complementary information for property prediction. We found that, for Zatom-1, this information is not concentrated in the final layer. Instead, the most informative representations occur at different depths depending o
s63a765c367.summary: Researchers propose adaptively selecting and combining representations from multiple structural encoders for materials science multimodal language models.

s44c5959210.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
s44c5959210.description: arXiv:2611.24651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard with a score of 75.59, while Piccolo-9B and Piccolo-4B achieve 68.35 and 67.46, respectively. All three rank first on the Private benchmark in their respective model-size categories. Research agents analyze model behavior, construct training data, conduct experiments, and use the results to refine subsequent proposals. Semantic slices an
s44c5959210.summary: Piccolo is a family of multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 27B parameters that co-evolve with training data via agentic data engineering and recursive self-improvement.
s44c5959210.why: Piccolo-27B reports top placement on the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard, a benchmark claim engineers may want to verify.

sc93a1a5d5f.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Qu\'ebec French
sc93a1a5d5f.description: arXiv:2611.24699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately capture its effects. In this paper, we present a controlled study of CPT for Qu\'ebec French language understanding across nine LLMs spanning different families and scales. Using a budget-matched protocol of 30M tokens per experiment, our results show that the benefit of CPT depends strongly on the starting model's existing competence in the target variety. When CPT is beneficial, the improvements are driven more by corpus composition than by data volume, with literary te
sc93a1a5d5f.summary: A controlled study tests when continual pre-training helps LLMs understand Québec French, across nine models with a budget-matched 30M-token protocol.
sc93a1a5d5f.why: It offers evidence on when domain or dialect adaptation pays off versus when aggregate benchmark scores may hide its real effects.

sbe670c0815.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents
sbe670c0815.description: arXiv:2611.24711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agents that do science must choose informative experiments and reason from their results, but most discovery benchmarks cannot separate that skill from recall, unstated scoring rules or shortcut policies. We introduce Openhagen Worlds, a suite of 27 procedurally generated environments (some with finite truth spaces), from classic puzzles of experimental reasoning to simulator-grounded physics and chemistry, in which an agent runs experiments under a budget and commits an answer that a deterministic verifier checks against a hidden truth. Every observation states the complete scoring rule, and each of the 178 difficulty levels is calibrated: it is admitted only if, on 64 development instances, a scripted oracle succeeds on at least 0.75, the
sbe670c0815.summary: Researchers introduce Openhagen Worlds, 27 procedurally generated environments for testing whether AI agents can run budgeted experiments and reach verified scientific answers.
sbe670c0815.why: It gives teams a benchmark that separates experimental reasoning from recall and shortcut policies when evaluating discovery agents.

sd34b042324.title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
sd34b042324.description: arXiv:2611.24728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure. A concise, selectively organised technical guide can provide an accessible starting point for developing a coherent understanding of this increasingly complex landscape. This article takes a generation-centred approach, connecting how models produce new observations with the modelling and learning principles that make generation possible. We develop a two-level perspective: first, distinguishing three recurring generation routes-direct transformation or decoding, sequential conditional construction, and iterative updating or transport; and second, examining the modelling a
sd34b042324.summary: A concise technical guide organizes the generative AI landscape around how different models produce new observations and how they sample.
sd34b042324.why: It provides a structured overview of generative model families, useful for engineers building a coherent mental map of the field.

sb009456a3f.title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schr\"odinger Bridges
sb009456a3f.description: arXiv:2611.24763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible. Cellular dynamics are inherently stochastic and involve changes in population size through proliferation and apoptosis. Growth-based methods represent population change as a rate on the density, which does not assign exits and entries to individual cells. Unbalanced Schr\"odinger bridges model individual events, but neural solvers for killed diffusion bridges simulate trajectories during training. We introduce Elysium, a simulation-free solver that jointly learns state transition and mass change. Using a killed Brownian reference and its time reversal, Elysium construct
sb009456a3f.summary: Elysium proposes a simulation-free neural solver for unbalanced Schrödinger bridges to model cellular dynamics with proliferation and apoptosis.

s353a4bf506.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
s353a4bf506.description: arXiv:2611.24764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning the spatiotemporal dynamics of cells from spatial transcriptomics requires connecting snapshots of different cells acquired in different coordinate frames. A rotation or translation of a section can appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence. We introduce horizontal flow matching, which learns changes in tissue organization, molecular state, and cell abundance up to shared rigid motion. The dynamics follow a continuity--reaction equation whose action assigns no cost to shared rigid motion, and the resulting horizontal projector removes this component from spatial prediction errors during learning and from predicted velocities during generation. An equivalent endpoint problem jointly estimates correspondence and
s353a4bf506.summary: Horizontal flow matching is introduced to learn single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics from spatial transcriptomics while ignoring shared rigid motion between tissue sections.

s4b6b3ba92a.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
s4b6b3ba92a.description: arXiv:2611.24765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models. Topology-based approaches capture connectivity but lack adversarial reasoning, while simulation-driven methods are primarily suited for offline analysis and are less effective for rapid evaluation of evolving attack scenarios. As a result, identifying realistic attack paths that jointly capture topology, threat semantics, and physical impact remains challenging. This paper presents a physics-grounded framework for identifying cyber-physical attack paths using large language models (LLMs), with cascading-failure-deri
s4b6b3ba92a.summary: Researchers propose using an LLM to identify high-impact cyber-physical attack paths in smart grids by combining topology, threat semantics and simulation.
s4b6b3ba92a.why: Grid operators and security teams may find LLM-guided attack path analysis useful for faster evaluation of evolving threat scenarios.

s536b59031a.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
s536b59031a.description: arXiv:2611.24778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance? Its answer separates bad decisions from bad luck. We prove that world models trained on factual transitions cannot answer it on their own, whatever their data or capacity. For many physical systems, the observed outcome and a simple property of the dynamics suffice: natura non facit saltus, nature makes no leaps. When actions and disturbances act as separate forces, their interaction is second-order in time, so the counterfactual outcome is, to first order, the observed ou
s536b59031a.summary: The paper proves that world models trained only on factual transitions cannot answer counterfactual 'what if' questions alone, and proposes JEPA-based counterfactual models.

sa21dfc2cb7.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
sa21dfc2cb7.description: arXiv:2611.24782v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories? We tested whether final weights reveal initialization, task order, and earlier trajectory states. Training reorganized the ensemble: initial pairwise distances did not consistently predict final distances. Nevertheless, all 30 trained networks were correctly matched to their initial weights among ten candidates per dataset. Networks sharing an initialization also developed recognizable final hidden representations across different batch schedules, although direct comparisons with initial acti
sa21dfc2cb7.summary: Experiments show that neural networks trained on the same task retain decodable traces of their initialization, task order, and training trajectory in their final weights.
sa21dfc2cb7.why: Training history leaves recoverable traces in weights, which matters for reproducibility, auditing and model provenance questions.

s6b0d5e5519.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
s6b0d5e5519.description: arXiv:2611.24788v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call. Its verification interface spans single-step execution, block-level proof checking and whole-theory builds, with checkpoints for cheap branching and backtracking, and a build from scratch as the final arbiter. The service runs as a single container with monitoring and is accessible via a Python client, two MCP servers and a raw HTTP API. In our measurements IPS is level with PIDE MCP, a PIDE frontend for agents, at one worker and ahead of it at eight, at its commit of October 2026 (the tool is now PIDE AI). Once its session
s6b0d5e5519.summary: Isabelle Pool Server is a verification service offering pooled warm Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with Python client and MCP servers.
s6b0d5e5519.why: Teams training provers or running multi-agent proof systems get a deployable verification backend with leasing, admission control and time budgets.

sebf13212d4.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks
sebf13212d4.description: arXiv:2611.24797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks with randomly initialized, fixed weights and trainable biases are universal approximators, yet the dynamics of bias-only training remain largely unexplored. We study these dynamics in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks through activation codes, the binary patterns of active neurons that partition the input space into convex polyhedral regions. We show that the gradients with respect to the biases depend on each input only through its activation code, and hence the training dynamics can be characterized with these codes. In particular, as long as the activation codes remain fixed, training reduces to a linear least-squares problem with the codes as features. Training can then be understood as a sequence of least-squares problems,
sebf13212d4.summary: The paper analyzes training dynamics when only biases are trained in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with fixed random weights, via activation codes.

s9ab52b2eed.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
s9ab52b2eed.description: arXiv:2611.24798v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus. In this work we propose Soft-MoQE, a Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts architecture that replaces variational quantum training with the input-dependent selection and combination of fixed quantum feature maps. The model is composed of a heterogeneous pool of non-trainable quantum circuits, each defining a distinct embedding, and a classical gating network that learns how
s9ab52b2eed.summary: Soft-MoQE proposes a soft mixture of quantum experts that replaces variational quantum training with input-dependent expert selection for hybrid quantum-classical learning.

s2e1c13d31b.title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
s2e1c13d31b.description: arXiv:2611.24810v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers. We present LAaDT-DSS, decision-support software that answers all three under Turkish tariff rules from one simulation core. Non-experts reach it by clicking a house on a 3D map or by asking in plain words; a language model is asked to call the simulation tools, not to compute. Each entry of its 125-entry parameter registry is marked as sourced or estimated. Case studies test the system. Its PV yield lies within $\pm$3.6% of two independent tools at equal losses. Across 2,048 draws of its estimated inputs, the answer for PV alone held in all but one; with a
s2e1c13d31b.summary: LAaDT-DSS is decision-support software that simulates rooftop PV investment, incentives and grid limits under Turkish tariff rules, with a language model calling simulation tools.
s2e1c13d31b.why: It shows a pattern for LLM-driven tools where the model routes requests to deterministic simulation rather than computing results itself.

se9b4f62a38.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
se9b4f62a38.description: arXiv:2611.24830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological con
se9b4f62a38.summary: Chiron is a foundation model fine-tuned to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align response distributions with human population statistics.

s1238ab8364.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
s1238ab8364.description: arXiv:2611.24840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics.
s1238ab8364.summary: The paper probes whether action-conditioned semantic forecasting for autonomous driving actually depends on the ego vehicle's action, not just prediction fidelity.
s1238ab8364.why: World models used for driving planning may ignore the conditioning action, so teams should verify action dependence, not only forecast accuracy.

s2baf47cd69.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
s2baf47cd69.description: arXiv:2611.24888v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human. Testing with 30 participants, we establish a human baseline and report the identity signals interrogators rely on: stylometric features, personality traits, and biographical facts. To demonstrate the framework, we design an LLM-based system that plays the game for one of the paper's authors, drawing on an autoethnographic dataset spanning ten years of personal digital communication. In a 20-person deception study, interrogators choose our system over the author's own friends in 7 of 1
s2baf47cd69.summary: The Personal Imitation Game proposes testing whether an LLM can replicate a specific individual in conversation, with a 30-participant human baseline.

sb034d9ec96.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
sb034d9ec96.description: arXiv:2611.24924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima. We introduce Agentic Harness Engineering Beta (AHE-Beta), a requirement-centered loop that brings real-world engineering practices into harness evolution. The loop consists of three steps: (1) User-driven evaluation lets simulated users raise their requirements as issues while they work with the harness over multiple turns. (2) Tea
sb034d9ec96.summary: Researchers introduce AHE-Beta, a requirement-centered loop for evolving agent harnesses that targets implicit user requirements and interaction needs.
sb034d9ec96.why: It suggests harness improvements driven by requirements rather than benchmark scores alone, which may reduce narrow patches and benchmark-specific overfitting.

s6c63640809.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
s6c63640809.description: arXiv:2611.24927v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI. We motivate the examination of the organizational AI supply chain---highlighting concerns about concentration, power, chokepoints, cascading failures, fragmented accountability, and risk---then describe our pipeline for mapping the AI supply chain. Our pipeline yields our main contribution: a multilayered,
s6c63640809.summary: A paper maps the organizational AI supply chain, examining dependencies, vulnerabilities, and market concentration across the actors that build and deploy AI.
s6c63640809.why: Understanding supplier dependencies and concentration risks helps leaders assess vendor lock-in and single points of failure in AI stacks.

s6b7ca1cf50.title: Human-AI Interactions and Societal Pitfalls
s6b7ca1cf50.description: arXiv:2309.10448v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When working with generative artificial intelligence (AI), users may see productivity gains, but the AI-generated content may not match their preferences exactly. To study this effect, we introduce a Bayesian framework in which heterogeneous users choose how much information to share with the AI, facing a trade-off between output fidelity and communication cost. We show that the interplay between these individual-level decisions and AI training may lead to societal challenges. Outputs may become more homogenized, especially when the AI is trained on AI-generated content, potentially triggering a homogenization death spiral. And any AI bias may propagate to become societal bias. A solution to the homogenization and bias issues is to reduce
s6b7ca1cf50.summary: A Bayesian study models how users decide how much information to share with generative AI, finding individual choices and AI training can homogenize outputs.

sebf30649c3.title: Games played by Exponential Weights Algorithms
sebf30649c3.description: arXiv:2407.06676v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the last-iterate convergence properties of the exponential weights algorithm with constant learning rates. We consider a repeated interaction in discrete time, where each player uses an exponential weights algorithm characterized by an initial mixed action and a fixed learning rate, so that the mixed action profile $p^t$ played at stage $t$ follows an homogeneous Markov chain. At first, we show that whenever a strict Nash equilibrium exists, the probability to play a strict Nash equilibrium at the next stage converges almost surely to 0 or 1. Secondly, we show that the limit of $p^t$, whenever it exists, belongs to the set of ``Nash Equilibria with Equalizing Payoffs''. Thirdly, we show that in strong coordination games
sebf30649c3.summary: A paper analyzes last-iterate convergence of exponential weights learning in repeated games, showing behavior near strict Nash equilibria.

s69b9207735.title: A Survey on Collaborative Mechanisms Between Large and Small Language Models
s69b9207735.description: arXiv:2505.07460v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) deliver powerful AI capabilities but face deployment challenges due to high resource costs and latency, whereas Small Language Models (SLMs) offer efficiency and deployability at the cost of reduced performance.
