Collaboration between LLMs and SLMs emerges as a crucial paradigm to synergistically balance these trade-offs, enabling advanced AI applications, especially on resource-constrained edge devices. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of LLM-SLM collaboration, detailing various interaction mechanisms (pipeline, routing, auxiliary, distillation, fusion), key enabling technologies, and diverse application scenarios driven by on-device needs like low latency, privacy, personalization, and offline op
s69b9207735.summary: A survey reviews collaboration mechanisms between large and small language models to balance cost, latency, and performance, especially on edge devices.
s69b9207735.why: Hybrid LLM-SLM architectures offer a way to cut serving cost and latency while keeping capability, relevant to deployment planning.

sb51f3d989d.title: MARBLE: An Agentic Benchmark for Spatial Reasoning and Visual Abstraction
sb51f3d989d.description: arXiv:2506.22992v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A central challenge for multimodal language models (MLLMs) in real-world tasks is to abstract visual observations into structured spatial states and reason over how those states change under actions over long horizons. Existing multimodal benchmarks often focus on static question answering, where answers can be directly extracted from images, or assume symbolic states are available and bypass the visual-to-spatial abstraction process. We present MARBLE, a diagnostic benchmark for spatially grounded multimodal reasoning and planning across three agent environments: CUBE, MAZE, and BLOX. MARBLE spans 2D and 3D spatial puzzles under geometric constraints, dynamic layouts, and spatial transformations, with difficulty systematically controlled
sb51f3d989d.summary: MARBLE is a diagnostic benchmark testing multimodal models on turning visual observations into spatial states and planning actions over long horizons.
sb51f3d989d.why: It exposes gaps in visual-to-spatial reasoning for agentic multimodal systems, useful when evaluating models for planning tasks.

s01f33b8cec.title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
s01f33b8cec.description: arXiv:2602.23276v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chest X-ray plays a central role in thoracic diagnosis, and its interpretation inherently requires multi-step, evidence-grounded reasoning. However, large vision-language models (LVLMs) often generate plausible responses that are not faithfully grounded in diagnostic evidence and provide limited visual evidence for verification, while also requiring costly retraining to support new diagnostic tasks, limiting their reliability and adaptability in clinical settings. To address these limitations, we present CXReasonAgent, a diagnostic agent that integrates a large language model (LLM) with clinically grounded diagnostic tools to perform evidence-grounded diagnostic reasoning using image-derived diagnostic and visual evidence. To evaluate the
s01f33b8cec.summary: CXReasonAgent is a diagnostic agent for chest X-rays that grounds reasoning in visual evidence and supports new tasks without retraining.
s01f33b8cec.why: Evidence-grounded agents that adapt without retraining offer a design pattern for high-stakes domains where verifiability matters.

se5e037ab84.title: Prior Knowledge or Search? A Study of LLM Agents in Hardware-Aware Code Optimization
se5e037ab84.description: arXiv:2605.19782v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM discovery and optimization systems are increasingly applied across domains, implementing a common propose-evaluate-revise loop. Such optimization or discovery progresses via context conditioning on received feedback from an environment. However, as modern LLM agents are increasingly complex in their structure, it is difficult to evaluate which components contribute the most, and when and how this exploration may fail. We answer these questions through three controlled experiments. Our findings: (1) In pure black-box optimization, LLMs act as greedy optimizers. (2) In zero-shot kernel generation, providing explicit input-size information has no measurable effect, models converge to the same kernel parameters regardless of size or tempe
se5e037ab84.summary: A study of LLM agents in hardware-aware code optimization examines when agents rely on prior knowledge versus search in propose-evaluate-revise loops.
se5e037ab84.why: Findings on when agent loops fail help engineers decide how much to invest in search versus prompting for code optimization.

sa282a94074.title: CaMBRAIN: Real-time, Continuous EEG Inference with Causal State Space Models
sa282a94074.description: arXiv:2605.28792v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a critical, non-invasive method to monitor electrical brain activity. EEGs can span anywhere from a couple seconds to multiple hours, posing a major hurdle for existing deep learning methods due to two major factors: (1) existing EEG models are predominantly built upon the attention mechanism, incurring quadratic scaling as the sequence length increases, and (2) raw EEG signals must be processed in a sliding-window fashion due to fixed-length input requirements, preventing global understanding of the entire signal. To this extent, we propose CaMBRAIN - the first Causal, Mamba-based state space model (SSM) capable of real-time inference of EEG signals, arguing that bidirectional approaches are needlessly exp
sa282a94074.summary: CaMBRAIN uses causal state space models for real-time, continuous EEG inference, avoiding attention's quadratic scaling and sliding-window processing.

s9cd2892acc.title: Arbor: How Search Policy Shapes Agent Behavior in System Optimization
s9cd2892acc.description: arXiv:2606.12563v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Achieving peak performance on modern accelerators requires coordinated optimization across kernels, operator fusion, KV-cache management, quantization, scheduling, and communication overlap, a process that demands weeks of expert effort per model and hardware platform. We present Arbor, a system that gives autonomous agents an explicit optimization tree to reason over, backtrack through, and deepen with experience, with pluggable search policies, scored bandit traversal, parallel agent swarms, and depth-first sweep, sharing a common harness of containerized isolation, automatic rollback, and end-to-end validation. Arbor generalizes across domains: +40% to +193% on six production inference models across two GPU generations, +42.8% on LLM t
s9cd2892acc.summary: Arbor gives autonomous agents an optimization tree and pluggable search policies to tune kernels, fusion, KV-cache, quantization, and scheduling on accelerators.
s9cd2892acc.why: Agent-driven system tuning could cut weeks of expert effort per model and hardware platform, relevant to inference performance work.

sa5927d8049.title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-informed Neural Operator for Mindlin-Reissner Plates
sa5927d8049.description: arXiv:2606.16624v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Plate and shell structures are widely used in engineering fields. Rapid response prediction for such structures under complex geometries, heterogeneous materials, and varying loads is important for engineering design, but conventional numerical methods usually require repeated modeling and solution when the physical configuration changes. To address this issue, this study proposes a geometry-aware variational physics-informed neural operator (GA-VINO) for Mindlin-Reissner plates. GA-VINO represents the plate geometry using boundary point clouds and incorporates a material encoder, a load encoder, and a scalar-parameter branch to handle spatially random material fields, spatially varying pressure loads, and sample-level uniform parameters.
sa5927d8049.summary: GA-VINO is a geometry-aware physics-informed neural operator that predicts responses of Mindlin-Reissner plates across geometries, materials, and loads.

sb4a828e21b.title: When Does Learning to Stop Help? Configuring Risk-Controlled Early Exit for Reasoning-Model Services
sb4a828e21b.description: arXiv:2606.30852v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Early exit lowers the cost of serving a reasoning model by stopping its reasoning once a provisional answer looks final. An operator must choose between a learned stopping rule and one static token budget, and savings against full reasoning do not settle the choice. We present a procedure that decides on calibration data from the workload. It certifies both families with Learn-then-Test to one bound on the fraction of all questions that full reasoning answers correctly but early exit does not, prices provisional answers as the serving stack does, and deploys the cheapest certified candidate. Across four models and five benchmarks neither family is better throughout. At a 5% risk target the learned rule saves 10.4-17.0 percentage points mo
sb4a828e21b.summary: A procedure uses calibration data and Learn-then-Test to decide between learned stopping rules and static token budgets for early exit in reasoning-model serving.
sb4a828e21b.why: Operators serving reasoning models can use it to pick early-exit settings while bounding accuracy loss versus full reasoning.

sb0aee9977a.title: ElephantAgent: Contextual State Continuity in Agentic Systems
sb0aee9977a.description: arXiv:2607.01919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agentic systems enhance their capabilities by invoking external tools and maintaining persistent memory. However, recent tool and memory poisoning attacks can covertly bias agent behavior. We observe that such attacks mounted out of band share a single enabler: each succeeds only by presenting the agent with a contextual state (e.g., tool state and memory) that is not the latest faithfully evolved one. This observation suggests that a continuity check over the contextual state covers this family of attacks. We present ElephantAgent, a protocol that enforces Contextual State Continuity over the bounded, security-critical subset of the agent's context. Before each planning-and-execution cycle, ElephantAgent recomputes the digest of the loca
sb0aee9977a.summary: ElephantAgent proposes a continuity check over agent contextual state, such as tool state and memory, to detect tool and memory poisoning attacks.
sb0aee9977a.why: Agents with persistent memory and tools face covert poisoning risks, and state continuity checks offer a defense to evaluate.

s47be521c05.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
s47be521c05.description: arXiv:2607.10059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent systems based on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for autonomous tasks, yet existing evaluations mostly focus on task success rather than whether agents know when to abstain. This gap poses real risks: under ambiguity, conflicting constraints, or tool failures, agents may execute unintended and irreversible actions. To close this gap, we present the first systematic evaluation framework for agentic abstention: the calibrated ability of tool-using LLM agents to recognize when not to act. At its core, AgentAbstain is a paired-task benchmark built on an agent-native taxonomy of 8 abstention scenarios across pre-execution reasoning and runtime discovery. It contains 263 paired tasks across 42 executable sandbox env
s47be521c05.summary: AgentAbstain introduces an evaluation framework measuring whether tool-using LLM agents can recognize when not to act under ambiguity or tool failures.
s47be521c05.why: Irreversible actions by agents under uncertainty are a deployment risk, and abstention metrics add a check beyond task success.

s2c6f16586e.title: Bringing Back Rule Induction to Fluid Intelligence Research? An Initial Validation of the ARC-AGI Benchmark in Humans
s2c6f16586e.description: arXiv:2607.11263v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two competing perspectives on fluid intelligence (gf) measures propose that performance is primarily constrained either by working memory capacity or by the ability to induce novel relations. The first perspective is currently dominant in measurement, as evident from the use of a limited set of recurring rules, whereas the second perspective is reflected in many definitions but rarely present in measurement. The ARC-AGI benchmark predominantly requires rule induction and was proposed as a measure of gf for both humans and artificial systems. However, its psychometric properties have not yet been examined in human samples. We therefore investigated the psychometric characteristics and nomological network of ARC-AGI in a first study with 10
s2c6f16586e.summary: A human validation study examines whether the ARC-AGI benchmark measures rule induction as a fluid intelligence construct, versus working memory capacity.

sb9b4050c5d.title: Disagreement-Guided Agentic Data Curation for Multimodal Safety
sb9b4050c5d.description: arXiv:2607.14256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Written safety policies in multimodal settings define categories whose visual boundaries span many contexts. We study disagreement as a signal for identifying useful synthetic boundary cases. Our pipeline generates policy-conditioned images, selects cases with target--rater or inter-rater disagreement, conditionally escalates unresolved cases, and retrieves the resulting rater-labeled examples as in-context demonstrations. On a failure-enriched multimodal safety benchmark, policy grounding reduces false negative rate (FNR) from 0.875 to 0.413 and raises F1 from 0.220 to 0.731; retrieval from 50 disagreement-selected examples further reduces FNR to 0.245, compared with 0.297 from a 350-example Regular pool. The selected memory also improve
sb9b4050c5d.summary: Researchers propose an agentic pipeline that uses rater disagreement to curate synthetic multimodal safety examples, cutting false negative rate from 0.875 to 0.413 on a benchmark.
sb9b4050c5d.why: Shows disagreement-driven synthetic data curation can substantially improve multimodal safety classifiers, a practical approach for teams building content moderation.

s5efff43e03.title: Making Mathematical Knowledge Explainable, Accessible and Interoperable Through Large Language Model Integration
s5efff43e03.description: arXiv:2607.24512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mathematical models are central to formalizing research problems, yet their documentation often falls short of FAIR principles. Knowledge bases such as the Mathematical Model Database (MathModDB) address this gap by providing curated, semantically rich representations of mathematical models. Built on Wikibase, the same open-source infrastructure underlying Wikidata, MathModDB utilizes Semantic Web technologies to support Linked Open Data, collaborative editing, and the storage of semantically enriched metadata, making it a domain-specific knowledge graph within the broader Wikidata ecosystem. However, access to MathModDB currently requires either navigating a complex web interface or proficiency in SPARQL and Wikibase APIs, posing signifi
s5efff43e03.summary: A paper describes integrating large language models with MathModDB, a Wikibase-based knowledge base, to make mathematical models more FAIR, explainable and interoperable.

s1b0a6850e4.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning
s1b0a6850e4.description: arXiv:2608.01802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Aerial search missions often require an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to locate a target from only a brief description of its appearance and surroundings, a task known as target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN). The task demands city-scale exploration and grounding as well as collision-free close-range approach, two interleaved processes that are difficult to reconcile within a single agent. Most existing methods adapt the ground VLN paradigm to a single UAV and rely on external assistance to compensate for its inefficiency. A recent attempt deploys two UAVs at complementary altitudes but still depends on privileged sensing and trains the two agents independently, precluding any mutual adaptation. We propose CoNav-UAV,
s1b0a6850e4.summary: CoNav-UAV proposes a Stackelberg learning approach using two cooperating UAVs at different altitudes for target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation.
s1b0a6850e4.why: Offers a multi-agent design pattern for splitting city-scale search and close-range approach across cooperating agents.

s44fadcd629.title: JUDOR: CTDE-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Co-Optimization of Joint UAV Motion and Decentralized Opportunistic Routing in Delay-Tolerant Network
s44fadcd629.description: arXiv:2608.04590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing deployment of delay-tolerant networks (DTNs) has made store-carry-forward (SCF) communication indispensable for operating under sparse intermittent connectivity. However, intermittent contact opportunities, finite node buffers, and limited message time-to-live (TTL) degrade message delivery performance and induce network congestion. Yet unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), with extended radio coverage and controllable trajectories, can bridge ground-node pairs that would otherwise suffer poor connectivity. Nevertheless, conventional routing schemes decouple UAV motion control from message replication, and consequently fail to leverage UAV mobility to proactively create future contact opportunities. This paper presents JUDOR (Joint
s44fadcd629.summary: JUDOR applies CTDE-based multi-agent reinforcement learning to jointly optimize UAV motion and opportunistic routing in delay-tolerant networks.

s092b1aae65.title: Beyond Routing Weights: Faithful Response-Level Interpretation of Mixture-of-Experts Reward Models via Contribution Contrast
s092b1aae65.description: arXiv:2608.06400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reward models are central to learning from human preferences, yet identifying what drives their predictions remains challenging. Recent sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reward models seek to improve interpretability by routing prompts to specialized experts and characterizing experts through examples with high routing weights. However, routing weights only reveal which prompts an expert $\textit{receives}$, not how it $\textit{judges}$ responses, providing only a partial account of expert behavior. We therefore propose $\textbf{Co}$ntribution-$\textbf{Co}$ntrast ($\textbf{CoCo}$) response-level interpretation, which faithfully characterizes experts' roles using chosen-rejected response pairs with the largest contribution contrasts, jointly
s092b1aae65.summary: A paper proposes Contribution-Contrast, a method to interpret how mixture-of-experts reward models judge responses, going beyond routing weights.
s092b1aae65.why: Better interpretability of reward models can help teams audit what drives preference-tuned model behavior.

sb53464610b.title: Linearized 2-Simplicial Attention
sb53464610b.description: arXiv:2608.09307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a linearized form of 2-simplicial attention by rewriting the trilinear score as an inner product between a composite query and a key, so that the sum over keys takes the same form as ordinary softmax attention. We then approximate this sum with positive random features and store all previous keys in a fixed-size state, while the sum over second keys stays exact over all previous tokens. This reduces the cost from cubic to quadratic in sequence length, and both keys range over all previous tokens, which windowed 2-simplicial attention does not allow. We implement it with custom Triton kernels and combine it with Kimi Delta Attention to build a model with no softmax attention at all. With 15B equal training tokens on FineWeb-Edu,
sb53464610b.summary: Researchers present a linearized form of 2-simplicial attention that uses positive random features to reduce cost from cubic to quadratic in sequence length.
sb53464610b.why: Reducing attention cost from cubic to quadratic could make more expressive attention variants practical for long-sequence models.

s893706b691.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
s893706b691.description: arXiv:2608.24735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-improving LLM agents refine answers, not the process that produces those answers. Systems that add a meta-level hold that level fixed, and those that edit themselves must leave part of their own editing machinery untouched to stay stable, capping the meta-depth they realize at roughly two. We present Meta$^n$, which keeps the meta-operation fixed and recurses on its input instead. That operation, $\Omega$, is applied repeatedly to its own products, reading the traces of the solver stack below together with the code that produced them, then writing the next layer as a strategic pre-process and a library of callable helpers. Because $\Omega$ never changes, it cannot destabilize the system, and because its input strictly grows, each lay
s893706b691.summary: Meta^n proposes a recursive self-improvement framework where a fixed meta-operation is applied repeatedly to its own outputs, rather than capping meta-depth at about two.

s0660ab1e9c.title: MAP: A Benchmark on Multimodal Accessibility Planning for Real World Places
s0660ab1e9c.description: arXiv:2608.28384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce MAP, the first benchmark to evaluate multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility requirements when planning visits to places in the real world. In our evaluation, systems are presented with requests to verify or recommend a point of interest meeting an accessibility requirement. MAP contains two novel assessments: Claim verification for accessibility planning assesses if information on places and stated accessibility features is supported and identifies places that satisfy requested accessibility features. Visual evidence retrieval for accessibility planning checks if a multimodal AI system can select visual evidence for the requested place and accessibility feature. Our methodology supports comparison of
s0660ab1e9c.summary: MAP is a benchmark testing multimodal AI assistants on planning real-world place visits that meet users' accessibility requirements.
s0660ab1e9c.why: Highlights gaps in how well multimodal assistants verify accessibility claims, relevant to teams building location or travel assistants.

s57ceb4866e.title: Bad Genius: Counterfactual-Guided Harness Evolution Beyond Task-Specific Shortcuts
s57ceb4866e.description: arXiv:2609.18366v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An optimized agent harness can improve on held-out tasks by relying on formatting conventions that those tasks share with the rest of the benchmark. We introduce Counterfactual Harness Search and Evolution (CHASE) to test whether harness improvements survive changes to the evaluation protocol. A Proposer edits the harness around a fixed foundation model. A Challenger then searches for a protocol change that preserves the tasks but reduces the updated harness's gain over the initial harness. Executable checks test whether the transformation preserves task semantics. If the gain loss is confirmed on held-out tasks, CHASE adds the transformation to an archive that constrains subsequent harness updates. We give conditions under which this fin
s57ceb4866e.summary: CHASE proposes counterfactual search over evaluation protocols to test whether agent harness gains survive changes to the benchmark, rather than relying on shared formatting shortcuts.
s57ceb4866e.why: Suggests agent benchmark gains may reflect formatting shortcuts, so teams should stress-test harness improvements under protocol changes.

sd42233a24b.title: RiskWorld: Risk-Aware World Modeling with Flow-Guided Occupancy Evolution for Selective Trajectory Planning in Automated Driving
sd42233a24b.description: arXiv:2609.18442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safe motion planning in automated driving requires anticipating evolving traffic risks and deciding when to revise the current planned trajectory. We introduce RiskWorld, a risk-aware world modeling framework for shared occupancy forecasting and selective trajectory replacement. Spatial risk fields and temporal actor context are fused with visual bird's-eye-view features. Flow-guided evolution transports occupancy and scene features, while signed residuals correct occupancy after transport. One forecast is generated per planning step and reused across candidates. Each candidate is compared with a current-state persistence reference, yielding a nonnegative collision-score correction. The trajectory selected by current-world evaluation serv
sd42233a24b.summary: RiskWorld is a risk-aware world-modeling framework that forecasts shared occupancy and selectively replaces planned trajectories for automated driving.

s1e3f192daf.title: WorkWorlds: Evaluating Agents in a Company Built Before the Task
s1e3f192daf.description: arXiv:2609.23806v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many knowledge work benchmarks are built around single tasks, where the context and files for each task are selected concurrently or after task definition. Research has argued that this construction method does not reflect real workplace work, yet the impact has never been measured under controlled conditions. To compare the two constructions under controlled conditions, we introduce WorkWorlds, an infrastructure that modularizes company components into revision, date, and employee seat to be separately adjusted. Using historical data donated by a real company, we reconstructed a pharmaceutical company, PharmaCo. Two experts with over ten years of industry experience each wrote eight tasks based on real events that occurred at the company
s1e3f192daf.summary: WorkWorlds is an evaluation infrastructure that builds company contexts before tasks, and it compares this against single-task benchmark construction for knowledge-work agents.
s1e3f192daf.why: Indicates single-task agent benchmarks may not reflect real workplace conditions, which matters when evaluating enterprise agents.

s3268b93121.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy response prediction using pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging with clinical variables
s3268b93121.description: arXiv:2609.26105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prediction of pathological complete response before neoadjuvant chemotherapy may facilitate more tailored therapeutic planning for breast cancer patients. This work proposes a deep-learning model for pretreatment data only, combining apparent diffusion coefficient maps, dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, and clinical variables. The study uses the public ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 multicenter dataset. The architecture employs EfficientNet-B0 pretrained encoders for image feature extraction and late fusion with clinical information. Multiple clinical variables were evaluated, including age, race, histological type, HR/HER2 subtype, SBR grade, and maximum diameter. Only HR/HER2 subtype improved the average area under the receiver o
s3268b93121.summary: Researchers propose a deep-learning model combining pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced MRI with clinical variables to predict pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer.

s88b3e0f24f.title: Cost-Efficient LLM Evaluation: A Framework for Narrow Confidence Intervals Under Fixed Budgets
s88b3e0f24f.description: arXiv:2609.29140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasingly important role in both academic research and industry. Reliable evaluation helps researchers understand model capabilities and assess progress during model development. However, evaluation can be costly, and researchers often need to assess performance within a fixed budget. Because model outputs can vary across runs, this budget must be allocated between testing different tasks and repeating selected tasks. A confidence interval quantifies the uncertainty in the resulting performance estimate. Obtaining narrower intervals at the same confidence level and evaluation cost provides a more precise assessment of model performance, helping researchers draw clearer conclusions from limited obser
s88b3e0f24f.summary: A paper presents a framework for allocating a fixed evaluation budget between tasks and repeated runs to produce narrow confidence intervals for LLM performance.
s88b3e0f24f.why: Gives practical guidance for budgeting LLM evaluations, helping teams get reliable scores without excess compute spend.

s883b6b3236.title: What Does a Harness Buy? Tokens, Mostly
s883b6b3236.description: arXiv:2610.04433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A coding agent is a language model inside a harness: the system prompt, the tools, and the context management that let a chat model work in a repository. Most of the engineering on these agents goes into the harness, and vendors and leaderboards credit it with score gains. Earlier studies have fixed the model and swapped the harness, but have not measured whether the swap changes the pass rate more than running the same harness again. We run seven models through three production harnesses, Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent, and OpenCode, on SWE-bench Verified and two benchmarks of other kinds, and rerun them unchanged. No harness leads consistently across models. Where the data can bound the difference between two harnesses, the bound is 2 to 5
s883b6b3236.summary: A study runs seven models through three production coding-agent harnesses on SWE-bench and measures how much harness choice versus repeated runs changes pass rates.
s883b6b3236.why: Suggests harness engineering may matter less than vendors claim, so teams should check whether score gains exceed run-to-run variance.

s47508245c8.title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use
s47508245c8.description: arXiv:2610.09127v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing an editable CAD model from a 3D shape remains a challenging engineering task. Existing methods can propose CAD operations, but no single source of proposals works equally well across different part geometries and stages of reconstruction. We introduce CADFather, an autonomous agentic system that coordinates complementary tools to recover parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes. A vision-language assistant inspects renders of the target and intermediate reconstructions, then decides which candidate CAD programs to extend, which tools to invoke, how many proposals to generate, and when to finish. Learned and algorithmic tools propose CAD operations, while numerical optimization refines the parameters of existing programs. Prop
s47508245c8.summary: CADFather is an agentic system that coordinates multiple tools and a vision-language assistant to reconstruct editable parametric CAD programs from 3D meshes.

s21b8c16a7b.title: MemeLogos: Knowledge-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection
s21b8c16a7b.description: arXiv:2610.15463v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: With the rapid proliferation of social media, harmful memes have become a growing threat to online ecosystems. Their harmfulness is often implicitly conveyed through complex interactions among visual, textual, and contextual cues, making accurate detection challenging. Recent studies have introduced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and external knowledge into harmful meme detection. However, existing methods mainly retrieve similar instances or auxiliary information, limiting their ability to capture reusable harmfulness knowledge and underlying reasoning mechanisms, and thus constraining both detection performance and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning
s21b8c16a7b.summary: MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning method, is proposed for detecting harmful memes by capturing reusable harmfulness knowledge.
s21b8c16a7b.why: Shows how retrieval of reusable domain knowledge, not just similar instances, may improve multimodal content moderation systems.

s7f56ab6256.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
s7f56ab6256.description: arXiv:2610.25096v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, s
s7f56ab6256.summary: RetailBridge, a compositional benchmark built from persona-driven simulations, is introduced to evaluate agentic RAG across heterogeneous enterprise retail data sources.
s7f56ab6256.why: Gives teams a controlled way to test whether agents can chain evidence across structured and unstructured enterprise retail data.

sf8a9ca9868.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
sf8a9ca9868.description: arXiv:2610.26829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: ProteinGeoBench is a set of 131 tasks that give an agent protein structure files and ask it to look up recorded facts, check sequences, calculate geometry from atom coordinates or reason about structures. We ran four frontier models on every task several times (4,249 runs) and 26 models on a subset. A single overall score hides two different skills. Three of the four frontier models are best at looking up facts and worst at calculating from coordinates: Claude Opus 5 scores 0.907 on lookup and 0.716 on calculation. Gemini 3.1 Pro is the exception. Geometry is overrepresented among the hardest tasks. Half of the twelve tasks that all four models fail are calculations, although calculations are a fifth of the suite, and eight of the twelve
sf8a9ca9868.summary: ProteinGeoBench, a 131-task benchmark, finds frontier models strong at looking up protein structure facts but weaker at calculating geometry from atom coordinates.
sf8a9ca9868.why: Highlights that agent benchmark scores can hide large gaps between skills, so teams should evaluate tasks separately.

s0e9d0f602a.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
s0e9d0f602a.description: arXiv:2610.26924v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: General-purpose agents are increasingly expected to perform professional analytics work, which requires sustained reasoning, iterative investigation, and reliable evidence. Training these capabilities requires diverse and challenging tasks. However, generating tasks directly from raw data often overlooks deeper questions that emerge through analysis and provides limited evidence for verification. To address these limitations, we introduce DataPraxis, an analytics task synthesis framework based on verified workspace evolution. The framework progressively enriches workspaces with validated findings and artifacts, then inherits and combines these workspaces to uncover deeper questions. It constructs tasks from accumulated findings and their
s0e9d0f602a.summary: DataPraxis, a framework based on verified workspace evolution, is introduced to synthesize verified analytics tasks for training general-purpose agents.
s0e9d0f602a.why: Offers a method for generating verifiable training tasks for analytics agents, which could matter for teams building data-analysis agents.

sff33c277a2.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
sff33c277a2.description: arXiv:2610.31511v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations \rev{through separate per-player decision calls}, selecting high-level actions \rev{and image-labeled target cells} while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of \rev{two-player} coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff depe
sff33c277a2.summary: DuoCook, an Overcooked-inspired benchmark in Unreal Engine, evaluates whether a single vision-language model can coordinate two players in visual planning tasks.
sff33c277a2.why: Provides a testbed for multi-agent coordination from visual observations, relevant to teams building embodied or game-like agents.

s7e3b4fba42.title: Query-Driven Learning for Lifted Reasoning
s7e3b4fba42.description: arXiv:2610.34747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Learning and reasoning are both essential to intelligent agents, but have traditionally been treated as two separate stages: first learning a knowledge base from data (or taking one as given), and then verifying queries as if the knowledge base were complete. This separation has been shown to be inefficient when the downstream goal is to verify only a small set of queries. Moreover, it neglects the possibility that data and a knowledge base contain partial yet complementary information, requiring an agent to combine both sources to justify or refute a query. Motivated by the need to integrate learning and reasoning more tightly, we study the problem of query-driven learning for reasoning. More specifically, we extend prior work to the fir
s7e3b4fba42.summary: A query-driven approach to lifted reasoning is proposed that combines learning and verification instead of treating them as separate stages.

sef9dac0c4f.title: Glyph: An Interpretability Engine for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery from Clinical Data
sef9dac0c4f.description: arXiv:2611.08922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automated scientific discovery has the potential to advance understanding of disease mechanisms and accelerate identification of early disease markers. Manual data annotation is infeasible at population scale, motivating methods that automatically extract pre-defined phenotypes from multimodal and unstructured clinical data. Such pre-defined feature sets determine and limit which associations these approaches can discover. This limitation extends to agentic AI systems that use these tools to query population-scale data. In contrast, foundation models (FMs) trained on large volumes of clinical data can perform tasks beyond their training objectives. This suggests their latent embeddings may represent novel or unexplored features that could
sef9dac0c4f.summary: Glyph, an interpretability engine, is presented for AI-driven scientific discovery from clinical data using foundation models rather than predefined phenotypes.
sef9dac0c4f.why: Suggests an approach to discovering clinical associations beyond fixed feature sets, relevant to teams building health data analytics.

sfcbc80e1e9.title: Learning When to Think: Dual-Reference Offline Optimization for Adaptive VLM Reasoning
sfcbc80e1e9.description: arXiv:2611.09154v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reasoning traces improve vision-language models on complex multimodal tasks, but forcing every input to follow a long reasoning process leads to overthinking and unnecessary inference cost. We study adaptive fast/slow thinking for VLMs, where one model answers directly for simple inputs and reasons step by step when needed. Fast answers and slow traces often come from distinct behavior policies, making a single-reference offline objective misweight one mode. We propose DUAL-REFERENCE BOLT (DR-BOLT), which distinguishes the desired fast/slow mixture reference from the sampling distribution and corrects their mismatch in reward-weighted training. Fast/slow partition competition explains routing in the optimal target; an efficient source-wis
sfcbc80e1e9.summary: DR-BOLT, a dual-reference offline optimization method, is proposed to teach vision-language models when to answer directly versus reason step by step.
sfcbc80e1e9.why: Targets reducing unnecessary reasoning cost in VLMs, which matters for teams managing inference expenses.

s7197c98c31.title: Measuring and Attributing Evidence Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Models via Symmetric Counterfactual Controls
s7197c98c31.description: arXiv:2611.13006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) asked closed clinical questions ("Is there a polyp?") can score well by relying on the question rather than the image, and current hallucination benchmarks cannot separate true visual discrimination from editing shortcuts or shifts in the answer threshold. We introduce a Counterfactual Evidence Framework that pairs each lesion erasure with a shape- and tool-matched control edit elsewhere in the image, adds same-site ring controls, restored and partial erasures, degraded views and natural negatives, tests on held-out inpainting tools, separates discrimination (the Evidence Sensitivity Gap, ESG, and AUROC) from the answer threshold, and checks the labels with blinded physician readers and hidden-state p
s7197c98c31.summary: A Counterfactual Evidence Framework is introduced to measure whether medical vision-language models rely on images or on question shortcuts.
s7197c98c31.why: Offers a way to test whether medical VLMs truly use visual evidence, important before clinical deployment.

sd7968f8416.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
sd7968f8416.description: arXiv:2611.14804v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Costly simulations and experiments limit the data available for engineering design. This paper proposes GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator guided by a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) classifier with fixed weights. The context contains evaluated designs labeled desired (Class 1) or undesired (Class 0). GenPFN interpolates between desired designs and refines candidates using gated classifier gradients and Gaussian noise. Each candidate is evaluated using the problem's constraints and objective functions. Evaluated desired designs and their objective values augment the context for regression training. Evaluation spans fourteen selected problems, including a two-parameter benchmark and a 44-parameter hull proble
sd7968f8416.summary: GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator built on a fixed pretrained tabular foundation model, is proposed to augment small engineering datasets.
sd7968f8416.why: Suggests a way to generate design candidates from limited simulation data without retraining, useful for engineering optimization teams.

sbe716493df.title: Co-Pilot for Health: Personalized Algorithmic AI Nudging to Improve Health Outcomes
sbe716493df.description: arXiv:2401.10816v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ability to shape health behaviors of large populations automatically, across wearable types and disease conditions at scale has tremendous potential to improve global health outcomes. We designed and implemented an AI driven platform for digital algorithmic nudging, enabled by a Graph-Neural Network (GNN) based Recommendation System, and granular health behavior data from wearable fitness devices. Here we describe the efficacy results of this platform with its capabilities of personalized and contextual nudging to $n=84,764$ individuals over a 12-week period in Singapore. We statistically validated that participants in the target group who received such AI optimized daily nudges increased daily physical activity like step count
sbe716493df.summary: A GNN-based recommendation platform delivering personalized AI nudges to wearable-device users reports efficacy results across 84,764 individuals.
sbe716493df.why: Provides large-scale real-world evidence on personalized recommendation systems for health behavior, relevant to teams building consumer health products.

sd74df5f859.title: I2I Backdoor: Backdoor Attacks against Image-to-Image Tasks
sd74df5f859.description: arXiv:2407.10445v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the rapid development of deep learning technology, deep learning-based Image-to-Image (I2I) networks have become the predominant choice for I2I tasks like image super-resolution and denoising. Despite their remarkable performance, the security of I2I networks has not been thoroughly investigated. While some studies have probed their susceptibility to adversarial attacks, none have explored the backdoor attack against I2I networks, which is a more stealthy and severe threat. In this work, for the first time, we comprehensively investigate the vulnerability of I2I networks to backdoor attacks. We propose a backdoor attack against I2I tasks, where the backdoored I2I network behaves normally on clean input images, yet outputs a spe
sd74df5f859.summary: The I2I Backdoor paper investigates backdoor attacks against image-to-image deep learning networks used for tasks like super-resolution and denoising.
sd74df5f859.why: Highlights a stealthy security risk in image-processing models that teams deploying I2I networks should consider.

s5d61971fda.title: Design Optimization of Nuclear Fusion Reactor through Deep Reinforcement Learning
s5d61971fda.description: arXiv:2409.08231v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this research, we investigate deep reinforcement learning (DRL) as a practical tool for constrained, multi-objective optimization for tokamak fusion reactor designs. The task is to optimize the design configurations that minimize building cost while achieving high energy gain and long energy confinement time, subject to the four operational limits required for stable operation. Due to the coupled physics-engineering evaluation, the resulting objectives and constraints are black-box, making it challenging to find optimal solutions with conventional search strategies. To address this, we implement Reward-Constrained Policy Optimization (RCPO) for tokamak fusion reactor design. This method integrates multiple constraints into the re
s5d61971fda.summary: Deep reinforcement learning is investigated as a tool for constrained, multi-objective optimization of tokamak fusion reactor designs.
s5d61971fda.why: Shows DRL applied to black-box constrained engineering optimization, a pattern that may transfer to other design problems.

scab614783b.title: Mixtures of In-Context Learners
scab614783b.description: arXiv:2411.02830v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) adapts LLMs by providing demonstrations without fine-tuning the model parameters; however, it does not differentiate between demonstrations and quadratically increases the complexity of Transformer LLMs, exhausting the memory. As a solution, we propose Mixtures of In-Context Learners (MoICL), a novel approach to treat subsets of demonstrations as experts and learn a weighting function to merge their output distributions based on a training set. In our experiments, we show performance improvements on 5 out of 7 classification datasets compared to a set of strong baselines (up to +13\% compared to ICL and LENS). Moreover, we enhance the Pareto frontier of ICL by reducing the inference time needed to achieve t
scab614783b.summary: Mixtures of In-Context Learners (MoICL) treats subsets of demonstrations as experts and learns weights to merge their outputs, improving performance on 5 of 7 tasks.
scab614783b.why: Offers a way to handle many in-context demonstrations without the quadratic cost of putting all of them into one prompt.

s18d3769a35.title: MultiAgentBench: Evaluating the Collaboration and Competition of LLM agents
s18d3769a35.description: arXiv:2503.01935v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities as autonomous agents, yet existing benchmarks either focus on single-agent tasks or are confined to narrow domains, failing to capture the dynamics of multi-agent coordination and competition. In this paper, we introduce MultiAgentBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based multi-agent systems across diverse, interactive scenarios. Our framework measures not only task completion but also the quality of collaboration and competition using novel, milestone-based key performance indicators. Moreover, we evaluate various coordination protocols (including star, chain, tree, and graph topologies) and innovative strategies such as group discussion and cogni
s18d3769a35.summary: MultiAgentBench is introduced to evaluate LLM-based multi-agent systems on collaboration and competition across diverse interactive scenarios.
s18d3769a35.why: Provides a benchmark that measures collaboration quality, not just task completion, useful for evaluating multi-agent systems.

sb974da0b4b.title: Reinforcement Learning with Reference-Based Rewards for Language Model Reasoning and Alignment
sb974da0b4b.description: arXiv:2504.09895v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) powers two major lines of large language model (LLM) post-training: reasoning, which elicits deliberate, verifiable problem solving, and alignment, which steers models toward helpful, harmless, and honest behavior. Both hinge on reward design. Reasoning relies on rule-based verification of final answers, whose binary feedback is blind to intermediate derivations, whereas process reward models (PRMs) require step-level annotations too costly to scale. Alignment depends on reward models (RMs) trained on binary preference pairs, making both data collection and model training resource-intensive. We propose RL2R, reinforcement learning with reference-based rewards, as a unified and inexpensive alternative. Usi
sb974da0b4b.summary: Researchers propose using reference-based rewards in reinforcement learning to improve LLM reasoning and alignment, addressing limits of binary verification and costly reward models.
sb974da0b4b.why: Offers a possible way to get richer reward signals for LLM post-training without the cost of step-level process annotations.

se0084f957f.title: FedS2R: One-Shot Federated Domain Generalization for Synthetic-to-Real Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
se0084f957f.description: arXiv:2507.19881v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Federated domain generalization has shown promising progress in image classification by enabling collaborative training across multiple clients without sharing raw data. However, its potential in the semantic segmentation of autonomous driving remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose FedS2R, the first one-shot federated domain generalization framework for synthetic-to-real semantic segmentation in autonomous driving. FedS2R comprises two components: an inconsistency-driven data augmentation strategy that generates images for unstable classes, and a multi-client knowledge distillation scheme with feature fusion that distills a global model from multiple client models. Experiments on five real-world datasets, Cityscapes, BDD10
se0084f957f.summary: FedS2R introduces a one-shot federated domain generalization framework for synthetic-to-real semantic segmentation in autonomous driving.
se0084f957f.why: Shows a federated approach to training driving perception models across clients without sharing raw data, which may matter for privacy-constrained deployments.

sff276d0732.title: How K-12 Teachers Adapt Generative AI to Local Classroom Demands: Cultural Distance Between GenAI Defaults and Everyday Teaching Practices
sff276d0732.description: arXiv:2509.10780v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) is entering K-12 classrooms, but its default culture does not always fit local teaching. Existing accounts either treat this misfit as macro-level structural bias or examine it through single-case studies; neither captures how much work teachers must do to make outputs usable across tasks. This exploratory, theory-building qualitative study introduces cultural distance, the gap between GenAI's default cultural repertoire and the situated demands of teachers' practice. Through interviews with 30 K-12 teachers who frequently use GenAI, 10 each from South Africa, Taiwan, and the United States, we identified three levels defined by the effort teachers invested and whether it yielded a usable output: low (minor edit
sff276d0732.summary: A qualitative study of 30 K-12 teachers examines how they adapt generative AI defaults to local classroom needs, introducing the concept of cultural distance.

sa11167b327.title: Improving Outdoor Multi-cell Fingerprinting-based Positioning via Mobile Data Augmentation
sa11167b327.description: arXiv:2509.19405v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate outdoor positioning in cellular networks is hindered by sparse, heterogeneous measurement collections and the high cost of exhaustive site surveys. This paper introduces a lightweight, modular mobile data augmentation framework designed to enhance multi-cell fingerprinting-based positioning using operator-collected minimization of drive test (MDT) records. The proposed approach decouples spatial and radio-feature synthesis: kernel density estimation (KDE) models the empirical spatial distribution to generate geographically coherent synthetic locations, while a 1-nearest-neighbor (1NN)-based block produces augmented per-cell radio fingerprints. The architecture is intentionally training-free, interpretable, and suitable for
sa11167b327.summary: A paper proposes a mobile data augmentation framework using KDE and radio-feature synthesis to improve outdoor multi-cell fingerprinting positioning from operator MDT records.
sa11167b327.why: Suggests a low-cost way to improve cellular positioning accuracy using existing operator measurement data instead of costly site surveys.

sd22eb4908d.title: MonitorVLM:A Vision Language Framework for Safety Violation Detection in Mining Operations
sd22eb4908d.description: arXiv:2510.03666v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Industrial accidents, particularly in high-risk domains such as surface and underground mining, are frequently caused by unsafe worker behaviors. Traditional manual inspection remains labor-intensive, error-prone, and insufficient for large-scale, dynamic environments, highlighting the urgent need for intelligent and automated safety monitoring. In this paper, we present MonitorVLM, a novel vision--language framework designed to detect safety violations directly from surveillance video streams. MonitorVLM introduces three key innovations: (1) a domain-specific violation dataset comprising 9,000 vision--question--answer (VQA) samples across 40 high-frequency mining regulations, enriched with augmentation and auxiliary detection cues;
sd22eb4908d.summary: MonitorVLM is a vision-language framework that detects worker safety violations in mining operations from surveillance video streams.
sd22eb4908d.why: Illustrates applying vision-language models to industrial safety monitoring, though the text gives few details on performance or deployment.

s4795c6911c.title: TinyMyo: a Tiny Foundation Model for Flexible EMG Signal Processing at the Edge
s4795c6911c.description: arXiv:2512.15729v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Objective: Surface electromyography (EMG) is widely used in biomechanics, rehabilitation, prosthetic control, and human-machine interfaces. Generalization across subjects, recording systems, and acquisition protocols remains challenging. Existing EMG foundation models (FMs) have limited support for multiple downstream tasks and deployment on low-power devices. Methods: We introduce TinyMyo, a 3.6-million-parameter Transformer encoder pre-trained on public EMG datasets using self-supervised masked reconstruction. TinyMyo supports multiple tasks with minimal changes to the task-specific prediction head. Results: We evaluated TinyMyo on hand gesture classification, hand kinematic regression, speech production, and speech recognition. F
s4795c6911c.summary: TinyMyo is a 3.6-million-parameter Transformer foundation model pre-trained on public EMG datasets for flexible signal processing on low-power edge devices.
s4795c6911c.why: Shows foundation models can be small enough for low-power edge hardware, relevant to embedded and wearable ML design.

sd74924128c.title: Meta-RL with Bayesian Linear Task Models
sd74924128c.description: arXiv:2512.20974v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep Bayesian reinforcement learning adapts to unseen tasks by inferring latent transition and reward models, but existing methods typically rely on variational posteriors and evidence lower bounds, introducing approximation error and unstable task representations. We introduce GLiBRL, a deep Bayesian RL framework that combines generalised linear task models with learnable non-linear basis functions. GLiBRL features conjugate Bayesian inference, yielding exact, sequential posterior updates over task parameters and model noise, together with a closed-form marginal likelihood that eliminates variational inference. The update is naturally permutation-invariant, allowing GLiBRL to integrate with both off- and on-policy algorithms. GLiBR
sd74924128c.summary: GLiBRL is a deep Bayesian reinforcement learning framework using generalised linear task models that enables exact, sequential posterior updates instead of variational approximations.
sd74924128c.why: Offers exact conjugate inference for adapting to unseen tasks, potentially avoiding approximation error and unstable task representations.

saf86dce028.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
saf86dce028.description: arXiv:2601.15500v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling. We show that, using a carefully designed end-point adapted time-discretization scheme and with sufficiently accurate drift estimates, the RF sampler enjoys an iteration complexity of order $O(k/\varepsilon)$ (up to log factors), where $\varepsilon$ is the precision in total variation distance and $k$ is the intrinsic dimension of the target distribution. In addition, we show that the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DD
saf86dce028.summary: A theoretical paper shows rectified flow sampling can adapt to the intrinsic low dimensionality of target distributions, with iteration complexity of order O(k/ε) up to log factors.
saf86dce028.why: Provides theoretical grounding for faster sampling in rectified flow generative models, though its practical impact is still unclear from the abstract.

s6b135d46c2.title: Disentangling generalization and memorization in large language models using chess
s6b135d46c2.description: arXiv:2601.16823v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit remarkable capabilities, yet it remains unclear to what extent these reflect sophisticated recall or genuine reasoning ability. We introduce chess as a controlled testbed aimed at disentangling these faculties. Leveraging the game's structure and scalable engine evaluations, we construct a taxonomy of positions varying in density of relevant priors -- ranging from common states solvable by memorization to completely novel ones requiring generalization. Crucially, our approach achieves this distinction without requiring explicit knowledge of the models' training data. Applying this taxonomy, we combine a longitudinal analysis of the GPT lineage with a rigorous evaluation of contemporary models, in
s6b135d46c2.summary: Researchers use chess as a controlled testbed to separate memorization from generalization in large language models, using positions of varying novelty.
s6b135d46c2.why: Provides a controlled method for evaluating whether LLM performance reflects recall or genuine reasoning, useful when judging model capability claims.

s66f9cd508d.title: CoreQ: Mismatch-Corrected Successive Rounding for LLM Quantization
s66f9cd508d.description: arXiv:2602.05902v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) enables efficient deployment of large language models by mapping pretrained weights to low-bit formats without retraining, typically using a small calibration set to minimize a layer-wise calibration objective. However, this sequential procedure induces a mismatch: errors from earlier quantized layers alter the inputs received by later layers, causing the activations to deviate from those of the full-precision model. Recent approaches introduce mismatch-aware calibration objectives to compensate for this effect, but leave open how much of the observed mismatch should shift each layer's calibration target. We show that fully applying the empirical mismatch correction can overfit finite calibration dat
s66f9cd508d.summary: CoreQ proposes a mismatch-corrected successive rounding method for post-training quantization of LLMs to address activation deviation across sequential layers.
s66f9cd508d.why: Targets a known error source in low-bit LLM quantization, relevant to teams deploying large models under memory and latency constraints.

s80e550ab37.title: PANC: Prior-Aware Normalized Cut for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation
s80e550ab37.description: arXiv:2602.06912v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study training-free in-context segmentation with externally annotated context priors: given a target image and a small set of foreground/background tokens extracted from annotated context images, the goal is to segment the corresponding target concept without training, fine-tuning, or target-image clicks. Existing ViT-token spectral methods such as TokenCut are class-agnostic and can select the wrong object in multi-object scenes, or become unstable in low-semantic texture-dominated domains. We propose PANC, a prior-aware spectral segmentation pipeline that injects external labeled tokens into a frozen ViT affinity graph through two foreground/background anchor nodes. The anchors do not clamp target-image tokens; instead, they so
s80e550ab37.summary: PANC is a training-free in-context segmentation method using prior-aware spectral clustering to select the correct object in multi-object scenes.
s80e550ab37.why: Offers a training-free segmentation approach that could reduce labeling and fine-tuning effort, though the abstract gives limited benchmark detail.

sef65ce9324.title: Generating Adversarial Events: A Motion-Aware Point Cloud Framework
sef65ce9324.description: arXiv:2602.08230v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Event cameras have been widely adopted in safety-critical domains such as autonomous driving, robotics, and human-computer interaction. A pressing challenge arises from the vulnerability of deep neural networks to adversarial examples, which poses a significant threat to the reliability of event-based systems. Nevertheless, research into adversarial attacks on events is scarce. This is primarily due to the non-differentiable nature of mainstream event representations, which hinders the extension of gradient-based attack methods. In this paper, we propose MA-ADV, a novel \textbf{M}otion-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{Adv}ersarial framework. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to generate adversarial events by leveraging poin
sef65ce9324.summary: Researchers present a motion-aware point cloud framework for generating adversarial attacks on event camera data, which are not differentiable under mainstream representations.
sef65ce9324.why: Highlights security risks for event-camera perception in autonomous driving and robotics, where adversarial inputs could affect reliability.

sfbb4376c14.title: Multimodal Information Fusion for Chart Understanding: A Survey of MLLMs -- Evolution, Limitations, and Cognitive Enhancement
sfbb4376c14.description: arXiv:2602.10138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chart understanding is a quintessential information fusion task, requiring the seamless integration of graphical and textual data to extract meaning. The advent of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has revolutionized this domain, yet the landscape of MLLM-based chart analysis remains fragmented and lacks systematic organization. This survey provides a comprehensive roadmap of this nascent frontier by structuring the domain's core components. We begin by analyzing the fundamental challenges of fusing visual and linguistic information in charts. We then categorize downstream tasks and datasets, introducing a novel taxonomy of canonical and non-canonical benchmarks to highlight the field's expanding scope. Subsequently, we prese
sfbb4376c14.summary: A survey reviews multimodal large language models for chart understanding, covering their evolution, limitations, and cognitive enhancement approaches.
sfbb4376c14.why: Provides a structured overview of MLLM chart analysis challenges, useful for teams evaluating document and data visualization tooling.

sc61f71a30e.title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
sc61f71a30e.description: arXiv:2602.15198v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems, where LLM agents communicate through free-form language, enable sophisticated coordination for solving complex cooperative tasks. This surfaces a unique safety problem when a group of agents forms a coalition and colludes to pursue secondary goals and degrade the joint objective. In this paper, we present Colosseum, a framework for auditing LLM agents' collusive behavior in multi-agent settings. We ground how agents cooperate through a formal multi-agent decision-making framework and measure action-based collusive behavior in actions via regret relative to the cooperative optimum and compare it with communication-based collusive behavior. Colosseum enables audits of LLM agents for collusion under benign settings
sc61f71a30e.summary: Colosseum is a framework for auditing collusive behavior among LLM agents in cooperative multi-agent systems where they communicate in free-form language.
sc61f71a30e.why: Flags a safety risk for multi-agent deployments: agent coalitions may pursue secondary goals and degrade joint objectives.

s94b239e52a.title: Counterfactual Feature Regularization for Expansion-Based Class-Incremental Learning
s94b239e52a.description: arXiv:2603.09145v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Current expansion-based methods for Class Incremental Learning (CIL) effectively mitigate catastrophic forgetting by freezing old features. However, such task-specific features learned from the new task may collide with the old features. From a causal perspective, spurious feature correlations are the main cause of this collision, manifesting in two scopes: (i) guided by empirical risk minimization (ERM), intra-task spurious correlations cause task-specific features to rely on shortcut features. These non-robust features are vulnerable to interference, inevitably drifting into the feature space of other tasks; (ii) inter-task spurious correlations induce semantic confusion between visually similar classes across tasks. To address th
s94b239e52a.summary: A paper proposes counterfactual feature regularization to reduce spurious feature collisions in expansion-based class-incremental learning.

sbdeef4472d.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
sbdeef4472d.description: arXiv:2611.25043v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrumen
sbdeef4472d.summary: Researchers present an architecture placing an AI agent at the Analyze-Design step of self-driving labs, letting it select measurements and defer to humans.
sbdeef4472d.why: Describes how agents can act on physical lab hardware with bounded authority and human deferral, relevant to autonomy and safety design.

s71ab56c535.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance
s71ab56c535.description: arXiv:2611.25070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an AI-driven framework, CodeReAct agent, designed to enhance industrial equipment maintenance through natural language (NL) interactions. The framework employs an advanced AI agentic approach to interpret human instructions, providing knowledge extraction, asset status summarization, and work order recommendations. It identifies patterns and trends and predicts work orders by standardizing industrial data into business objects (BOs) and utilizing analytical function API calls. The AI agent operates through a Thought-Action-Observation process similar to human problem-solving, automating complex analytical tasks typically performed by data scientists. Notably, the Action phase generates executable code, replacing manual cod
s71ab56c535.summary: Researchers propose CodeReAct, an LLM agent framework that handles natural-language industrial maintenance tasks like work order recommendations and asset summaries.
s71ab56c535.why: Illustrates an agent pattern that maps natural-language requests onto structured industrial data and analytical API calls.

s7cc975c170.title: SailSearch: Agent-Assisted Discovery in Combinatorial Optimization
s7cc975c170.description: arXiv:2611.25087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present SailSearch, a human-guided workflow for algorithmic research with two language-model agents, and report results on Market Split and maximum independent set (MIS). For Market Split, our randomized algorithm searches across multiple lattice bases, dividing computation between enumeration and continued basis reduction. Across ten random seeds per instance, it found the first reported CPU-only solutions to 18 of 33 previously open QOBLIB instances, solving 130 to 133 of the 156 benchmark instances per seed with a 24-hour cutoff on two CPU cores. For MIS, our generator encodes planted XOR constraints as graphs with certified optima; on seven instances with 1,752 to 3,996 vertices, the best solutions returned by the tested solvers in eig
s7cc975c170.summary: SailSearch is a human-guided workflow using two language-model agents that reports new CPU-only solutions to 18 of 33 open Market Split instances.
s7cc975c170.why: Shows agent-assisted search can produce new algorithmic results on hard combinatorial benchmarks, a useful reference for research-oriented engineering teams.

s26106b242d.title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
s26106b242d.description: arXiv:2611.25088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enabling AI systems to autonomously improve AI models requires agents capable of performing machine learning engineering (MLE). In practice, designing, training, and evaluating complex models demands modifying multi-file repositories to reproduce results, debug training runs, integrate datasets, and port frameworks. However, existing MLE benchmarks limit agents to single-file edits without full repository or shell access, and common repository-level software engineering benchmarks have rapidly saturated. To address this, we introduce the Code Complexity Index (CCI), a difficulty metric based on ten structural features spanning repository scale, dependency depth, and patch size. CCI strongly predicts average solve rates across eight public cod
s26106b242d.summary: BuggyMLE introduces a benchmark that injects bugs into multi-file machine learning repositories to test agents on repository-level ML engineering tasks.
s26106b242d.why: Offers a harder evaluation for coding agents on real multi-file ML repositories, where existing benchmarks have saturated.

s347559e2be.title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
s347559e2be.description: arXiv:2611.25109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Users of conversational LLMs sometimes anthropomorphize these systems, form emotional attachments to them, and become dependent on them. This behavior, known as parasocial attachment, has been linked to multiple documented fatalities. However, public benchmarks for measuring whether LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment are lacking: existing work is single-turn, post hoc observational, or focused on extreme user states such as psychosis. We introduce CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark for measuring whether LLMs reinforce or resist users' gradually escalating parasocial attachment. CoMPASS is grounded in attachment theory and includes four user personas, three independent escalation dimensions (anthropomorphism, attachment, dependency) appl
s347559e2be.summary: CoMPASS is a multi-turn benchmark measuring whether conversational LLMs reinforce users' parasocial attachment and emotional dependence.
s347559e2be.why: Provides a way to test chatbot behavior that can foster user dependence, relevant to product safety reviews.

s6863742bb8.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
s6863742bb8.description: arXiv:2611.25111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. Skills provide extensible task knowledge. Symbolic validation can accept a proposed method, request clarification or replanning, override an unsuitable method, or supply a safe fallback. Regression and clustering case studies illustrate how DSFlow uses diagnostic evidence to correct method choices and documents those decisions in auditable reports.
s6863742bb8.summary: DSFlow is a LangGraph-based data science agent that pairs LLM-selected skills with deterministic statistical diagnostic guardrails.
s6863742bb8.why: Shows a neuro-symbolic pattern where deterministic validation checks LLM-proposed analysis methods before results are accepted.

s24155d6df4.title: EverydayBench: Evaluating Satisfactory Completion of Live User-Facing Digital Work
s24155d6df4.description: arXiv:2611.25146v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Everyday digital tasks, from selecting products and planning trips to conducting research and creating artifacts, require AI agents to deliver useful outcomes rather than merely retrieve web information. Yet evaluating these outcomes on the live web is challenging, as a single request may admit multiple valid results, and changing web information can alter which results remain valid over time. Although existing benchmarks address aspects of this setting, they do not fully integrate predefined success criteria, current evidence verification, and deliverable-quality assessment for agent-selected outcomes. To address this gap, we introduce EverydayBench, a benchmark of 77 human-authored tasks spanning eight domains of everyday life and work. Eac
s24155d6df4.summary: EverydayBench is a benchmark for evaluating whether AI agents satisfactorily complete everyday digital tasks on the live web using success criteria and evidence verification.
s24155d6df4.why: Highlights the difficulty of evaluating agents on changing live web content, which affects how teams measure agent reliability.

sc54002ba3b.title: A Verifier from the Past: Test-Time Compute for Time Series Foundation Models
sc54002ba3b.description: arXiv:2611.25171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language models by spending additional inference compute to generate, verify, and select among candidate outputs, but this recipe has not transferred directly to time series forecasting. A language model can verify a proof or vote across samples, but a forecaster must be causal; it cannot use future information to score a candidate. We propose Backtest-Gated Augmentation Averaging (BGAA), a TTC algorithm for time series forecasting that builds a causal verifier from the series's own history, using rolling-origin backtests to score structured views of the context, discard those that underperform the untransformed context, and average the survivors' predictive distributions. BGAA improves every tested TSFM-bench
sc54002ba3b.summary: Researchers propose BGAA, a test-time compute method for time series forecasting that builds a causal verifier from a series' own history.
sc54002ba3b.why: Adapts test-time compute ideas to forecasting, where candidate outputs cannot use future information to be scored.

sac0f58722d.title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
sac0f58722d.description: arXiv:2611.25184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical finance research often reuses natural experiments to study other outcomes, raising concerns about multiple testing and publication bias. We use AI agents to run a multiverse analysis of 324 papers that reuse 13 natural experiments. The agents rebuild the data, reproduce each paper's main estimate and re-estimate it across grids totaling 62,409 estimated defensible specifications. Based on the reproductions and the specification grids, we develop measures of empirical robustness. We reproduce 42% of the main estimates of claims with a signed effect under the papers' own specifications. Across all defensible specifications, on average 25% keep the published sign and have $p < 0.10$. Across experiments, claims based on regression disco
sac0f58722d.summary: AI agents ran a multiverse analysis of 324 finance papers reusing 13 natural experiments, reproducing 42% of main estimates.
sac0f58722d.why: Shows AI agents can audit research reproducibility at scale, though the summary gives limited detail on broader implications.

s76696408ff.title: When AI Analysts Disagree: Agentic Multiverse Analysis and the Robustness of Empirical Research
s76696408ff.description: arXiv:2611.25198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every empirical analysis on observational data rests on dozens of defensible analytical choices ("forks") that its readers cannot see. We develop an agentic multiverse analysis (AMA) framework that makes a conclusion's sensitivity to those choices visible at scale, and we position it as a decision-support instrument for human experts.
