QVAC Genesis III is built via a dual generation strategy that performs targeted teacher distillation using a weak edge-scale student model as signal: the
s586cc7bf73.summary: QVAC Genesis III releases a 191.43B-token open synthetic STEM pretraining corpus covering 19 domains, aimed at small models for edge and on-device deployment.
s586cc7bf73.why: An open, large STEM synthetic corpus gives teams training small on-device models a reusable pretraining dataset.

s752842484d.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory for Graphic Design Agent
s752842484d.description: arXiv:2609.22086v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deployed software agents face a continuous stream of user requests while their foundation-model weights remain frozen between releases. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) via external memory offers a practical path to continual adaptation, yet prior methods largely assume programmatic verifiers, cheap retries, or a single global prompt. Creative software breaks these assumptions, as open-ended visual briefs lack ground truth, VLM judges are noisy, and multi-step tool executions are costly and confounded by external assets. We present Designer-RSI, which evolves a modular SKILL.md skill bank from unlabeled design trajectories for an agent spanning over 230 raster, vector, and layout tools. Designer-RSI couples widening (acquiring new skills
s752842484d.summary: Designer-RSI proposes evolving procedural memory so a graphic design agent can keep adapting to user requests without weight updates between model releases.
s752842484d.why: External memory for continual adaptation in creative agents without verifiers is relevant to teams building deployed agents with frozen foundation models.

s3c0948c47a.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
s3c0948c47a.description: arXiv:2609.24974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimi
s3c0948c47a.summary: arXiv:2609.24974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the…

seb683e9bfb.title: Evaluating Real-Time Voice Agents: A Survey from Component Quality to Grounded Outcomes
seb683e9bfb.description: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it. But currently their evaluation is fragmented and is split across speech quality, turn-taking, tool calling, and task completion. We review 136 primary works published up to October 2, 2026, and code each on two axes: the capability an evaluation exercises, namely timing, recovery, grounded outcome, and, where relevant, multiparty conduct; and the strength of its evidence, namely evaluation conditions and grading instrument. The coding locates the gaps. Only 13 of 91 evaluation works check external state or action traces, only 5 of 21 grounded-outcome benchmarks use real human speech, and only 2 of 26 multiparty benchm
seb683e9bfb.summary: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it.

s3996265c85.title: DeepEdu-F: A Framework for Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs in Vietnamese Education
s3996265c85.description: arXiv:2609.31568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cloud AI assistants send student data to foreign servers, conflicting with data-sovereignty laws such as Vietnam's Decree 53, and are not grounded in the national curriculum, so they often hallucinate on local content. Self-hosting an open model keeps data on-premise but faces two costs that weight quantization does not remove. sad161db0ab.title: One Latent, Many Tokens: Jointly Learning Compressed Embeddings for Efficient Language Diffusion
sad161db0ab.description: arXiv:2609.33698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Most continuous diffusion language models process one latent position per token at each sampling step, making generation expensive. Two-stage methods lower the cost by reducing the latent length, but they fix the compressed embedding space before training the diffusion model. Embeddings from the fixed space can be difficult to model with diffusion and decode reliably into tokens, which limits generation quality after compression. To address this problem, we introduce JPEG-DLM (Joint-embedding Prediction for Efficient Generation with Diffusion Language Model), which jointly trains a compressor, a flow matching model and a decoding module. s0bdc78165f.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
s0bdc78165f.description: arXiv:2609.34654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate fitness prediction is central to protein engineering and understanding sequence-function relationships. With advances in deep learning, protein foundation models (PFMs) have become widely used for this task. Recent analyses, however, show that these models share preferences reflecting their training corpora, while unreliable inputs can further distort fitness predictions. Family-specific evolutionary evidence and structural context can help address these limitations by providing complementary constraints on model scores, motivating VenusREM-Harness (VRH), a general, model-agnostic, training-free Retrieval-Enhanced Mutation harness. sfa44a54df7.title: UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval
sfa44a54df7.description: arXiv:2609.36805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents draw on external memory to guide new tasks, raising the question of which memories to retrieve together to improve execution. Learning set values requires outcome feedback, but evaluating each untested alternative costs an additional rollout. We introduce \textsc{UpliftMem}, which learns set-level execution uplift relative to the same executor without memory. Our analysis of how retrieval preferences limit feedback coverage motivates targeted probes. s7ab9d3eb51.title: Can Computation from Earlier Problems Help LLMs Solve New Ones?
s7ab9d3eb51.description: arXiv:2609.39394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often solve independent problems in the same conversation. Can computation from earlier problems help them solve new ones? Preliminary experiments show that retained history can raise or lower later-turn accuracy, even within the same domain. To trace this effect, we hold each problem fixed and vary its preceding history. The resulting changes in the model's internal states contain a recurring, problem-dependent component. s7ab9d3eb51.summary: arXiv:2609.39394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often solve independent problems in the same conversation.

s1050b0161f.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
s1050b0161f.description: arXiv:2610.11723v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world. We introduce MultiWorldBench, a diagnostic Minecraft benchmark comprising 495 case configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities, including independent control, cross-view motion, shared-state synchronization, persistence, structural reasoning, concurrent interaction, and delayed revisit. Using Engine GT as a reference, we evaluate two multiplayer world models, Solaris (MP) and Gamma-World, together with a single-player generation variant, Solaris (SP). s1050b0161f.summary: arXiv:2610.11723v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world.

s9d70fd7172.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models
s9d70fd7172.description: arXiv:2610.17205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based decision-making systems, also called System One models, have recently gained popularity, most notably through Jev (Almeida, 2026). Given a typed input state, a question, and a set of options, they return a calibrated probability for each option in a single forward pass, without text generation. We show that open instruction-tuned LLMs can achieve performance comparable to Jev without any additional training, by reading out answers from letters (A, B, C, etc.) in the model's output logits at the last token position. Next, we propose a simple supervised LoRA fine-tuning recipe that can improve their performance further. s3b8497069e.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
s3b8497069e.description: arXiv:2610.18088v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Autoresearch systems increasingly undertake entire research projects. In practice, scientific research requires systems to pursue multiple interdependent claims through a continuous, multi-stage workflow and revise experiments as evidence accumulates. Existing evaluations of autoresearch systems, however, typically score isolated tasks or final artifacts, leaving these process-level capabilities largely unmeasured. sd3dc13f325.title: What the Trace Shows and What the Label Says: Auditing Behavioral Detectors in Agent Evaluation
sd3dc13f325.description: arXiv:2610.30491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM agents are often evaluated by reducing execution traces to labels such as final-answer correctness, tool verification, and fault propagation. These labels are measurements produced by parsers, behavioral detectors, and harness rules, yet evaluations rarely report whether a measurement actually fits the trace it describes. We study what happens when those measurements do not fully capture the trace's behavior. Agents solve GSM8K problems with a calculator whose outputs are occasionally corrupted, which gives ground truth for what the tool returned, what the model later used, and what the detectors reported; a chemistry task with search and retrieval tests the case where the model cannot recompute the tool's output. s00fd8362fc.title: Noise Steering: Exploiting Wake Steering and Acoustic Directivity for Noise-Constrained Wind Farm Control via Reinforcement Learning
s00fd8362fc.description: arXiv:2610.36888v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing noise mitigation strategies for wind farms usually consist in reducing turbines power output, without accounting for the wake interactions between them and the noise emission directivity. This leads to over-conservative policies and unexploited wind power. Yet, turbine yaw can simultaneously affect wake interactions and the direction of noise emission, offering an additional degree of freedom for farm-level noise control. s11ef88e9fe.title: Kairos: A Unified PDDL Planner for Robots: Plans in Milliseconds, with a Guarantee for Every Answer
s11ef88e9fe.description: arXiv:2610.39454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means. Models are written in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), which has grown from classical planning to durative actions, numeric resources, time windows and continuous change, while planners cover one fragment each and differ in what their failures mean. The contribution in artificial intelligence is Kairos, a single planner, not a portfolio of existing planners, that covers the whole language and derives what each answer guarantees from the search that produced it. s11ef88e9fe.summary: arXiv:2610.39454v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means.

s9d4239e43b.title: The Real Cost of Context: Predicting Compute Time and Energy Consumption in LLM Prefill and Decode Phases
s9d4239e43b.description: arXiv:2610.39621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into agentic architectures has substantially increased token consumption, raising concerns about their energy footprint. s760a620198.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
s760a620198.description: arXiv:2611.14183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Temporal-difference critics regress onto a bootstrapped target and usually need a target network. s192b15e64d.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
s192b15e64d.description: arXiv:2611.15592v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In September 2026, TypeSafe announced Jev as the first model in its System One category: unstructured state goes in, and typed, calibrated decisions that software can use directly come out. Jev's architecture and training data are unpublished, but many open typed-decision models have followed. They answer structured questions about a piece of text, such as a yes/no check, a choice among labelled options or a graded score, by reading the text with a language model and scoring the options with a small readout. s192b15e64d.summary: A controlled study compares typed-decision models, which answer structured questions about text using a language model and a small readout head.
s192b15e64d.why: Gives engineers a comparison of readout designs for yes/no, multiple-choice, and graded-score tasks built on LLM text understanding.

s3d4ca1bc2c.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
s3d4ca1bc2c.description: arXiv:2611.17309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. However, these models can be unstable, slow to train, and use many parameters and FLOPs to solve simple puzzles. Descent on an energy not only mitigates these issues but also offers advantages: built-in early stopping, compute that adapts to problem difficulty, fast training without differentiating through a solver, and interpretable weights that learn the constraints of the puzzle. s3d4ca1bc2c.summary: Researchers report that energy-based descent solves reasoning puzzles like Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique far faster than looped models, claiming up to 1,000x speedup.
s3d4ca1bc2c.why: Suggests a cheaper, more stable alternative to looped models for puzzle-style reasoning, with built-in early stopping and fast training.

sb4f35c6f49.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
sb4f35c6f49.description: arXiv:2611.18714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI syste
sb4f35c6f49.summary: A paper proposes a descriptive research program for AI moral agency, drawing on sentimentalist and rationalist moral psychology to identify underlying human capabilities.

s779ccf5408.description: Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are "undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy," Signal president […]
s779ccf5408.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots on Android and iOS to stop built-in AI features like Gemini and Siri from reading users' on-screen messages and data.
s779ccf5408.why: Shows OS-level AI assistants can conflict with app privacy guarantees, so teams building messaging or sensitive apps should weigh how platform agents access screen content.
